news.Title: Google's next TV gadget may do much more than stream
news.Content:
It's possible that Google's next streaming device could detect when you enter a room and let you communicate with it without using the remote.

Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google is developing a new generation of its Google TV Streamer with built-in microphones, presence sensing, a faster processor and additional storage, according to 9to5Google , citing a source familiar with the company's plans.

The microphones would allow users to issue "Hey Google" commands directly to the streaming device rather than first picking up its remote.

When no one is actively viewing the television, presence detection might give it a new purpose. Similar technology can automatically show pictures, the time, the weather, and other ambient data when someone enters a room.

Google has not disclosed the gadget, its cost, or the anticipated debut date.

However, the claimed additions suggest that this is more than just a standard CPU update.

Google TV viewers can already ask conversational questions, find entertainment, and receive assistance with topics unrelated to television using Gemini.

Google's next streamer may resemble an AI-powered smart-home hub that just so happens to be located underneath the TV if it has microphones and the capacity to identify people in the vicinity.

Google's TV Streamer could stop depending on the remote

As Chromecast's replacement, the current Google TV Streamer debuted in 2024.

It was already a significant change.

The $99.99 gadget was designed to sit prominently next to the TV and serve as a smart-home hub with Matter connectivity and a Thread border router, rather than hiding behind it like Chromecast.

Google TV users can control compatible lights, thermostats, and cameras and see video doorbell notifications without pausing their show.

Google's purported successor appears to extend that approach.

Microphones that could receive "Hey Google" requests from across the room would be housed in apertures on the gadget itself, according to 9to5Google .

Additionally, the business apparently plans to add proximity detection, a faster CPU, and more storage than the 32 gigabytes that the present Streamer has.

The remote is expected to retain a similar design but gain two additional shortcut buttons alongside dedicated YouTube and Netflix controls.

Those aren't equally important upgrades.

Apps should load more smoothly with additional storage and processing capability.

Presence sensors and microphones can completely alter how users engage with the device.

Related: Google's AI chip could become a $75 billion business

Story Continues

To communicate with Gemini on the current Streamer, users must push the microphone button on the remote.

Gemini could be reached from across the room without first locating anything thanks to the microphones included within the box.

Because of this, Google's television plan resembles its smart-speaker strategy more and more, with the exception that the AI now has the largest screen in the house.

Gemini is already turning Google TV into more than television

In November 2025, Google began distributing Gemini to the Google TV Streamer.

Gemini can handle conversational requests rather than just simple instructions.

When a couple is looking for something to watch, they may explain their two different preferences and ask Gemini to recommend a film that suits both of them. Someone who doesn't remember how the previous season of a program ended might ask for a recap.

The assistant may also answer inquiries unrelated to entertainment.

Google says Gemini on TV can explain school topics, help with recipes, and walk users through DIY projects using TV videos.

Google has increased such capacities even further in 2026.

Gemini may provide more detailed visual responses, sports-related information, and in-depth voiced analyses of challenging topics.

Additionally, Google TV can create pictures and videos straight on the TV, search users' Google photographs libraries, and convert photographs into slideshows.

This feature increases the significance of the reported microphones.

The TV is now Gemini's home, but the remote is still the main means to access it.

Far-field microphones may eliminate that barrier.

Another layer is added by presence detection.

Instead of waiting for someone to pick up a remote, the TV may respond when they walk into the room.

TCL has already used presence sensing on a Google TV to activate its Google Photos screensaver and show information such as weather and the time when someone approaches, according to 9to5Google .

Put those pieces together and Google's long-term opportunity becomes clearer.

Gemini, Google Photos, entertainment, and connected-home controls all appear on the TV, which increasingly reacts to its surroundings.

Google's smarter TV gadget could come with a price problem

There is one clear issue.

Google has already significantly increased the price of its existing streaming gadget.

The Google TV Streamer originally launched for $99.99 in September 2024.

Google raised the U.S. price by $50 to $149.99 on Aug. 31, citing rising component costs.

According to 9to5Google, that represented a 50% price increase for a device that had previously been discounted during holiday sales.

The current 4K Streamer, which has 32GB of storage and 4GB of RAM, is still listed on Google's store for $149.99.

For whatever happens next, it presents an intriguing challenge.

The next model would be more capable with a quicker CPU, greater storage, microphones, and presence detection.

However, they could also make it more difficult to market Google's streamer as a low-cost replacement for an outdated TV.

Walmart's Onn 4K Pro, for example, was selling for around $60 in September while offering Google TV and many of the basic capabilities users expect from a modern streaming box.

Google, therefore, needs the next Streamer to justify something more than streaming.

This might be the reason why the purported improvements focus more on AI and smart homes than just video quality.

More Google:

Google is making a change in November that might catch Gemini users off guard

Google set to challenge Meta Muse in the Agentic AI race

Google just disclosed something troubling about its AI

There are many less expensive alternatives to watch Netflix, YouTube, and Disney+ on a television than a $149 streaming box.

A room-aware Gemini gadget that manages the home, responds to inquiries, locates pictures, and simultaneously streams Netflix is a different story.

The significance of Google's next hardware update may depend on this difference.

For years, the business has been putting Gemini on watches, phones, vehicles, and TVs.

The next phase might be more subtle thanks to built-in microphones and proximity tracking; users would not even need to intentionally reach for Gemini.

They may just enter the living room and strike up a conversation.

Related: Google's $180 Fitbit Edge makes a bet on smartwatch fatigue

news.Title: Not Nvidia. Not Microsoft. This "Magnificent Seven" Stock Is the Cheapest Right Now.
news.Content:
As the old adage goes, you get what you pay for. In other words, if you want quality, you can expect to pay a premium for it. The idea applies within the world of investing as well.

Still, knowing that stocks' prices and valuations constantly ebb and flow -- sometimes to extremes -- it's not wrong to think about the price you're paying to plug into a particular company's performance.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

This premise presents a potential opportunity to investors interested in the market's biggest and highest-profile names. Although they're all so-called " Magnificent Seven " stocks, one of these names is measurably cheaper than all the others right now. While not a reason in and of itself to step in, this valuation bolsters the existing bullish case.

This Mag-7 bargain? Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), priced at just over 16 times this year's analyst-projected per-share earnings of $20.59.

The numbers

If you've been keeping tabs on Google's parent company and its recent quarter, you already know something important. Its earnings projection includes a $6.26-per-share second-quarter accounting benefit linked to the growth of the company's investments in SpaceX and Anthropic. Without that one-time bump, Alphabet's only on track to earn $14.33 per share this year, translating into a price-to-earnings ratio of a little more than 23.

That's not exactly cheap, but it's not outrageous either. It's less than Nvidia 's 2026 comparison of 24, as well as Microsoft 's P/E ratio of 27 based on this year's expected earnings of $19.76 per share. Indeed, the only Magnificent Seven name that's even sort of close is Amazon . However, like Alphabet, it too reported a big gain from its stake in Anthropic during Q2 of this year. Indeed, $53.4 billion of its Q2 $62.6 billion in net income came from its Anthropic holding. Strip that out, and Amazon stock is valued at roughly 27 times 2026's anticipated profit.

There's more than one way to value a stock, of course. Arguably the more meaningful way is based on that company's future earnings. That's where things start changing a bit here.

Although GOOGL shares are only slightly more expensive on a forward-looking basis than Facebook parent Meta's stock price of around 21, Nvidia is technically trouncing both by this measure at only 14 times its expected 2027 earnings of $15.80 per share. It's an outlook that requires a near-doubling of this year's likely profits, on year-over-year revenue growth of nearly 70%. Nvidia might be able to do it, but there's no room for error. Even the slightest balk in overall capital spending on AI hardware could pull the rug out from underneath this name.

In other words, don't be too trusting of what superficially looks like a bargain price. Most investors aren't, in fact. That's why NVDA shares are valued so cheaply compared to next year's predicted profits.

In the right business(es) in the right way at the right time

Those are the comparative numbers, and they matter. Just don't become so valuation-focused that you lose sight of the fact that numbers aren't everything. As an investor, you're also buying into parts of a business that you can't quantify.

That's the crux of the reason to consider stepping into a stake in Alphabet over any other Mag-7 name right now, regardless of any of their valuations. It's arguably better positioned than any of these other companies to stand up to whatever headwinds might soon start blowing.

Its revenue mix has a great deal to do with this resiliency. While Google Cloud's Q2 revenue soared 82% to triple this arm's operating income, the company's breadwinning business remains search-based advertising, which is a reliable cash cow regardless of the economy's condition. For perspective, Google and its related profit centers still contribute more than four times what cloud computing does to Alphabet's bottom line.

To the extent that AI is a key driver of future growth, Alphabet's got a competitive edge. That's the fact that it's in a better position to sell artificial intelligence as a recurring service than most of its top rivals are.

Most of the major names in the business offer such options one way or another. However, with processors, data centers, and software -- the full "stack" -- plus existing relationships with business customers, Google is more likely to remain a provider even if competitors lose customers in a slowdown of the AI industry's current growth.

Google Cloud's total backlog of future revenue that's been contracted but not yet consumed or booked now stands at $514 billion. That's 20 times last quarter's top line for this arm alone, none of which will necessarily require the outright sale of computing hardware.

A compelling buy at this valuation, no matter what it is

Perhaps the big takeaway here is simply understanding that while Alphabet is often categorized as a technology company, that's not quite what it is. It's a service company. It's always served consumers, and now it serves a sizable slice of the technology industry too. That may also be why -- like most recurring-service stocks -- its ticker is usually priced and valued more like a service name, and that's OK.

There's never a bad time to own this consistent performer, but it's particularly attractive when you can get in at something of a discount, like you can right now.

news.Title: 'The world's super company': Wall Street weighs SpaceX earnings, company's likely Tesla tie-up
news.Content:
Elon Musk's vision for SpaceX ( SPCX ) has Wall Street sizing up a potential giant unlike anything it's seen before. Mix in a possible tie-up with Musk's EV giant Tesla ( TSLA ), and investors could be looking at a monster play.

Wall Street strategists are already looking at SpaceX and Tesla as one.

Musk, who is CEO of both companies, projects SpaceX's annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 to fall "somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion." Its booming AI compute business is fueling bets that SpaceX could emerge as a fifth hyperscaler alongside Meta ( META ), Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Amazon ( AMZN ).

"Couple that with the fact that they have a satellite business that's growing, they have a lucrative space business that the AI profits can continue to underwrite, and now we have a possible merger with Tesla," Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman told Yahoo Finance after the space company posted better-than-expected quarterly results.

"This doesn't only become the fifth hyperscaler, this becomes the world's super company," he added.

A deal with Tesla would bring SpaceX into the EV maker's plans to roll out Optimus robots, its Cybercab business, and ultimately Terafab, Musk's ambitious plan to manufacture chips and reduce production costs by up to 90%.

"This is their way of bypassing Nvidia and bypassing TSMC," RBC Capital Markets lead equity analyst Tom Narayan told Yahoo Finance. "If they can do that, it's huge."

Those chips would power everything from data centers to hundreds of thousands of humanoid robots. Tesla plans to produce 20,000 Optimus per week by the end of 2027.

Canaccord Genuity Capital Markets analyst George Gianarikas raised his price target on Tesla to $442.00 from $410 following the EV maker's quarterly results, with the call based fundamentally on a merger.

"If they merge, you are buying the future of the physical world," wrote Gianarikas on Thursday. "A company that is attempting to make, not just program, Tomorrowland. You are buying the Berkshire Hathaway of tomorrow's physical technology."

Meanwhile, JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth more than doubled his price target on SpaceX to $500 after the company posted better-than-expected quarterly results last week. On Friday, shares were trading at $146.

SpaceX has grown well beyond rockets and satellites with plans to become a leading mobile carrier and build out data centers in space.

"SpaceX's ambitions are bigger than any company's we've seen — to make life multi-planetary, leverage the Sun to build out AI in space, & build bases on the Moon and cities on other planets, " wrote Anmuth.

Story Continues

"No other company is as well-positioned to go after the combined anticipated [total addressable market] of $28T+," he added.

With committees at both companies and Musk pushing for a deal, Wall Street is increasingly betting on the biggest merger in history.

"We believe there is an 80% to 90% chance that Tesla and SpaceX merge by the end of 2027 for a number of strategic AI and data-driven reasons and this is the right move for Musk," wrote Yorkville Ives' Dan Ives.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

news.Title: Intel vs. SK Hynix: Revenue Trends to Help Investors Weigh Which Artificial Intelligence Stock to Buy
news.Content:
Intel: Maintaining Steady Revenue Levels

Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) primarily generates its revenue by designing, developing, and manufacturing various computing processors, discrete graphics units, edge computing solutions, and connectivity components tailored specifically for global original equipment manufacturers, cloud service providers, and other enterprise network builders.

During the late summer months, it priced an upsized $20 billion public offering of common stock. In October, it entered a technical collaboration with Applied Materials to develop next-generation transistor packaging technologies.

SK Hynix: Rapid Revenue Expansion

SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) primarily generates its revenue by designing, manufacturing, and selling a wide variety of advanced memory semiconductors, including specialized dynamic random-access memory (RAM) and flash products with various performance characteristics customized to meet complex customer computing requirements.

It recently signed a preliminary memorandum to receive federal government grants. In August, the company officially broke ground on an advanced semiconductor packaging facility in Indiana, while its publicly traded shares experienced a notable price decline during the middle of October.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue represents the total gross sum of money a business successfully brings in from its primary commercial operations before any associated operating expenses, employee salaries, material costs, debt interest payments, or taxes are deducted to determine final profitability. This metric helps investors measure a company's overall size, market footprint, and long-term trajectory.

Foolish Take

A look at Intel and SK Hynix's sales over the past two years is eye-opening. In 2024, the Korean memory giant's revenue was less than Intel's. Not only did SK Hynix grow past the semiconductor titan in 2025, it has blown Intel's sales out of the water in 2026.

This demonstrates the massive demand for the advanced memory components sold by SK Hynix, giving the company pricing power and enabling it to achieve historic profitability thresholds across all major margin metrics during the second quarter of 2026. For example, it hit a 76% operating margin in Q2, up substantially from 41% in the prior year. The big unknown is how long the demand will last and whether SK Hynix's expansion of its manufacturing facilities will lead to lower margins as prices stabilize.

Intel is in the midst of a turnaround. Amid the artificial intelligence boom, the semiconductor veteran should be seeing strong sales growth. Yet it struggled to do so, and in Q4 of 2025, its revenue declined year over year.

The situation appears to be reversing in 2026. CEO Lip-Bu Tan took over in 2025, and he implemented changes that helped Intel achieve its highest quarterly sales total in the last two years in Q2 of this year. From here, the expectation is that Intel's revenue will continue to climb under Tan's leadership, which investors should keep an eye on to confirm that happens.

news.Title: 別只押台積電！它從晶片一路吃到AI散熱　規模較去年成長118%
news.Content:
全球AI競賽從晶片算力延伸至電力、散熱及資料中心建置，台灣企業在供應鏈的關鍵角色更加鮮明，國泰台灣領袖50（00922）聚焦50檔領袖級台股企業，持股涵蓋台積電、聯發科、台達電、鴻海及日月光投控，串聯晶片設計、先進製程、封裝測試到伺服器與電源散熱。這項跨環節配置特色，促使00922基金規模比2025年底成長118.02%、增逾一倍的重要觀察亮點。

00922基金經理人蘇鼎宇進一步分析，00922成分股各自掌握這波AI建設需求的重要環節，台積電以先進製程與封裝支援高效能運算，聯發科拓展邊緣AI及終端應用；鴻海透過AI伺服器製造與系統整合參與硬體建置，台達電回應資料中心的電源與散熱需求，日月光投控則提供封裝測試服務。

從晶片生產到整機交付，這些能力不僅共同支撐AI系統運作，更使得00922能透過不同企業參與產業升級，從每個環節掌握產業發展脈動，機構法人普遍看好台股今明兩年獲利表現， 成分股與大盤貼近的00922，亦成為熱門投資標的。除了科技供應鏈，00922同時涵蓋富邦金、中信金等金融企業，擴大參與台灣大型企業的發展。國內13家金控今年前8月獲利創新高，合計稅後獲利達5,789.07億元，刷下歷年同期新高紀錄，也讓金融產業的營運表現成為台股另一項觀察重點。科技與金融的兩大支柱，可望為00922再添助攻動能。

00922追蹤MSCI台灣領袖50精選指數，以市值代表性為基礎，精選流動性佳、獲利穩定的50檔企業，基金結合AI相關企業與金融等跨產業配置，投資人可依自身財務狀況、投資目標與風險承受度，將00922納入台股資產配置的考量，亦可透過定期定額分批投入，以長期投資紀律參與台灣領袖企業的發展。

news.Title: Cathie Wood buys $24.5 million of tumbling megacap stock
news.Content:
Cathie Wood, chief of Ark Investment Management, often buys her favorite tech stocks when their prices fall.

That's what she's doing with Meta Platforms (META), adding shares after the Facebook parent's stock tumbled following its earnings report.

Last year, the flagship Ark Innovation ETF gained 35.49%, far outpacing the S&P 500's return of 17.88% in the same period. So far this year, Wood's flagship Ark Innovation ETF (ARKK) is up 6.59% as of Oct. 23, while the S&P 500 surged 11.37 %.

Wood gained a reputation after the Ark Innovation ETF delivered a rosy 153% return in 2020. But her style also brings painful losses in bearish markets, as seen in 2022, when the ETF tumbled more than 60%.

Those swings have weighed on Wood's long-term gains. As of Oct. 23, her Ark Innovation ETF has delivered a five-year annualized return of -6.83% , while the S&P 500 has an annualized return of 10.9% over the same period, according to data from Morningstar .

Cathie Wood remains optimistic about AI and tech revolution

Wood focuses on high-tech companies across artificial intelligence, blockchain, biomedical technology, and robotics. She believes these businesses have strong growth potential, but their volatility often causes fluctuations in the Ark's funds.

Over the decade ended 2025, the Ark Innovation ETF wiped out nearly $5 billion in investor wealth, according to a report by Morningstar's analyst Amy Arnott . That made it the fourth-biggest wealth destroyer among mutual funds and ETFs in the ranking.

Wood defended her investment strategy after an audience member at a recent summit questioned ARK's performance compared with the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ).

Related: Cathie Wood sells $16 million of surging tech stock

"Investors deserve to understand both their returns and the decisions behind them," Wood said in an Oct. 5 post on X .

She argued that the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) and QQQ are built differently. QQQ tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index, while ARK actively invests in companies it believes are driving disruptive innovation across industries, including healthcare, financial services, and transportation.

Wood has long been optimistic about AI, which she sees as a major driver of productivity, economic growth, and corporate profits in the years ahead. She has also pushed back against recent fears that AI could pose an existential threat to humanity.

In September, Wood reposted a post by David Sacks on X, saying he makes a good case that the "AI will kill humanity" headlines were orchestrated.

Story Continues

Meanwhile, she acknowledged that AI, like other technologies, can be used for harmful purposes. She said people such as Elon Musk who highlight AI's potential risks are "doing us a great service," adding that "half of the solution — including AI — is understanding the problem."

In August, Wood said U.S. corporate profits remain unusually strong, with domestic profits before tax at 13.2% of GDP, a level she said is near multi-decade highs.

Some of that strength came from the massive monetary and fiscal stimulus during the pandemic, but Wood believes another factor is helping sustain margins today: Companies are leaning into AI and productivity gains to protect them.

"I think we're still early in seeing how far that can go," she said, adding that companies that use AI effectively will "separate themselves from the ones that don't."

Not all investors agree with Wood's optimism. Over the past 12 months through Oct. 22, the Ark Innovation ETF saw roughly $1.73 billion in net outflows, according to data from ETF research firm VettaFi .

Cathie Wood buys $24.5 million of Meta stock

On Oct. 22, Wood's Ark funds bought a total of 38,110 shares of Meta Platforms (META), according to Ark's daily trading information sent to TheStreet. These shares were worth about $24.5 million based on the latest trading price of $642.62.

Wood's purchase came as Meta shares tumbled despite strong earnings.

The social media giant reported third-quarter earnings on Oct. 21, beating Wall Street's revenue expectations. But shares plunged 7% the following day and fell another 1% on Oct. 23, as investors grew concerned about the social media giant's aggressive spending on artificial intelligence.

Related: Cathie Wood buys $11.8 million of tumbling tech stock

Meta posted third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, beating analysts' expectations of $63.41 billion. Earnings came in at $3.83 per share, below the consensus estimate of $5.46, largely due to a $9.89 billion charge related to a settlement over teen mental health. Excluding that, Meta said earnings would have reached $7.40 per share.

The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, compared with Wall Street's estimate of $73.75 billion.

Meta also raised the lower end of its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to $135 billion to $145 billion, up from $130 billion to $145 billion. It also increased its full-year expense outlook to $175 billion to $179 billion.

"Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization," the company said in a statement .

Meta is pushing deeper into AI agents. In September, it launched Muse, a personal AI agent that can take actions on users' behalf and help with daily tasks such as sending emails. The app has become one of the most popular personal AI agents since its debut.

Citi analyst Ronald Josey raised his price target on Meta stock to $905 from $895 and maintained a Buy rating, citing Muse's potential, according to a research note sent to TheStreet.

"We are incrementally positive on shares of Meta following 3Q26 results as we believe Meta is entering into an AI product super-cycle with multiple monetization tailwinds," Josey wrote. "Meta's growing compute capacity gives it the ability to launch multiple new products and services and press its first-mover advantage across Personal Agents."

Josey pointed to strong early adoption of Muse, with 10 million users signing up and 25% returning daily. Shopping is the most common use case, which Citi believes could open up revenue opportunities through subscriptions, transaction fees, and enterprise services.

The analyst also noted that time spent on Instagram and Facebook Reels reached all-time highs, helped by AI-powered content recommendations.

"While 2027 remains an investment year (particularly as Muse ramps), we believe Meta's AI products are well positioned," Josey wrote.

Wood had a similar bullish take on Meta.

"For those of us who doubt that 'old-world' companies will thrive in the new world, Meta's third quarter stats were impressive," Wood said in an Oct.23 post on X .

Wood has been actively buying Meta stock over the past few weeks after Meta's September Muse launch. But Meta isn't a top 10 holding in the Ark Innovation ETF yet.

news.Title: Can Walmart's New Bundled Subscription Beat Amazon?
news.Content:
Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) is offering a bundled subscription deal that could knock Amazon 's (NASDAQ: AMZN) Prime membership off its pedestal. Earlier this week, the company announced a combined Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus membership for just $120 per year. That's $100 less than the two programs priced separately, and $19 less than Amazon Prime's $139 cost.

The bundle includes free delivery, 2% Sam's Cash on select purchases, $0.10 off per gallon of gas, and a choice between Peacock and Paramount+ streaming, among other perks. The catch is that it is only available as an annual subscription, and there's no free trial or monthly option available at this time.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Memberships have proven to be lucrative revenue channels for companies like Walmart and Amazon. Shoppers tend to spend significantly more with the merchant when they have a membership, roughly four times as much as non-members in Walmart's case.

So can Walmart's new subscription bundle dethrone Amazon Prime ? Probably not. Amazon Prime is so deeply entrenched at this point that the mix of streaming, fast shipping, and ubiquity among consumers is almost immovable. However, Walmart doesn't have to beat Amazon to succeed. This is what investors should focus on.

This particular offering strengthens Walmart's flywheel and advertising business. Walmart stock trades at a hefty premium, leaving little room for stumbles this holiday season. Some investors may want to wait for a better entry point. Still, overall, Walmart is an incredibly strong business that just created a new product that will help solidify and deepen customer engagement.

Shares of Walmart have risen nearly 6% year to date as of this writing. The stock is trading at roughly 40 times both forward and trailing earnings. The company's e-commerce segment continues to grow substantially, increasing 23% in the fiscal 2027 second quarter. Walmart's membership growth was also impressive at 17%.

Whether it overtakes Amazon or not, Walmart is a worthy investment.

news.Title: Does enough capital exist to finance everyone’s ambitious AI spending plans?
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Meta last week said that recent capital raises by peers such as Alphabet and SpaceX, and expected fundraising by Anthropic and OpenAI, have created an "increasingly challenging fundraising environment," raising questions over whether enough capital exists to fund AI spending plans.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

In results announced Wednesday, Meta reported revenue rose 26% from a year earlier to $64.6 billion, but free cash flow was -$2.1 billion.

It raised the low end of its 2026 capital spending forecast to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion and announced a new class of non-voting shares to make future capital raising easier.

Other executives voiced similar worries. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warned capital could become the biggest constraint on AI development. BlackRock CEO Larry Fink said competition for capital was the fiercest he had witnessed in his career. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said neocloud demand is "off the charts" but capital is scarce.

AI-linked stocks led the selloff. Nvidia fell 4.4%, CoreWeave 10.1% and Lam Research 11.8%, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) dropped 6.8%. The Nasdaq fell 2.6%, its worst day in four months.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Money moved to other parts of the market rather than out of stocks altogether, Yardeni Research said.

The S&P 500 with every company weighted equally edged up 0.7%, while the version weighted by company size fell 1.2%. The Dow edged up 0.02% and the Russell 2000 gained 0.11%.

Treasury yields fell across maturities. The 2-year yield dropped to 4.64%, and the 10-year yield fell below 5% for the first time in nearly a month.

Yardeni said the rally suggests market participants are increasingly concerned that tighter access to capital could slow the AI buildout.

Yardeni nonetheless expects the biggest players to keep access to financing, and called market-driven tightening healthy for the AI boom because it should mean money is used more efficiently and the risk of overspending falls.

Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle are projected to spend almost $780 billion in 2026 and more than $1 trillion a year from 2027 through 2030. Yardeni said their strong cash flows, balance sheets and market access should let them keep investing in AI.

news.Title: Sundar Pichai Reported Alphabet's Cloud Revenue Grew 82% Last Quarter While the Gemini App Reached 950 Million Monthly Users. Is Google Cloud Becoming a Bigger Growth Driver Than Search?
news.Content:
When it comes to artificial intelligence (AI), no company has a greater opportunity or threat from the novel technology than Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL). The parent company of Google, Android, YouTube, and other platforms is trying to steer its ship toward the AI opportunity head-on, with ChatGPT, Claude, and other chatbots potentially threatening Google Search's monopoly.

So far, this effort has not shown up in the financials, even as Google Search reached an all-time high in revenue last quarter. However, so did Google Cloud, with revenue growing 82% year over year, much faster than any other part of Alphabet's business.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Is Google Cloud now a bigger growth driver than Search?

Rapid cloud growth in the age of AI

Due to the AI infrastructure build-out, Alphabet's Google Cloud business is booming. As mentioned, revenue grew 82% year over year last quarter, reaching $24.8 billion. That is up from $13.6 billion in the same quarter a year ago, representing highly impressive growth for a business of this size, adding $11.2 billion in new quarterly cloud revenue compared with the previous year.

Google Search is not growing nearly as quickly on a percentage basis, as Q2 revenue rose 17% year over year. However, it is much larger than Google Cloud today, generating $63.3 billion in revenue last quarter and $54.2 billion in the same quarter a year ago.

Still, it was a lower nominal revenue increase than at Google Cloud, with $9.1 billion in revenue growth from a year prior, meaning that Google Cloud is now officially more important to Alphabet's revenue growth story than Google Search.

Can Cloud replace Google Search?

The fear with Alphabet's business is that ChatGPT, Claude, and even Alphabet's homegrown chatbot, Gemini -- which just reached 950 million monthly active users -- will replace Google Search volumes and, therefore, lead to a decline in advertising revenue. This is a real risk to the business given the rise in chatbot usage, and I think Google Search revenue could eventually hit a wall. However, it is not an apples-to-apples comparison, because the Gemini AI infrastructure now underlies all of Alphabet's services, including Google Search AI summaries.

Google Cloud has ample growth potential to mitigate any AI-related declines affecting Google Search. If the AI boom continues and Google Search is hurt, Alphabet may face a revenue headwind, but that will only mean more demand for Google Cloud's data center services.

Story Continues

Even so, Google Search revenue shows no signs of slowing, meaning the business is benefiting from Google Cloud growth alongside Google Search, which is why overall revenue grew 23% year over year last quarter.

I believe this matters to investors looking for the best AI inference stocks over the next five years because it expands AMD's rack-scale strategy beyond GPUs to include CPUs.

AMD's CPU-only configuration uses 6th Gen EPYC processors, while the all-in-one version pairs EPYC CPUs with Instinct MI350P GPUs. About AMD

Founded in 1969, AMD began as a small Silicon Valley second-source chipmaker, spent decades battling Intel (INTC) in CPUs, expanded into graphics through ATI, and, under Lisa Su, has evolved into a broad high-performance computing company increasingly positioned as Nvidia's (NVDA) principal challenger in AI accelerators. The company serves original equipment and design manufacturers, public cloud services providers, system integrators, distributors, and add-in board manufacturers.

AMD continues to benefit from strong demand for AI chips and server processors. Valued at a market cap of $843 billion, AMD has had a rocking 2026 so far, rallying by 147% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. It comfortably outperformed VanEck Semiconductor ETF's (SMH) gain of 49% during the same period. Surging data center sales and rising AI-driven CPU demand pushed it to an all-time high of $658.52 on Oct. 6.

Growth Makes the Premium Look Reasonable

AMD's valuation remains elevated, with a forward P/E of 75.24x, about 88% above its five-year average of 40.08x. Its forward price-to-sales ratio of 18.29x is also more than twice the five-year average of 8.72x. While these multiples represent a steep premium, strong earnings growth helps support the valuation. Analysts project EPS growth of 81.94% in 2026 and 107.67% in 2027. If those estimates hold, the P/E would fall around 36x on 2027 earnings, below its five-year average. Growth is expected to remain strong through 2029, reducing the multiple to approximately 18x. The company's balance sheet provides additional room for investment, with $13.11 billion in cash against $4.28 billion in debt. Both figures are relatively modest compared with its $931.85 billion market value.

Story Continues

If Advanced Micro delivers the expected earnings growth and Helion helps it capture agentic AI demand, I believe the company is positioned to grow over the next five years. This potential is why the stock appears on our list of the best American stocks to buy for the period.

Earnings Have Been Strong

Advanced Micro Devices reported its second-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings on August 4. It delivered strong second-quarter 2026 results that largely met high expectations. Despite a share price decline after the release, the company once again delivered a double beat on both revenue and earnings. Revenue rose 50% year-over-year (YoY) to $11.5 billion. Data center revenue reached $6.7 billion, reflecting growth of 107% from the prior year. Gross margins expanded meaningfully to 54% from 40% in the year-earlier period. Earnings per share surged 246% YoY to $1.66, exceeding the consensus forecast of $1.62. This marked the seventh consecutive quarter in which AMD outperformed profit expectations.

Looking ahead, AMD said it expects third-quarter revenue to be between $12.7 billion and $13.3 billion, with the $13 billion midpoint 41% above consensus. Adjusted gross margin is expected to be 56%. Su also said server revenue should grow more than 80% in the second half of 2026. Management now expects long-term revenue growth well above its prior target of over 35%. It also expects to beat its long-term $20 EPS target comfortably.

What Do Analysts Expect for AMD Stock?

Analysts are bullish on AMD stock. With an overall consensus rating of "Strong Buy," the mean target price of $653.74 is 18% above AMD's current price. The high target price of $1,250 indicates a potential upside of 126% from current levels. Out of 47 analysts covering the stock, 37 have a "Strong Buy" rating, two have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and eight have a "Hold" rating.

The firm expects AMD and other semiconductor companies to report slightly better-than-expected Q3 results and provide stronger Q4 guidance. It believes AI demand will continue to drive much of this growth. Similarly, Wedbush also reiterated a Buy rating with a price target of $600.

news.Title: Marvell’s Road to $90B: The 3 Moves Behind the Boldest Target in AI Chips
news.Content:
Investors don't have to bet on Nvidia (NVDA) alone to benefit from AI chip spending. Marvell Technology (MRVL) ranks among the top global chipmakers, thanks to its role in custom AI chips and data center connectivity. As companies develop more of their own processors due to the AI boom, Marvell could benefit from designing those chips and connecting the systems around them. This opportunity has led management to raise its fiscal 2028 revenue target to $20 billion. But can earnings grow fast enough to justify the stock's valuation?

Custom AI Chips Are Just One Part of Marvell's Growth Story

In my view, Marvell's biggest advantage is that its revenue streams are not just dependent on processors. The company raised its fiscal 2031 revenue target to $70 billion to $90 billion at its Oct. 6 investor day. It also expects custom chip revenue to exceed $12 billion in fiscal 2029. But I believe the broader opportunity is just as important. Marvell also sees opportunities in XPU-attached products, which add networking, memory, and other functions to AI processors. These products could give Marvell another source of growth beyond designing complete custom chips. CEO Matt Murphy's comments on the company's broader connectivity portfolio further support this thesis.

news.Title: Meet Wall Street's Newest Major Stock Split: It Has Soared 1,730% Since Its 2012 IPO, and There Is Plenty of Upside Left
news.Content: A stock split is a corporate action in which a company increases the number of shares it has outstanding by dividing existing shares into multiple shares and proportionately decreasing its share price. Stock splits don't change a company's intrinsic value, but they can garner significant attention because they make each share more affordable, potentially increasing trading activity. And the latest major corporation on Wall Street to announce a stock split is none other than Meta Platforms ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Meta Platforms (META) announced a stock split alongside its strong third-quarter results, which included a 26% year-over-year revenue increase to $64.6 billion.
• The company's operating income saw a year-over-year drop of 37% to approximately $13 billion, largely due to a $9.89 billion legal settlement charge.
• Excluding the legal charge, operating income would have increased by 11% year-over-year, and earnings per share rose 265% year-over-year to $3.83.
• Meta's daily active people across its platforms increased by 3% year-over-year to 3.64 billion.
• The stock split, involving the creation of Class C non-voting shares, is intended to help Meta raise capital for its aggressive artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions.
news.Keywords: stock split, Q3 earnings, revenue growth, AI investment, capital raising

It's a move aimed at boosting the potential for Amazon's custom application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) to take market share away from Nvidia 's (NASDAQ: NVDA) ...
news.AI_Summary:

• Amazon's AI chip business has a $25 billion annual revenue run rate, which is significantly smaller than Nvidia's revenue.
• Despite developing its own chips, Amazon continues to purchase large quantities of Nvidia chips, indicating Nvidia's continued dominance in the AI chip market.
• Nvidia reported 106% year-over-year revenue growth in its most recent quarter, and its guidance suggests continued substantial growth.
• The article suggests that while Amazon's chips may find niche applications, they are unlikely to significantly impact Nvidia's financial results in the near term.
news.Keywords: AI chips, market share, custom ASICs, competition, data center infrastructure

news.Title: Microsoft May Be the Only Hyperscaler to Stay Cash-Flow Positive. What It Means for MSFT Stock
news.Content: The artificial intelligence (AI) boom has pushed the world's largest technology companies into an unprecedented spending race. Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), and Meta Platforms (META) are pouring billions into data centers, advanced AI chips, and supporting infrastructure to meet surging demand for AI computing. While that spending has helped fuel optimism about the industry's long-term growth prospects, it has also raised an increasingly important question for investors: How much financial pressure can these companies absorb before their massive investments begin generating meaningful returns? A new report from BofA Global Research has brought that question into sharper focus. ...
news.AI_Summary:
• The AI boom is driving massive spending by hyperscalers like Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), and Meta Platforms (META) on data centers and AI chips.
• A BofA Global Research report indicates that Microsoft is the only major hyperscaler projected to maintain positive free cash flow (FCF) over the coming year.
• Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms are projected to experience negative FCF, with estimates suggesting their NTM FCF could fall below -$25 billion between 2026 and 2028.
• This divergence in FCF is becoming critical as investors scrutinize the financial returns on massive AI investments, which have seen AI capex growth outpace AI-related revenue growth.
• Microsoft's strong projected cash flow position is attributed to its diversified business model and AI strategy, particularly its Azure cloud platform and Copilot AI assistant.
news.Keywords: hyperscalers, free cash flow, AI spending, capital expenditure, financial sustainability

news.Title: Bloom Energy Just Reported—Its Biggest Order Is Still Waiting on a Pipeline
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Bloom Energy Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Bloom Energy's Q3 results show that Oracle's force majeure notice on its Jupiter project has minimal impact, since it represents only about 10% of a growing 25GW backlog.

Bloom Energy raised guidance for the third consecutive quarter after reporting $1.24 billion in revenue, up 138.9% year over year, with expanding margins and earnings beats.

Analysts remain bullish with a Moderate Buy rating and significant upside potential, even as share dilution and broader market corrections weigh on recent stock performance.

Bloom Energy's (NYSE: BE) Q3 earnings report shows strong growth despite uncertainty surrounding Oracle's (NASDAQ: ORCL) force majeure notice. While a headwind, it is offset by numerous tailwinds, and investors must not get this wrong: Bloom's broader growth outlook does not depend solely on Oracle's Project Jupiter, although any significant delay or cancellation would still carry risks.

The project represents roughly 2.4 GW, or about 10% of the 25 GW of potential deployments Bloom has identified, rather than its contracted backlog, which is growing and diversifying across industrial applications. Bloom has other clients to sell to.

→ Lam Research's Earnings Beat Wasn't the Real Story—Its 2027 Outlook Was

Oracle's lean into Bloom Energy fuel cells did what it needed to do for the business: validate them and put them in the spotlight. reported visibility into about 25 GW of potential deployments in Q2, underpinned by a growing number of clients. The critical detail is that Bloom's fuel cells, while not mobile, are modular, portable, easy to install, and production capacity is highly divertible. Oracle's headwind could become a tailwind for another project, which may now receive its cells sooner than expected.

And the status of Oracle's Jupiter New Mexico project? The pipeline intended to supply the center is now expected to enter service in February 2027, nearly six months later than originally planned. Oracle and Bloom have since confirmed the deal remains in place, but risks remain. The hang-ups include land and air quality, with New Mexico regulators pushing back against pipeline routes and environmental impact. As it stands, the issues are under review, but the project faces numerous legal challenges, not just those impeding the gas and power. The biggest risk is to Oracle, which took on billions in debt to fund its AI ambitions. While Jupiter is not directly tied to the debt increase, monetizing the asset is critical to its outlook.

Story Continues

→ Tesla's Flying-Car Hype Hits an Earnings Reality Check

Bloom Energy's Q3 Revenue Surges as Guidance Climbs Again

Bloom Energy had a very strong quarter, reporting $1.24 billion in net revenue, up 138.1% year over year (YOY) and nearly 16% above expectations. Product sales drove the strength, up 179.4%, with strength in the services and other segments. More importantly, volume leverage is clear in margins: gross margin expanded by more than 400 basis points, adjusted operating margin more than doubled from 8.9% to over 20%, and adjusted earnings per share rose to 94 cents, up 79 cents and 25 cents above forecast.

→ Is Texas Instruments Setting Up for Its Next Big Breakout?

The catalyst, however, is the guidance. Quarterly strengths and production trends led management to raise guidance for the third consecutive quarter. Revenue is now expected to be $4.5 billion at the midpoint this year, a 122% increase from last year, about 9% above the consensus target, with an equally strong earnings forecast. Earnings are expected to be $3.25 per share at the midpoint, more than four times the 2025 adjusted result, a forecast that could be exceeded.

One reason future results may exceed expectations is a new deal with American Electric Power Company (NASDAQ: AEP). Headquartered in Ohio, it serves 11 states, but the new 702-megawatt project is planned near Cheyenne, Wyoming, to serve Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL). The Bloom Energy deal combines its natural gas-fueled, noncombustion fuel cells with planned carbon capture to provide near-zero-emission power for Google data centers. While not immediately accretive, it reflects broader acceptance of Bloom Energy's technology and its growing importance in the distributed, colocated, lower-emissions energy ecosystem.

Wall Street Sees Upside, But Bloom Energy's Risks Remain

Analyst trends have been bullish all year, with coverage rising, sentiment firming, and price targets rising; post-earnings price-target changes have been mixed. Analysts maintain a consensus Moderate Buy rating on Bloom Energy, with price targets suggesting about 20% upside on average and more than 60% at the high end, despite the stock's recent decline.

The takeaway is that forces beyond the analysts are also in play, including the recent S&P 500 Index addition. It triggered an accumulation wave within an already-correcting market. Up about 2,000% over two years at its high, the market was already pricing in future strength and needed a correction. The narrative today is that the company is still outperforming, still driving a bullish outlook, and setting up for another upswing in its share price. The catalysts are numerous, but the most powerful is advancing the Jupiter project or capturing a deal to offset it.

The biggest risk to investors is dilution (also a factor in stock price action). The company's capacity ramp costs money and is being funded, at least in part, with share sales. The bad news is that outstanding shares increased by about 5.5% from year-end 2025 through Q3 2026, but there is an upside. Balance sheet highlights reflect a robustly growing, solvent business, with execution as its biggest challenge. Balance sheet details include a flat cash position, increased receivables, contract assets that grew 4x, and higher inventory, outpacing liability gains and leaving equity up 2.5x. The likely outcome is that Bloom Energy's backlog continues to grow, it converts contracts into capital, and it fuels its flywheel, which is building momentum.

news.Title: 美股分裂成兩大陣營！AI股與其他類股多空拉鋸 投資人被甩得暈頭轉向
news.Content: 美國股市分裂成兩大陣營的態勢愈來愈明顯，市場走勢宛如蹺蹺板，一端是人工智慧(AI)概念股，另一端則是其他類股。 標普500指數周四(22日)下跌逾1%，創7月以來最差表現，但同一天仍有超過300檔標普500成分股收漲。根據道瓊市場數據，大盤指數與成分股之間出現如此劇烈的分歧走勢，前一次發生在2025年1月。 市場戲劇性變化也反映出AI交易熱潮正面臨壓力。CNN的「恐懼與貪婪指數」發出強烈的恐懼訊號，而10年期美國公債殖利率則創下矽谷銀行(SVB)倒閉以來最大單日跌幅。 然而，通用磨坊(General Mills)(GIS-US)與金寶湯(Campbell's)(CPB-US)等民生消費必需品類股周四分別大漲8%及8.7%，仍不足彌補熱門AI概念股的跌勢。 費城半導體指數(SOX)當天收黑6.72%，與6月高點相比回落逾26%，正式遁入「熊市」。投資人今年稍早大舉買進被視為AI產業「瓶頸」受惠者的股票，曾推動費半指數在短短數個月內翻倍，如今卻已大幅回檔。 AI股與其他類股像蹺蹺板 市場輪動加劇 Nationwide首席市場策略師Mark Hackett表示，這只是美股日益分裂成兩大陣營的最新例證，2026年的交易走勢開始像蹺蹺板，一端是AI概念股，另一端則是其他所有類股，「領漲類股出現如此頻繁的變化，實屬罕見。」 美國銀行資產管理集團(U.S. Bank Asset Management Group)投資長Dan Farley指出，投資人在兩大陣營之間反覆轉換，持續的來回震盪讓一部分人感到暈頭轉向。 Farley以形容這種情況「就像坐上遊樂園的旋轉飛椅一樣，人會被甩來甩去」。 指數與成分股走勢分歧創紀錄 美股多頭行情已持續四年，市場對AI提升勞動生產力與企業獲利的期待，推升標普500指數與科技股為主的那斯達克綜合指數，使兩大指數的權重愈來愈集中於被視為AI建置受惠者的企業。 標普500指數成分股的平均表現，與市場認為的AI受惠股愈來愈脫節。目前標普500市值最大的10家公司，合計約占整體指數市值的40%，由於標普500採市值加權，個股市值愈大，對指數每日漲跌的影響也愈大。 以截至周四收盤的行情來看，標普500等權重指數有望收漲，但被視為AI交易核心的費半指數則可能收跌。若周五行情沒有大幅逆轉，兩大指數將連續第八周走勢相反，創下可追溯至1990年代中期以來最長紀錄。 資金仍留在市場 但分析師警告恐出現同步賣壓 瑞穗美洲(Mizuho Americas)股票交易部門執行董事Farzin Azarm認為，這種分歧未必全是壞事，投資人並非把資金撤出市場，而是持續在不同類股之間調整配置。 Azarm說：「類股輪動正在加速，但投資人實際上只是在市場內部重新調動資金。」 大型機構投資人、例如避險基金，也正在加速這項趨勢。高盛(Goldman Sachs)主要券商業務部門近期數據顯示，避險基金客戶已大幅降低整體槓桿部位。 Azarm說：「去槓桿的幅度相當大，但在我看來，這其實是個好現象。」

news.Title: 台股跌到季線就是買點？ 他搬出去年走勢：先蹲後跳
news.Content:
近期台股屢經震盪，對於台股未來走勢的預測也成為熱門話題。有網友對照去年第四季情況，認為回測季線後就可望迎來下一波漲勢，「先跌後漲」的歷史會重演，引發熱議。

該名網友在論壇PTT上以「大盤歷史重演多」為題發文，回顧去年第四季的股市情況，表示2025年的第四季也是在2萬8千點附近起伏，當時眾人也都期盼台股攻上3萬點，期間卻遭遇震盪，11月底、12月中曾兩度測試季線，但之後仍迎來漲勢，直接一波突破超過3萬點 。他由此分析， 認為第四季是最容易漲的一季，加上今年又有選舉年的行情，樂觀評估像去年「先跌後漲」的歷史會重演，甚至樂觀預回測季線之後，台股可望繼續迎來下一波漲勢，並附上兩張台股日K線圖佐證自己的看法。

▼原PO認為第四季是全年最容易漲的一季，並佐證去年第四季「先跌後漲」的經驗，認為同樣的歷史可望在今年重演。（示意圖／AI生成）

此論點吸引許多網友留言討論，對於原PO看好歷史重演的預測，眾人看法不一，有網友認同現在是進場布局的好時機：「長線來看，這裏是買點」、「特價買一下不好嗎」、「現在全世界散戶都知道AI未來很好，無腦買放著就是賺」、「千點震盪摩擦上五萬，雜質本來就該被洗出場」。

▼對於原PO第四季「回測季線後就會上漲」的樂觀預測，眾人看法不一。（示意圖／AI生成）

但也有網友認為原PO的預測太過樂觀，認為目前情況不能完全和去年類比：「都知道會崩到11月底12月中了，怎麼會選現在進場」、「去年很難重演啦」、「股票最大的盲點就是以歷史經驗來推測未來的走向」，認為即使後續有反彈行情，但未必如去年一樣會在短時間內發生，現在進場可能太早。此外，也有網友提醒，台股可能受美股影響，擔心若美股科技股修正，台股就可能被拖累，甚至認為融資水位仍有調整空間：「如果要續漲要清融資倒是真的」，甚至人直接批評「走下一波下跌」、「又一個反指標」。

還有些網友認為只要維持「分批進場、長期持有」原則，就不必過度猜測短線高低點。

news.Title: 台股失守季線原因找到了！陳龍直言「5萬點前最後洗盤」黑夜過後是黎明
news.Content:
台北股市昨（22）日加權指數重挫 846.34 點，當天盤中開高走低，失守季線支撐位置。長假避險賣壓加上國際地緣政治動盪，讓不少看著綠油油盤面的股民心驚肉跳。 對此， 知名資深分析師陳龍 在最新財經節目中直言，台股失守季線的原因找到了，當前的非理性拋售絕非 AI 產業基本面轉弱或泡沫破裂，而是台股在回頭挑戰 「5萬點前的最後洗盤」 。隨著下週美股四大雲端巨頭財報即將登場，AI 產業的強勁動能將重現光芒，展現 「黑夜過後就是黎明」 的強勢回升契機。

【外部雜音齊發！長假避險引發市場過度恐慌】

面對大盤急跌，陳龍強調，這波回檔並非台灣科技產業出了問題，而是多重外部利空巧合交織。一方面，連續假期讓避險資金抱持「先賣再說」的心態離場觀望；另一方面，中東胡塞武裝攻擊沙烏地機場推升油價、歐洲局勢動盪，加上台幣走弱，使市場避險情緒急速升溫。值得注意的是，全球資金大舉湧入美債避險，帶動 10 年期美債殖利率從高點顯著回落，這反而替台積電（2330）、聯發科（2454）等核心科技股的長線評價帶來上修空間。

【不是泡沫更無斷頭潮！神似年初歷史的「假破底」】

許多散戶擔憂台股是否會引發融資斷頭潮，陳龍給出堅定的定心丸。他分析，當前市場籌碼結構相當穩健，並不存在連鎖斷頭風險，整體型態極度類似今年年初大漲前夕的深蹲修正。當時市場同樣充斥著危機論調，但在震盪整理後，台股隨即迎來驚人的噴發走勢。陳龍指出，這一次短暫的假破底，本質上依舊是主力在挑戰更高峰前的清洗浮額，藉此醞釀下一階段躍升的龐大動能。

【算力需求爆發！AI革命才在初升段】

「AI 絕不是泡沫，而是剛剛拉開序幕的工業革命。」陳龍引用輝達（NVDA.US）執行長黃仁勳的說法指出，未來十年 AI 效能將迎來百萬倍躍升，現在只是基礎建設期的前三年，算力供給永遠趕不上爆發的需求。從 Meta（META.US）擴大資本支出，到台廠供應鏈如日月光投控（3711）先進封裝大幅擴產、京元電子（2449）砸重金擴建新廠，都證明半導體硬體鏈的成長引擎依然轟鳴作響。

【靜待下週巨頭財報！黑夜過後就是黎明】

下週大型科技股財報將成為市場焦點。Alphabet（GOOGL）與微軟（MSFT）預計於10月28日公布財報，亞馬遜（AMZN）則預計於10月29日登場。投資人除了關注營收與獲利，也將檢視雲端業務成長、AI需求，以及龐大資本支出能否帶來相應回報。

面對盤面風雨，陳龍提醒投資朋友，投資最忌諱在恐慌時被情緒牽著鼻子走。下週美國四大雲端服務巨頭即將接棒公布最新財報，屆時亮眼的真金白銀數據，勢必為 AI 族群再度注入強心針。當短期利空在連假後逐漸被市場消化，回頭來看，這段令人難熬的下挫，就是台股奔向 5 萬點大關前，市場給予投資人最後一次從容布局的禮物。

news.Title: 只要台積電破月線「就買進這檔」？ 他喊全力做多：勝率逾6成
news.Content: 近期台股震盪劇烈，投資人也開始思考未來的投資策略。有網友表示整理資料後發現，當台積電（2330）跌破月線時，就是富邦科技(0052)進場的好時機，引發討論。 該名網友在論壇PTT上以「只要台積電跌破月線就進場0052」為題發文，分享自己回測富邦科技（0052）的投資策略，表示自己整理相關數據後，發現只要台積電（2330）跌破月線，就是富邦科技(0052)進場的好時機，並嘗試回測，不論選擇在台積電跌破月線當天進場，或等到隔天再買進，獲得正報酬的機率都有6成以上，若持有1年，報酬更有超過10%的優異表現。除了月線之外，他還提到，「台積電跌破季線」也可能是另一個進場機會。 ▼原PO表示，自己整理資料並回測後發現，只要台積電個股跌破月線，就是0052進場的好時機，若持有時間超過1年，報酬可達逾10%。（東森新聞資料照） 因此他分析，市場回檔不一定代表應該急著出場，反而可以趁機觀察布局時點，並強調面對市場震盪，投資人不必因短期波動而過度恐慌。同時也分享自己的投資經驗，表示曾以3萬8千元買進的群益臺灣加權正2（00685L），目前已有約20%的報酬。他認為，單押0052這種持有多檔權值股如台積電、聯發科（2454）、鴻海（2317）、日月光投控（3711），對於希望長期布局科技產業的投資人而言，或許是相對容易理解的投資選擇。並認為只要維持「台積電跌破月線進場買0052，長期持有」的原則，就有一定勝率，最後還呼籲散戶網友們在市場震盪時，要「團結一心，全力作多！」 ▼原PO看好0052長期持有的獲利機率，認為近期台股震盪反而可能是進場布局的好時機。（示意圖／AI生成） 此話題吸引許多網友留言討論，有些網友認同原PO的論點，認為0052的表現不俗，也適合長期持有：「0052分批買起來！」、「0052長線報酬屌打0050」、「明天開始日日扣0052、0050」、「市值型平常定期定額，大跌手動買一些，然後蓋牌」。 不過也有網友認為，重點其實在於「長期持有」：「長期持有，你怎麼買都贏」、「長期持有可能跌不跌破月線差異不大」。還有一些網友主張直接買台積電個股就好：「為何不直接買台積就好？」、「為啥不跌破月線直接進台積零股」、「其實買台積電就好，長期投資，台積電的產品是寡占市場，所有公司都要跟台積電買」、「我也會直接撿台積電，價值慢慢浮現了」、「搞笑，買台積電就好啦」、「台積本來就是長期持有阿」。

news.Title: Microsoft wants to keep more of its AI billions from Nvidia

news.AI_Summary:

• Microsoft's Maia 300 chip, expected in 2027, aims to provide significantly more AI output per megawatt than top GPUs.

• Nvidia is not expected to be entirely replaced, as different AI tasks require different hardware, and Microsoft still relies on Nvidia's software ecosystem.

news.Title: 台積電護城河有多深？ 英特爾技術長揭「難追關鍵」：不只比技術
news.Content: AI算力需求持續飆升，全球半導體產業卻面臨設備供應跟不上需求的難題。英特爾技術長Pushkar Ranade近日接受Dwarkesh Podcast訪問時直言，即使資金不設上限，全球先進晶圓產能也不可能增加10倍，最多大約只能翻倍。問題不在電晶體設計，而是EUV曝光機、半導體製程設備、無塵室與晶圓廠建置速度都受到限制。 Ranade指出，全球每年交付的EUV設備不到100套，部分設備從下訂到交貨約需18個月，新廠擴建更可能耗時數年。這代表AI業者即使願意投入鉅資，也未必能立即換得更多晶片產能。當AI運算需求與實體製造能力出現落差，半導體競爭的核心，已從單純比拚技術，轉向設備供應、資本投入與量產效率的全面較量。 台積電規模優勢持續擴大 Ranade認為，英特爾與台積電真正難以拉近的差距，在於長期累積的規模經濟。晶圓廠建成後，約80%的成本屬於固定成本，因此產能利用率與良率每提高一些，都可能帶來可觀的經濟效益。台積電憑藉龐大的全球客戶群與先進晶圓產量，能將廠房、設備等成本分攤到更多晶圓上；英特爾過去則主要為自家產品生產晶片，近年才積極拓展外部晶圓代工業務。 依訪談內容，台積電先進晶圓產量超過英特爾3倍，2026年資本支出約500億美元，英特爾則約200億美元。台積電也持續擴大市場領先地位，《TrendForce》統計，台積電2026年第二季晶圓代工營收市占率達72.5%，三星電子以5.9%居次。對英特爾而言，即使製程技術逐步追近，若無法提高產能利用率、擴大客戶基礎並改善良率，龐大的固定成本仍可能成為競爭包袱。 High-NA EUV成關鍵分水嶺！ 先進設備的價值，也取決於各家晶片製造商採用的技術架構。英特爾製程主管Chris Auth指出，High-NA EUV曝光機透過提高數值孔徑，可在單次曝光中印出更精細的圖案，但設備價格極高，必須能減少多重曝光需求，才有機會證明投資效益。訪談估算，High-NA曝光機連同相關支援設備，整套系統約需4億美元。英特爾採用背面供電架構，將電源線移至晶圓背面，釋出正面佈線空間，因此認為High-NA有助降低曝光次數；台積電的製程架構不同，導入效益也不相同。 另一方面，英特爾過去曾因10奈米製程導入過多新技術而延誤進度，如今改採階段關卡審查，要求技術先達到良率、缺陷與效能標準，再進入下一階段。英特爾也計畫讓14A製程從一開始就提供較成熟的製程設計套件（PDK），改善18A初期在客戶設計工具與流程上的不足，爭取外部客戶信任。 技術只差幾個百分點 Ranade反駁英特爾與台積電之間仍存在整整一個世代的技術差距，認為雙方在效能、功耗與晶片密度等指標上，可能只差幾個百分點，但他強調，能否準時交貨、維持高良率並快速擴大產量，比單一技術指標更重要。英特爾規劃從18A邁向14A，部分既有設備可望沿用，有助降低新節點的設備需求與導入成本；不過，外部客戶是否願意採用，仍取決於製程成熟度、設計工具、交付可靠性與量產表現。 先進封裝也成為另一個戰場，英特爾持續發展EMIB與Foveros等技術，台積電則以CoWoS等方案服務AI晶片客戶，並已表態願意協助部分原先選擇英特爾封裝、卻面臨供應限制的客戶。從曝光機短缺到晶圓廠固定成本，再到封裝與客戶生態系，英特爾追趕台積電的挑戰不只是製程技術，而是能否建立可持續擴張的製造體系。

南韓KOSPI指數則在盤中一度下跌4%後，勉力轉為上漲0.3%。日本日經指數下跌0.3%，本周跌幅約4%。

中國A股藍籌股在跌至2025年7月以來低點後獲得買盤支撐，滬深300指數上漲0.8%。香港恆生指數也上漲0.7%，扭轉周四下跌3%的跌勢。

AMP副首席經濟學家Diana Mousina說：「目前還很難對整體股市過度看空，因為企業獲利仍在成長，實體經濟數據也維持穩健。這一切意味著，AI交易熱潮未必已經結束，但正在改變。市場不再是『什麼都買』的局面。」

Solidigm赴美IPO喊卡

SK海力士早盤股價一度下跌3%，但午盤後反彈漲逾4%。SK海力士周五發布聲明表示，評估近期資本市場情勢與股價走勢後，Solidigm將暫停評估上市前募資及IPO等選項。該公司同時正在探索各種融資方式，以因應AI記憶體需求持續成長，並為在美國興建新的半導體晶圓廠籌措資金。

SK海力士表示，Solidigm若能上市，原本有助於為業務擴張提供資金，並提高財務彈性，讓公司能透過發放股利、買回股票及註銷股票等方式回饋股東。

不過，金融市場波動加劇導致半導體類股普遍回檔，這使SK海力士重新評估，IPO是否有利於現有股東。

SK海力士另表示，Solidigm現有生產設施的產能有限，難以滿足AI帶動的記憶體需求成長，凸顯在美國增建產能的必要性。

南韓監管機關聚焦雙重上市規定

據路透報導，南韓金融監管機關周一表示，Solidigm若在美國上市，可能違反南韓限制雙重上市的規定。

南韓金融監督院院長李燦鎮(Lee Chan-jin)表示，監管機關正在檢視這項IPO是否須依照南韓相關規定接受審查，以保障少數股東權益。

對此SK海力士表示，Solidigm的投資需求維持不變，未來將持續尋求其他融資方式，以支持子公司成長並提升股東價值。

news.Title: 權證代號怎麼看？「購、售、牛、熊」代表什麼？一文看帶你從名稱快速看懂標的與類型！
news.Content: 當投資人打開券商 App 搜尋權證時，螢幕上總會跳出一長串像「密碼」一樣的名字，比如「台積電元大3A購01」或是「鴻海凱基39售02」等等。對剛接觸權證的新手來說，這些由中文、數字與字母組成的字串常讓人一頭霧水。但其實 發行券商早 ...
news.AI_Summary:
• 權證名稱包含標的股票、發行券商、發行序列及權證類型等關鍵資訊，可快速判斷商品性質。
• 「購」代表認購權證（看漲），「售」代表認售權證（看跌），「牛」代表牛證（看多），「熊」代表熊證（看空）。
• 權證名稱中的字尾「購」、「售」、「牛」、「熊」直接決定了投資人對未來行情的預判方向。
• 六碼數字代號也有識別標準，例如認售權證代號末位常為「P」，牛熊證系列則多帶有「C」或「B」。

news.Content: 「點開券商 App 看到一堆履約價、價內價外 15%、到期日…到底該怎麼選？」「看中某一檔台積電權證，萬一股票漲了但權證沒漲，是不是選錯履約價了？」權證雖然具備「低門檻、高槓桿」的優勢，但若搞不懂畫面上的參數與核心名詞，容易一不小心就買到快 ...
news.AI_Summary:
• 權證的價值取決於標的物、履約價、到期日與存續期間三大核心要素。
• 「價內」表示股票現價高於履約價（認購權證），具有內含價值；「價外」則反之，僅剩時間價值。
• 即使現股漲過履約價，若漲幅不足以彌補權利金成本，結算仍可能虧損。
• 建議挑選價平附近、存續期間長的權證，並嚴格執行短線停損，避免買入深度價外或即將到期的商品。
news.Keywords: 權證,履約價,價內價外,到期日,時間價值

news.Title: Meta found a new way to pay for its AI boom
news.Content: Meta Platforms (META) is preparing to give shareholders another share of stock. One crucial item that the new stock will deny them is a vote. Starting in January 2027, Meta will issue publicly traded Class C shares without voting rights. The economic effect of a two-for-one stock split will be one Class C share per Class A and Class B share. There is more to the move than just making Meta shares seem less expensive. As the corporation invests enormous sums of money in artificial intelligence, Meta claims that the new shares may be used to raise money, pay staff, ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Meta Platforms plans to issue non-voting Class C shares starting January 2027, effectively a two-for-one stock split, to raise capital for AI investments.
• The company anticipates capital expenditures between $135 billion and $145 billion in 2026 for AI development, including data centers and AI products.
• Issuing non-voting shares allows Meta to raise funds and compensate employees/acquisitions without diluting Mark Zuckerberg's control.
• Meta's free cash flow turned negative ($2.12 billion) in Q3 2026 after a year of positive flow ($10.63 billion), highlighting the increasing cost of AI initiatives.
news.Keywords: AI investment, capital expenditures, non-voting shares, stock split, free cash flow

news.Title: Amazon caught hackers probing a PHP flaw 4 days before the fix
news.Content: Most security breaches start with a lock nobody knew was broken. For years, that was the comfortable assumption behind the software that runs the internet. Bugs existed, but finding the dangerous ones took rare skill and a lot of time. That buffer has quietly disappeared. Artificial intelligence is now finding old flaws faster than humans can patch them, and attackers are using the same tools to turn fixes into weapons. If you have a website for your business, your side hustle or your church, this one lands on you too. The fix is free and already out. The hard part ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Amazon's security team detected attempts to exploit newly discovered PHP vulnerabilities on October 17, four days before a fix was released.
• AI is accelerating the discovery of software flaws, making it harder for developers to patch them before attackers exploit them.
• The identified PHP flaws (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) allow unauthenticated attackers to run code on vulnerable servers.
• The widespread use of PHP (estimated 75% of identifiable websites) and the rapid exploitation of these flaws led several government entities to take sites offline.
news.Keywords: cybersecurity, PHP vulnerability, AI, exploit, patch

news.Title: Google’s AI chip could become a $75 billion business
news.Content: Alphabet (GOOGL) built its artificial intelligence chips so Google would not have to depend entirely on Nvidia (NVDA) . These chips have the potential to grow into a massive enterprise. Evercore ISI predicts $75 billion in 2027 and $113 billion in 2028 sales of Google's TPUs to outside customers. As a result, technology that was initially intended to reduce Google's own computing expenses would become one of Alphabet's main new sources of income. Evercore analyst Georgia Anderson estimates TPU sales could represent roughly 35% of Google Cloud revenue in 2027 , according to Investor's Business Daily . She ...
news.AI_Summary:

• TPU sales could represent approximately 35% of Google Cloud revenue in 2027, positioning Alphabet as a key player in AI infrastructure beyond just cloud services.
• Google is offering TPUs to external clients for use in their own data centers, expanding revenue opportunities beyond its own cloud platform.
• The company's control over the entire AI stack, from processors to cloud and models, provides a competitive advantage, potentially offering 20-40% lower costs for optimized workloads.
news.Keywords: AI chips, TPUs, Google Cloud, revenue stream, AI infrastructure

news.Title: Volkswagen workers may get Microsoft AI instead of a raise
news.Content: Every company eventually has to decide what it will pay for when it can't pay for everything. For most of the last century, major industrial employers answered that question the same way. You hired people, trained them, and paid them more as they got better at the job. That bargain has been fraying for years at Volkswagen, the German group behind VW, Audi, Porsche, Skoda, and Cupra. Its chief executive has spent much of 2026 talking about job cuts, idle factory capacity, and a cost gap with rivals that he puts at roughly 20 percent. If you've ever sat through ...
news.AI_Summary:
• Volkswagen is equipping over 330,000 employees with Microsoft's AI assistant, Copilot, amidst discussions of a potential pay freeze for 2026 salaries.
• The company views the AI implementation as an investment to address a roughly 20% cost gap with rivals, rather than a discretionary expense.
• Microsoft's Copilot for enterprise costs $30 per user per month, suggesting a significant investment by Volkswagen in AI tools for its workforce.
• Labor representatives at Volkswagen are pushing back against the potential pay freeze, emphasizing that wage negotiations should occur at the bargaining table.
news.Keywords: AI adoption, employee productivity, cost reduction, labor negotiations, Microsoft Copilot

news.Title: Monolithic Power (MPWR) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
news.Content:
Monolithic Power (MPWR) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 29. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $7.80 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +64.9%.

Revenues are expected to be $1.16 billion, up 57.5% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 4.33% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts may not always get reflected in the aggregate change.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Monolithic?

For Monolithic, the Most Accurate Estimate is higher than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of +1.35%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination indicates that Monolithic will most likely beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Monolithic would post earnings of $5.88 per share when it actually produced earnings of $6.50, delivering a surprise of +10.54%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Monolithic appears a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Another stock from the Zacks Semiconductor - Analog and Mixed industry, NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), is soon expected to post earnings of $4.14 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +33.1%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $3.77 billion, up 18.8% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for NXP has been revised 0.5% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. However, a lower Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.27%.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), this Earnings ESP makes it difficult to conclusively predict that NXP will beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

Wall Street expects a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when Entegris (ENTG) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 29. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call will mostly determine the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations, it's worth having a handicapping insight into the odds of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This maker of equipment used in chip manufacturing is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.04 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +44.4%.

Revenues are expected to be $924.45 million, up 14.5% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.06% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

Story Continues

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Entegris?

For Entegris, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -2.06%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Entegris will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Entegris would post earnings of $0.83 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.93, delivering a surprise of +12.05%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Entegris doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

news.Title: Meta Stock Slips Despite 10 Million Muse Sign-Ups
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) reported third-quarter diluted EPS of $3.83, including a $9.89 billion charge tied to its settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health litigation. Excluding the charge, EPS would have been $7.40, above the analysts' consensus of $6.54. Revenue rose 26% to $64.60 billion, ahead of the $63.34 billion estimate. Meta shares fell 1.35% in premarket.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Average price per ad rose 14% and ad impressions 10%. Capital expenditures reached $34.91 billion, leaving free cash flow at negative $2.12 billion. Free cash flow turned negative for the first time since 2012. Meta guided fourth-quarter revenue to $73 billion to $76 billion and narrowed its 2026 capex outlook to $135 billion to $145 billion, from $130 billion to $145 billion. Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, CEO Mark Zuckerberg said.

On the earnings call , Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up Muse personal agents in about a month and a half, with about 25% using it on any given day. He said existing Muse users in the U.S. generate several hundred dollars a year each in Family of Apps revenue, and that Meta expects Muse to reach an even higher level over time because of the commerce it already sees. Muse is compute-intensive, but Meta expects to improve its cost efficiency more than tenfold in the next year.

Meta also approved a new non-voting Class C stock, to be issued in January 2027 as a one-time dividend it expects to work like a two-for-one split.

news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- A gauge of Meta Platforms Inc.'s credit risk surged to a fresh record Thursday and its bonds sank, as plans to ramp up capital spending reignited fears that tech giants will issue more debt for AI buildout in an already saturated market.

The price of five-year credit default swaps on the company's debt, which increases as investor concern grows, rose as much as 8.9 basis points to around 119.3 basis points a year, according to ICE Data Services. It's the highest intraday level since the swaps started trading.

Meta said it has agreed to spend about $825 billion in the future on various leases and contracts, many of them related to computing power and infrastructure for artificial intelligence. In July, Meta reported future spending commitments of almost $700 billion.

In addition to credit default swap prices rising, the company's bonds weakened relative to Treasuries.
