news.Title: Meta's new nonvoting shares create an overhang — and Wall Street wants it gone
news.Content:
Meta ( META ) has created a new overhang on its stock that Wall Street wasn't expecting when it established a new class of stock.

The Street's advice to Mark Zuckerberg and his team: Issue the stock fast so the focus can return to the clear product momentum the company is enjoying with its new Muse AI agent .

"The sooner the better in our view as it would remove the overhang and the Street now knows it will have non-voting shares in Jan'27, and Meta can still do a substantial equity raise before then without even coming close to impacting Mark's voting control," JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth said.

Meta announced late Wednesday that it is establishing a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock, which effectively serves as a 2-for-1 stock split.

Under the scheme — in part designed to keep founder Mark Zuckerberg working in California as the 5% billionaire's tax looms — existing shareholders will receive one new nonvoting Class C share for every Class A or Class B share they hold. Trading is slated to begin in January 2027.

Issuing nonvoting stock allows Zuckerberg to raise external capital for Meta's AI build-out without diluting his personal voting control over the tech giant.

The news took some air out of the balloon on what was an impressive quarter for Meta amid signs that its AI investments are paying off.

Meta's core advertising business reported a 26% increase in total revenue to $64.6 billion, powered by AI-driven recommendations, higher ad volume, and rising ad prices.

GAAP earnings per share came in at $3.83 versus analyst estimates of $3.56.

Meta stock fell 2% in premarket trading on Thursday.

"Net/net, some near-term noise in Meta shares, but we're encouraged by core Advertising and Meta's outlook for strong overall revenue growth in 2027, and the path to superintelligence is increasingly clear w/the Muse series of models & products," Anmuth said.

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

news.Title: TSX futures point lower following Meta, Tesla earnings
news.Content:
Investing.com - Futures linked to Canada's main stock index edged lower, as a surge in oil prices fueled concerns over energy-driven inflation, while worries swirled around the artificial intelligence trade following results from Meta Platforms.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

By 07:37 ET (11:37 GMT), the S&P/TSX 60 index standard futures contract had fallen by 13 points, or 0.6%.

On Wednesday, the S&P/TSX composite index finished higher by 0.6% at 36,324.99, notching its highest closing level since September 22.

Technology stocks advanced on strong quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer, while a jump in Toronto-Dominion Bank powered a climb in heavily weighted financial stocks.

Meanwhile, Canada and the province of Ontario announced a new slate of measures aimed to buffer domestic steel and auto companies against the impact of U.S. tariffs.

U.S. futures slide

U.S. stock futures fell sharply, as investors parsed through earnings from Meta and Tesla. By 07:50 ET, the S&P 500 futures contract had fallen by 78 points, or 1.0%, Nasdaq 100 futures had dropped by 514 points, or 1.7%, and Dow futures had retreated by 298 points, or 0.6%.

The main averages on Wall Street advanced in the prior session, buoyed by strong results from Musk's rocket company SpaceX and server maker Super Micro Computer. The returns helped to assuage some recent concerns around the sustainability of the artificial intelligence trade, although analysts at Deutsche Bank flagged that the decline in Nasdaq futures could be a sign that not all investors were reassured.

Jitters have surrounded the AI sector for several days, triggered by a combination of heavy debt-fueled spending on AI infrastructure and elevated borrowing costs. Roller-coaster movements in AI-exposed stocks have mirrored shifting sentiment around AI, especially after fresh corporate returns appeared to indicate that demand for the nascent technology remains solid.

"When it comes to AI overall, it really does seem like the space has (permanently) entered a new era, one defined by less hospitable (or at the least more discerning) capital markets, which is why investors aren't as impressed as they were before by big headline spending numbers given the increased scrutiny on how the infrastructure will be paid for," analysts at Vital Knowledge said in a note.

The analysts also flagged worries that fighting between the U.S. and Iran could flare up once again in the coming weeks, possibly threatening oil supplies out of the Middle East in the process. Partially driving these fears was a New York Times report that the U.S. and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections in November, targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile arsenal.

Story Continues

Against this backdrop, oil prices have marched higher. Benchmark Brent crude futures were last higher by 3.0% at $112.08 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures had gained 2.3% to $99.45 a barrel.

Gold prices, in turn, sank to their lowest level in more than two weeks.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

While the Federal Reserve is tipped to skip an interest rate hike at its October 27-28 gathering, markets are betting that the central bank will lift borrowing costs at its final meeting of the year in December. Last month, the Fed raised rates for the first time since 2023, citing a desire to quell mounting inflationary pressures.

Higher rates can dent the appeal of gold by increasing the opportunity cost of holding the non-yielding asset.

Meta, Tesla earnings in focus

Meta unveiled higher-than-anticipated third-quarter revenue and announced plans to create a new class of nonvoting stock to raise capital for its AI ambitions. Shares of the Instagram-owner turned lower in premarket U.S. trading.

Along with resilience in its core advertising business, the well-received debut of Meta's Muse AI assistant in September has helped bolster returns during a time when the tech titan is investing hundreds of billions of dollars into the AI race. Hopes have been high that Muse will eventually add $28.5 billion of incremental revenue by 2030, according to Truist Securities projections cited by the Wall Street Journal.

CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in a post-earnings call that roughly a fourth of people who have set up Muse use it on "any given day," particularly for shopping. Zuckerberg added that Meta is aiming to create a "large-scale Muse network," even though the app has been blocked on some websites, such as Amazon.com.

For the current quarter, Meta guided for revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, with the top end of the range exceeding Wall Street estimates. The firm also narrowed its capital expenditures forecast to $135 billion to $145 billion. The low end of the outlook was previously $130 billion.

Shares of Tesla also fell premarket, weighed down by the Elon Musk-led EV group reducing its goal for per-year sales by the end of the decade to 5 million units, while investors eyed the potential for a blockbuster tie-up with SpaceX.

Previously, Musk had guided for annual sales of 20 million vehicles. However, Musk has appeared to back away from this goal in recent years, focusing instead on pivoting Tesla's strategic focus to AI and robotics. Musk said the company is hoping to start shipping its Optimus humanoid robots to corporate customers by the end of 2027 and outlined plans for its autonomous taxis to become a major revenue source.

Cash flow was positive in the third quarter despite Tesla's big investments on AI and robotics. Still, Tesla predicted that it would end up spending around $20 billion in capital expenditures this year, compared to a prior estimate of $25 billion.

Quarterly revenue was flat, while net income dropped 4% to $1.7 billion.

Elsewhere on the earnings slate, American Airlines reported third-quarter results that exceeded analyst expectations but issued fourth-quarter guidance that fell short of estimates, sending shares down.

Lockheed Martin notched third-quarter results that surpassed estimates, as defense production accelerated across all business segments. Shares gained before the opening bell.

Spotify Technology premium subscribers grew by six million in the third quarter to 306 million, topping the audio streaming service's previous guidance and surpassing Wall Street estimates. Shares in the Swedish group advanced.

news.Title: Brokers Suggest Investing in Meta Platforms (META): Read This Before Placing a Bet
news.Content:
Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Meta Platforms (META).

Meta Platforms currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.29, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 56 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.29 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 56 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 47 are Strong Buy and two are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 83.9% and 3.6% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for META

Check price target & stock forecast for Meta Platforms here>>>

The ABR suggests buying Meta Platforms, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks.

There is also a key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank when it comes to freshness. When you look at the ABR, it may not be up-to-date. Nonetheless, since brokerage analysts constantly revise their earnings estimates to reflect changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in predicting future stock prices.

Should You Invest in META?

In terms of earnings estimate revisions for Meta Platforms, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has declined 7% over the past month to $29.94.

Analysts' growing pessimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates lower, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to plunge in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) for Meta Platforms. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, it could be wise to take the Buy-equivalent ABR for Meta Platforms with a grain of salt.

Super Micro Computer (SMCI) has expanded its AI data-center hardware lineup with a rack built around 256 NVIDIA Vera processors, designed to handle the parallel workloads generated by autonomous AI agents.

The liquid-cooled system contains 22,528 CPU cores and 45,056 threads, and can support as many as 22,500 agent sandboxes per rack. These isolated software environments let AI agents run tools, test actions and process intermediate steps while GPUs handle model computation.

news.Content:

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) Chief Operating Officer Javier Olivan sold 1,575 Class A shares for about $1.11 million on Oct. 19 under a trading plan established nearly a year earlier.

The shares sold at $707.2 each. Olivan disposed of 946 shares held directly, while the other 629 were sold through three limited liability companies and a family revocable trust. The plan was adopted on Nov. 17, 2025, under Rule 10b5-1, which allows insiders to schedule stock trades in advance. The reported transactions involved multiple ownership accounts rather than a single holding.

After the transactions, Olivan directly owned 5,986 shares. His reported indirect holdings included 5,670 shares through Olivan D LLC, 947 through Olivan Reinhold D LLC, 5,670 through Reinhold D LLC and 75,805 shares in the family trust.

news.Title: History Says This Will Happen to Sandisk Stock Heading Into Its Oct. 29 Report
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) has been one of the hottest stocks of the year. Its memory products are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers, and thanks to a shortage of those products, it's achieving extraordinary revenue and profit growth. As a result, the stock is up 478% so far in 2026.

The memory giant will report results for its fiscal 2027 first quarter on Oct. 29. Here's what history suggests might happen before it does.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Low supply for AI

As the artificial intelligence (AI) trend has progressed, the focus has shifted repeatedly. First, much of the interest was on the foundational models; then came demand for data centers and the AI accelerators and GPUs that provided compute for those models. There has been a concurrent boost to the energy sector as the tech players had to answer the question of where the electricity to power all of those new data centers was going to come from.

Now, getting enough memory for those data centers has become one of the most critical parts of the infrastructure build-out process.

Sandisk makes many kinds of memory products, from the memory cards in your smartphone to the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) in your laptop, but the recent frenzy is for its NAND flash memory, which can keep storing data even when it's not powered on, and is vital for AI training. Sandisk is one of the few makers of NAND, and data centers have become a huge part of Sandisk's business.

Scarcity is what's driving this rally -- demand from data centers far exceeds the supply of NAND that Sandisk and its peers can manufacture, so they've all been able to boost prices sharply, and all are experiencing rapid growth.

In Sandisk's fiscal 2026 fourth quarter (which ended July 3), revenue increased 372% year over year, and data center revenue doubled just from its fiscal Q3.

Is this the end of the cycle?

Despite its massive growth and soaring profits -- it booked $43.97 in earnings per share in its fiscal fourth quarter -- Sandisk stock is rather cheap, trading at a P/E ratio of under 19. That lack of a premium is tied to investors' worries that the end of this up phase of the memory cycle is inevitable.

Historically, memory companies have always gone through booms and busts based on the supply-and-demand cycle. When supplies are tight, prices rise, and manufacturers build new foundries to expand capacity. Then supply catches up to and exceeds demand (which often declines cyclically as well), and prices tumble again.

Story Continues

Right now, the AI build-out requires huge quantities of memory products, but data center construction and processor purchases are likely to taper off at some point. The question is when.

Anticipating this, Sandisk this year introduced its new business model (NBM) agreements, which lock in long-term sales deals with large customers, guaranteeing some price floors and purchase volumes for multiple years. It had eight NMBs as of the end of the fiscal fourth quarter. Management notes that it provides necessary infrastructure components to the biggest and most important tech companies, and those businesses are planning -- and purchasing -- several years in advance. It's also focusing on its highest-value products and markets, which management believes will lead to "more durable earnings power."

What might happen before Oct. 29

Western Digital spun off Sandisk in February 2025, and since its return to the market as an independent company, the stock has climbed prior to all previous earnings reports except the most recent one. By then, Sandisk stock had soared to an expensive level. It has started to rise again, but it's still not back to its previous high. So while history suggests it's going to climb again over the next few days, the trend has changed.

SNDK data by YCharts

Since the stock price is much lower today, there's room for it to rise in the coming days, and to keep heading higher after earnings if it meets or surpasses expectations. Management is guiding for $10.5 billion in revenue at the midpoint, a 357% increase over last year, and $45 in EPS. Wall Street is expecting a 363% increase and $46.27 in EPS. The market will also be looking for new business deals and guidance for continued high growth.

news.Title: 颱風薔琵衝擊台積電！ 10/24運動會取消
news.Content:
護國神山台積電（2330）預計10月24日舉行年度運動會，但卻碰上強颱薔琵，運動會取消。

台積電表示，受薔琵颱風影響，新竹縣市政府公告10/23 （五）停止上班，原訂於10/24 (六) 舉行之台積電運動會的準備工作也受到影響，考量人員安全，2026 台積電運動會將取消辦理。

每年台積電運動會都是市場焦點。回顧去年，輝達（NVIDIA）執行長黃仁勳特別到場挺台積電，創辦人張忠謀因為身體不適沒有出席，今年創辦人張忠謀是否出席原是外界矚目的關鍵。

更重要的是員工最期待的「神山紅包」，去年董事長魏哲家發給基層與中階台灣員工每人 2.5 萬元的特別獎金，並霸氣宣告會「一年比一年高」，今年在營運續旺下，原本各界相當期待發放金額能否再衝高，如今活動因颱風喊卡，也讓今年的獎金留待後續揭曉。

news.Title: Ford Plans to Overtake Toyota in a Critical Business. Here's Why It Matters.
news.Content:
About a year ago, Ford Motor Company (NYSE: F) made an intriguing move by partnering with online retailer juggernaut Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) that many investors overlooked. That was when Ford announced it would sell Ford Blue Advantage vehicles, or certified pre-owned (CPO) vehicles, on Amazon Autos.

Let's peel back the outer layers of this move, which has helped boost Ford's CPO sales by 44% during the third quarter and surpassed Toyota 's (NYSE: TM) volume for the first time. Here's exactly why Ford's expanding CPO sales is a great thing for long-term investors .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Pedal to the metal

Ford is well on its way to topping its 500,000 CPO sales target for 2027, which will likely remove Toyota from its spot as the industry's top certified seller. Better still, Ford's impressive 44% gain in CPO sales during Q3 comes with the industry's CPO sales declining 2.5% through August, according to Automotive News Data Center. This is all great news, but let's explain exactly how and why this is great news for long-term investors.

Ford launched its dealer-led CPO program, Ford Blue Advantage, in 2021. About 70% of Ford's 2,800 U.S. dealerships participate in the program, which also launched a similar program for Ford Pro commercial vehicles. What's interesting about Ford's CPO business is that when consumers buy a non-certified used vehicle, they return to the manufacturer only about 30% of the time. When that sale is for a certified vehicle, the consumer remains loyal and returns to the brand more than half the time.

"The biggest part that I press on our dealers of why it's important to certify the vehicles is that connectivity back to the brand," according to Rob Kaffl, Ford's director of U.S. sales and dealer relations. "You have an audience that we can now market to moving forward for a new vehicle or any of our other services."

Why CPO sales are important

Another big part of the CPO business for Ford is that after discontinuing the Escape and Lincoln Corsair last year, it has fewer entry-level options for consumers. CPO sales help the Detroit automaker fill this void for budget-conscious buyers and gives Ford another way for its dealers to retain and attract consumers.

CPO sales can also move the needle for Ford's overall sales, as it has started giving dealers certificates for each sale through its Ford Blue Advantage program, which effectively serves as an incentive to help lower new-vehicle prices. Ford's CPO sales have grown 96% since beginning in 2021 and are on pace to double its first six months of 2026 CPO sales during the second half of the year.

Story Continues

Investors shouldn't underestimate the importance of Ford's expanding CPO program because consumer loyalty in the automotive industry is incredibly powerful and "conquesting" consumers from a rival brand can be costly. Increasing loyalty, filling the void of entry-level options, and creating a new car sales pipeline through dealer certificates and incentives can move the needle for new vehicle purchases. All in all, if Ford executes and indeed surpasses Toyota in CPO sales next year, it's just one more reason to believe Ford is still turning into a well-rounded business for long-term investors.

news.Title: Stocks fall as Meta dents AI optimism; French bonds under fire
news.Content:
By Amanda Cooper and Alun John

LONDON, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Global stocks retreated on Thursday, as tech earnings could not offset nagging concern over the outlook for AI, while a stalemate in the Gulf pushed up oil prices ‌and investors took aim again at French markets.

MSCI's All-World index was set for its largest daily fall in two ‌weeks, down 0.4%, as tech shares from Seoul and Tokyo to Amsterdam and Paris tumbled.

Meta, the first of the so-called AI hyperscalers to publish quarterly results, reported ​third-quarter revenue late on Wednesday that beat expectations. But any optimism was short-lived, after the company unveiled a plan to issue non-voting stock that revived concern over its mounting capital commitments.

"There are lots of crosscurrents in markets at the moment, which are grappling for a narrative right now," Ben Laidler, head of macro and equity strategy at Bradesco BBI, said.

"The big concern is that AI-driven earnings narrative, which ‌has supported US earnings and spread to global ⁠equities, may be challenged here."

Meta also suffered a legal blow overnight, after a judge in New Mexico ordered the company to pay a $25 billion penalty to the state in a data privacy case.

In Europe, ⁠the STOXX 600 fell 0.7%, weighed down by tech-related stocks such as ASML, Schneider Electric and Siemens Energy. US stock futures fell between 1% and 1.7%, suggesting a drop at the opening bell later.

Shares in Meta fell around 3% and those in Tesla, which also reported earnings ​and ​cut its spending forecast ahead of a possible merger with SpaceX, dropped ​nearly 4% in the premarket.

Geopolitical concerns played out ‌in oil markets, where Brent crude rose nearly 3% to $112 a barrel, near a five-month high, after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised the risk of wider conflict and supply disruptions in the Middle East.

There was enough nervousness about the possible damage to the global economy to offset concern about a sustained pickup in inflation to drive flows into government bonds, which pushed US Treasury yields down by the most in a week. The 10-year note was last 10 basis points lower at 5.05%, trading below that of ‌France for the first time in 13 years.

French government bonds have been battered ​this month, driving yields above 5% for the first time since 2002, ​as investors looked for signs the government can contain ​social unrest and bring spending under control. French 10-year yields rose 11 bps to 5.107%, headed for ‌their largest weekly rise since May.

Story Continues

The euro, which has ​been dragged 0.8% lower this month, ​was steady on Thursday, falling 0.3% to $1.12, leaving the dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six others, up 0.1%.

The yen drew safe-haven demand, leaving the dollar down 0.7% on the day at 157.1, after Deputy ​Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino signalled ‌his readiness to raise borrowing costs.

Gold missed out on safe-haven flows, dropping 1.8% to $4,070 an ounce, while in ​cryptocurrencies, bitcoin and ether both lost 3.5% to trade at $81,837 and $2,405, respectively.

(Additional reporting by Jiaxing Li in Hong ​Kong; Editing by Kate Mayberry, Shri Navaratnam, Susan Fenton, Elaine Hardcastle)

news.Title: IBM Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates on Software, Infrastructure Growth
news.Content:
International Business Machines Corporation IBM reported strong third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings rising 11% year over year to $2.95 per share. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.88 by 2.4%. Revenues increased 4.7% to $17.10 billion, surpassing the consensus mark of $16.87 billion by 1.4%.

The upside reflected accelerating Software and Infrastructure growth, improved transaction execution and productivity initiatives. Software annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $24.9 billion, up 8% year over year. Operating pre-tax margin expanded 70 basis points (bps).

International Business Machines Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

International Business Machines Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | International Business Machines Corporation Quote

Software Growth Accelerates on Deal Closures

Software revenues increased 8.2% year over year to $7.80 billion, up 8.7% at constant currency. Hybrid Cloud revenues grew 11%, supported by Red Hat, while Data jumped 20% at constant currency, benefiting from Confluent's performance. Automation declined 3% amid a challenging comparison.

Transaction Processing rebounded sharply, growing 10% at constant currency after a soft prior quarter. Management attributed the recovery to renewed demand and the closure of approximately two-thirds of large transactions delayed from the second quarter. These deferred deals contributed roughly one-quarter of the sequential Software growth acceleration.

Red Hat bookings growth accelerated to the high teens, while OpenShift ARR surpassed $2.4 billion, increasing more than 30%. Software segment profit climbed 15.2% to $2.73 billion, lifting margin 210 bps to 35%.

Infrastructure Benefits From Storage Demand

Infrastructure revenues rose 4.2% year over year to $3.71 billion, representing 4.9% growth at constant currency. Hybrid Infrastructure advanced 9% at constant currency, driven by 32% growth in Distributed Infrastructure, reflecting broad-based strength in storage and Power systems.

IBM Z revenues declined 19% at constant currency against a demanding year-ago comparison. Nevertheless, the z17 program generated more than $1 billion in incremental revenues compared with the previous generation over six quarters. New midrange systems also delivered the platform's strongest midrange revenue launch in nearly two decades.

Infrastructure segment profit increased 11% to $715 million, while margin expanded 120 bps to 19.3%, aided by productivity initiatives.

Story Continues

Consulting Business Sees Modest Improvement

Consulting revenues were nearly flat year over year at $5.34 billion, increasing 1.8% at constant currency. Strategy and Technology grew 4% at constant currency, supported by application modernization and data and AI transformation demand. Intelligent Operations remained flat on a constant-currency basis.

Generative AI accounted for approximately 30% of quarterly Consulting revenues and 35% of backlog. Consulting signings totaled $5 billion, declining 2% at constant currency, while the trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio was 1.04.

Segment profit declined 4.8% to $653 million, with margin contracting around 60 bps to 12.2% as IBM reinvested productivity savings into digital capabilities.

Profitability Expands Despite Cost Pressure

IBM's non-GAAP gross profit rose 4% to $10 billion, although gross margin contracted 20 bps to 58.5%. Operating expenses and other income totaled $6.71 billion, declining roughly 2% year over year.

Non-GAAP pre-tax income increased 9% to $3.30 billion, while adjusted EBITDA rose 7% to $4.9 billion. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved approximately 60 bps to 28.7%, reflecting operational efficiencies across general administration, sales and software development.

Strong Cash Flow and Liquidity

IBM generated $4.03 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter compared with $3.08 billion a year earlier. Free cash flow increased $0.7 billion to $3 billion. For the first nine months, free cash flow reached $7.8 billion, up $0.6 billion year over year.

The company exited the September quarter with $11.1 billion in cash, restricted cash and marketable securities. Total debt was $63.8 billion, including $12.7 billion attributable to IBM Financing. Quarterly dividend payments totaled approximately $1.6 billion.

Outlook

IBM reaffirmed its full-year 2026 constant-currency revenue growth expectation of 4% to 5%. However, management raised its free cash flow outlook, now anticipating an increase exceeding $1 billion year over year.

Software revenues are projected to grow 7% to 8%, supported by double-digit Hybrid Cloud growth and mid-teens Data expansion. Transaction Processing is now expected to remain flat for the year, an improvement from previous expectations.

Infrastructure revenues are forecast to grow in the low single digits, while Consulting growth is expected to accelerate to the low-to-mid-single-digit range. IBM also maintained its target of 100 bps operating pre-tax margin expansion for 2026, supported by continued productivity improvements.

Zacks Rank

IBM currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Upcoming Releases

Arista Networks Inc. ANET is scheduled to release third-quarter 2026 earnings on Nov. 3. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at $1.08 per share, suggesting growth of 44% from the year-ago reported figure.

Arista has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 22.8%. Arista delivered an average earnings surprise of 8.9% in the last four reported quarters.

Akamai has a long-term earnings growth expectation of 5.9%. Akamai delivered an average earnings surprise of 4.8% in the last four reported quarters.

GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. GFS is set to release third-quarter 2026 earnings on Nov. 4. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings is pegged at 51 cents per share, implying a rise of 24.4% from the year-ago reported figure.

news.Title: Can Nebius' Open Compute Pricing Strengthen Its AI Cloud Growth?
news.Content:
The rapid expansion of AI is driving unprecedented demand for GPU computing, yet high-performance infrastructure remains costly and hard to manage. Nebius Group N.V. NBIS is addressing this challenge by introducing public live spot pricing for GPU compute. The initiative provides customers with greater visibility into computing costs and expands how they can access and pay for AI infrastructure. It also underscores Nebius' broader strategy to build a full-stack AI cloud powered by NVIDIA NVDA infrastructure, expand its European footprint and support workloads ranging from model training to production inference and physical AI.

Nebius is broadening its AI compute pricing options with transparent spot pricing, reserve auctions, pay-as-you-go access and a pilot program that lets customers recover value from idle GPUs. This flexible approach caters to both short-term and ongoing computing needs, while clearer pricing helps customers compare providers, simplify purchasing and scale AI projects from experimentation to deployment. Nebius is building its AI computing footprint across Finland, France, the U.K., Spain, Estonia and Iceland, while evaluating additional deployment opportunities. In August, NBIS expanded its U.K. AI footprint with NVIDIA-powered infrastructure at Vantage's Newport campus, supporting diverse AI workloads.

NVIDIA partnership strengthens the full-stack AI cloud strategy. Its AI Cloud combines NVIDIA accelerated computing and networking with custom servers, machine learning tools, managed inference and infrastructure engineering. The company is also expanding its Physical AI Workbench with agentic workflows for robotics and industrial applications. Nebius reports customers have reduced engineering time by up to 40%. In June, NBIS announced approximately £1.7 billion of committed capacity buildout across four U.K. sites. Newport expands Nebius' U.K. capacity while diversifying its AI cloud footprint.

However, Nebius faces intense competition from hyperscalers and specialized GPU cloud providers like CoreWeave CRWV and Microsoft MSFT, as transparent pricing alone may not provide an edge if rivals offer similar performance at lower costs.

Intense Competition Hurting NBIS' Opportunities

CRWV recently took a major step in its global expansion strategy by entering India, announcing plans to develop 240 MW of AI data center capacity through a collaboration with AdaniConneX at its Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai. CoreWeave also expanded beyond GPUs with NVIDIA Vera and Vera Rubin, targeting agentic AI and inference workloads while deepening its infrastructure strategy. In September, CRWV launched Physical AI Field Engineering, an offering designed to help automotive, aerospace, robotics and other engineering teams build, validate and deploy AI throughout the engineering lifecycle. In August, CoreWeave secured a multi-year HRT deal to build an AI research platform powered by NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 and Spectrum-X networking.

Story Continues

Microsoft capitalizes on AI business momentum and Copilot adoption alongside accelerating Azure cloud infrastructure expansion. In October, Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra powered by NVIDIA's RTX Spark chip, alongside a new Windows Hybrid Intelligence framework, a redesigned Windows Search, expanded Copilot capabilities including local file access and new AI agent security features via Microsoft Execution Containers. Recently, Microsoft pledged an additional $2 billion in investment in the Gulf region, deepening its AI and cloud infrastructure commitments across the Middle East. In August, Microsoft announced that it delivered NVIDIA's first production Vera Rubin GPUs to its data centers.

NBIS Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Shares of Nebius have gained 105% year to date compared with the Internet – Software and Services industry's growth of 10.7%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

In terms of price/book, NBIS' shares are trading at 4.2X, higher than the Internet Software Services industry's 3.6X.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for NBIS' earnings for 2026 has been revised upward over the past 60 days.

NBIS currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Investing.com - U.S. stock index futures fell sharply on Thursday as investors assessed quarterly results from Meta Platforms and Tesla, while renewed concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending weighed on technology shares.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The earnings reports put the focus on whether heavy investments in AI infrastructure, robotics and autonomous driving can deliver sufficient returns.

By 07:16 ET, S&P 500 futures had fallen 1.1%, Nasdaq 100 futures had dropped 1.7%, and Dow futures had retreated 0.7%.

Meta Platforms shares fell more than 1% in premarket trading despite the Facebook and Instagram parent beating third-quarter revenue and earnings estimates and forecasting stronger-than-expected revenue for the current quarter. Revenue rose 26% year over year to $64.60 billion, ahead of the $63.33 billion consensus, while earnings per share came in at $3.83, compared with estimates of $3.57. Advertising revenue also climbed 26% to $63.06 billion, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg saying engagement on Facebook and Instagram had reached record levels.

Meta forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, above expectations at the midpoint, but raised its annual capital spending outlook to $135 billion-$145 billion from $130 billion-$145 billion as it continues investing heavily in AI infrastructure. Earnings also included a $9.89 billion legal charge related to a settlement with 52 state attorneys general over teen mental health litigation.

Tesla shares dropped 5.0% in premarket trading to $367.20 as investors reacted to the company's outlook for spending, vehicle sales and future growth. The electric-vehicle maker reported adjusted earnings per share of $0.48, beating estimates of around $0.43-$0.44, while free cash flow reached $1.53 billion, well above expectations.

However, net income attributable to common shareholders fell 29% year over year to $787 million, and automotive revenue declined 3% amid lower average selling prices and battery supply constraints.

Tesla also cut its full-year capital expenditure forecast to around $20 billion from more than $25 billion, raising questions about the pace of its AI and robotics investments. CEO Elon Musk said the company was targeting 5 million vehicle sales by the end of the decade, well below his earlier projection of 20 million. Tesla expects to begin shipping Optimus humanoid robots to corporate customers by the end of 2027, while meaningful robotaxi revenue is not expected until 2027-2028.

Story Continues

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

International Business Machines shares slid 5.7% before the opening bell despite the technology company's third-quarter earnings and revenue beating analyst estimates. IBM reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.95, above the $2.86 consensus, while revenue of $17.1 billion topped forecasts of $16.82 billion.

However, the company's adjusted gross margin of 58.5% fell short of the 59.1% estimate, and IBM left its full-year constant-currency revenue growth forecast unchanged at 4%-5%. Comments from CEO Arvind Krishna about corporate customers questioning whether AI investments were generating measurable returns also weighed on sentiment.

Lam Research fell 8.4% in premarket trading even after the chip-equipment maker reported record fiscal first-quarter revenue and beat earnings estimates. Revenue for the quarter ended September 27, 2026, reached $8.22 billion, up 54% year over year, while adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.20, narrowly above the $2.18 consensus.

The operating margin also exceeded 40% for the first time in the company's history. Despite the strong reported results, investors appeared focused on what the company had not delivered, with the shares coming under pressure amid renewed concerns around technology and AI-related stocks.

CSX shares rose 2.4% in premarket trading after the freight railroad reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter results the previous evening. Adjusted earnings reached $0.57 per share, topping the $0.53 analyst estimate, while revenue rose to $4.02 billion from the $3.95 billion forecast. Operating income totaled $1.57 billion and net earnings reached $1.05 billion. CEO Steve Angel attributed the performance to disciplined execution that helped the company move more freight while maintaining its safety and service standards.

Rollins, the parent of pest-control company Orkin, dropped 7.3% after reporting third-quarter results that missed analyst expectations. Revenue increased 6.2% year over year to $1.09 billion but fell short of the $1.11 billion consensus.

Adjusted EBITDA of $257 million also missed estimates, while the operating margin contracted 140 basis points to 20.5%. Adjusted earnings per share of $0.34 came in below the $0.35 consensus. CEO Jerry Gahlhoff said the company was disappointed with its performance and was taking action to address the challenges affecting results.

Dow shares rose more than 2.5% in premarket trading after the chemicals maker reported third-quarter adjusted profit above Wall Street expectations, as higher polyethylene prices and cost-cutting measures helped offset rising raw material and logistics costs. Revenue from its Packaging and Specialty Plastics segment increased more than 18% year over year to $5.8 billion, supported by higher polyethylene and functional polymer prices across all regions. Dow has also been restructuring its operations, including plans to cut 13% of its workforce and close higher-cost assets.

Lockheed Martin gained nearly 2.5% in premarket trading after the defense contractor raised its full-year sales and profit forecasts following higher quarterly earnings, as geopolitical conflicts continued to support demand for military equipment.

The company now expects 2026 sales of $80 billion to $82 billion, up from its previous forecast of $79.75 billion to $81.75 billion, while its earnings-per-share outlook increased to $30.35-$30.75 from $29.95-$30.65.

Lockheed's backlog rose 27% sequentially to a record $292 billion, bolstered by a $52.5 billion multiyear award for PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement interceptors. The company joined RTX and Northrop Grumman in raising its outlook this week amid strong demand for missile-defense systems, munitions and military aircraft.

Spotify shares climbed more than 3.8% in volatile premarket trading after the music-streaming company forecast fourth-quarter operating income above analyst expectations, betting that AI-powered features will help drive user growth during the holiday season.

The Swedish company expects operating income of €820 million ($920.53 million), compared with the analyst consensus of €813.4 million. In the third quarter, operating income came in at €672 million, broadly in line with expectations, while revenue of €4.97 billion fell slightly short of the €4.98 billion forecast.

news.Title: Google Hits Major Quantum Breakthrough. This Could Be a Game-Changer for GOOGL Stock.
news.Content:
Alphabet (GOOGL) just made another headline with a major quantum breakthrough. That gives investors another reason to take Google's long-term research ambitions seriously. This time, Google said its "magic state cultivation" technique cut errors roughly 40-fold on its Willow quantum processor and achieved 99.99% logical fidelity for a critical quantum state. The result, published in Science , tackles one of the technical bottlenecks standing between today's experimental machines and useful fault-tolerant quantum computers.

For GOOGL stock, however, this is not an immediate earnings catalyst. Commercial applications remain years away, and Google acknowledges that the technique must work at a much larger scale. The bigger picture is that Alphabet continues to invest in research that could create new computing capabilities over time, while its existing businesses fund the effort.

More News from Barchart

'No Question Tesla's Going to Merge With SpaceX' — Kevin O'Leary Says If You Own Tesla Stock, You'll Own the New Company After Flying Roadster Demo

Jensen Huang Says the Next Wave of AI Is Physical. Forget Nvidia and Tesla, I'd Bet on These 2 Mid-Cap Stocks Instead.

AST SpaceMobile Stock Gets a New Catalyst. Wall Street Sees 93% Upside.

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

The stock has more immediate drivers. GOOGL closed at $340.3 on Oct. 20, 2026, up 8% year to date (YTD) but about 17% below its 52-week high of $408.6.

Google's Breakthrough Tackles a Costly Quantum Bottleneck

Certain operations are crucial for universal quantum computing that require the use of "magic states" in quantum computers. Creating these states reliably can require vast computing resources: Google claims that some estimates are as high as 95% of a machine's capacity. The way it is cultivated eliminates bad ideas for creating more faithful states, which may also influence the resources that are required to create more practical systems.

The ability to do this presents "a crucial step towards scaling-up quantum computing to practical use," said Google Quantum AI researchers. But this can't be interpreted to mean that Google has created a viable business-ready quantum computer. The team reports more engineering work and larger-scale demonstrations are required. The accomplishment bolsters Alphabet's technology reputation, though it still doesn't offer a breakdown of the revenue path or when it will begin generating cash.

Cloud Growth Is the Near-Term Story, but Spending Is Rising

Story Continues

The numbers of Alphabet reveal where the clear-cut financial opportunity lies. The tech company's revenue in Q2 2026 increased by 24% YoY to $119.8 billion due to strong growth in its AI infrastructure and services, whereas Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.8 billion. We saw huge growth in cloud operating income, and the backlog of operating revenue across the cloud segment of $514 billion was a good sign of the demand that was contracted.

In a message, CEO Sundar Pichai noted that the company's investments in artificial intelligence are changing the possibilities in all facets of its business. This declaration reflects Alphabet's wider goals, including that AI and sophisticated computing science research could help to cement Alphabet's products over time, and Cloud is already turning investments in infrastructure into earnings.

But the trade-off here is cash flow. Alphabet's free cash flow was negative $5.9 billion, while the company also boosted its capital expenditure guidance to $195 billion to $205 billion for the 2016 year. It offers such significant cash and marketable securities buffers, but if demand and/or monetization are disappointing relative to the high spending, then cash flow and returns on investment could become a challenge. In a portfolio of 'big money' bets for even longer duration, quantum research is a bet that shouldn't be made because of the advancement of science, but because of the expected increase in profit.

Some support is provided by valuation. Alphabet's P/E ratio is approximately 17x, which is lower than the communication services subindustry median of 19x. That indicates that investors are not buying into Alphabet at the highest valuation in the sector for its future earnings, but does not mean that higher valuations will lead to further gains.

Wall Street's View on GOOGL Stock

Wall Street sentiment remains extremely positive. The analysts covering GOOGL have a consensus of "Strong Buy" for the stock, with 53 analysts believing the shares are worth purchasing. Analysts have an average price target of $432, which means they expect the stock to see a 27% gain from the existing market price.

BMO Capital has just increased its forecast to $480, up from $465. The company highlighted robust sales of Cloud checks, as well as sales of scaling TPUs. KeyBanc also rated the stock Buy, but lowered its price target to $410 from $435.

J.P. Morgan moved its target to $425 from $420. Morgan Stanley keeps an Overweight rating. UBS, on the other hand, has rated the company Neutral with a $380 target.

One analyst summed it up well. The new releases for Gemini are reassuring for the execution of AI. Another commented that momentum from Cloud and TPU is a significant long-term force. That's a clear message. Alphabet has the means to succeed with the transition to AI. It's an unusual combination of growth and fair valuation on the stock. It simply has to try to keep that money flow in check.

news.Title: 台股震盪「瑤池金母」連5天砸117億再掃7檔AI股：這檔買到只輸台積電
news.Content: 台股今（22）日重挫846.34點，收在46,041.43點，跌幅1.81%，高檔震盪讓市場關注資金動向。被封為 「瑤池金母」 的統一投信基金經理人 陳釧瑤， 操盤的主動式ETF統一台股增長 （00981A） 卻持續加碼AI供應鏈。 財經專家《籌碼小哥葛》 指出，00981A截至昨（21）日已連續5個交易日「只買不賣」，累計買超金額約117億元，更於21日大盤反彈594點時，再次掃貨7檔AI大軍，展現強烈多頭意圖。其中欣銓（3264）獲買超5.75億元最多，欣興（3037）則升至第二大持股，僅次於台積電（2330）。 【00981A連5天只買不賣！累計加碼約117億元】 《籌碼小哥葛》在臉書發文分析，台股21日反彈594.84點，收在46,887點，但法人並未全面大舉回補，三大法人合計僅小幅買超約5.7億元。在市場震盪之際，00981A的操作方向格外受到關注。 他觀察，00981A近期操作呈現 「指數回檔就買、高檔反而調節」 的特徵，並非單純追逐股價上漲，而是趁市場震盪逐步增加看好的持股。截至21日，00981A已連續5個交易日「零賣出」沒有賣出股票，期間累計買超約117億元。即使21日台股反彈，基金仍持續加碼，顯示其資金配置依舊偏向看好的產業主線。 【瑤池金母再掃7檔！欣銓獲買超5.75億元居冠】 根據00981A於10月21日的持股異動資料，當天共加碼7檔個股，沒有新增或減碼其他持股。依買超金額排序如下： 1.欣銓（3264）：買進2,170張，約5.75億元。 2.奇鋐（3017）：買進114張，約3.69億元。 3.緯創（3231）：買進1,300張，約2.54億元。 4.富世達（6805）：買進100張，約2.40億元。 5.欣興（3037）：買進190張，約2.09億元。 6.智邦（2345）：買進67張，約1.22億元。 7.京元電子（2449）：買進236張，約0.66億元。 7檔個股合計買超金額約18.35億元，涵蓋半導體測試、AI伺服器、散熱、網通及PCB載板等領域。從持股異動來看，00981A並未因短線震盪轉向防禦型配置，而是繼續加碼AI與半導體相關供應鏈。 其中，緯創（3231）繼前一日剛建倉後，21日再加碼1,300張，以當日收盤價195元估算，買進金額約2.54億元，呈現連續兩個交易日加碼的情況。

庫藏股自救！有「吸金怪獸」之稱的半導體廠漢測（7856）一度凍資台股8千多億元，還創下新股抽中一張賺245萬元紀錄，如今上櫃才一個月就需要「護盤」。股價從9月中5445元天價跌到剩3410元，等於一張帳面蒸發203萬元，一台豪華轎車沒了，跌幅高達37%，今（22）日公司宣布實施庫藏股自救兼護盤，自明天（23日）起至12月22日買回自家公司股票300張，目的是轉讓給員工。

漢測經董事會決議明天開始實施庫藏股，日期為10/23~12/22日以上限15億4499萬元，自集中市場買回30萬股（等於300張）股票。買回區間價格為3,700.00~4,300元，以12.9億元作為買回股份之總金額上限，買回本公司普通股，預定買回股數為300,000股。

等於買回300張，作為激勵員工及提昇員工向心力，自買回股份之日起5年內，一次或分次轉讓予員工，以實際買回之平均價格為轉讓價格。

同時漢測今日董事會亦通過「中南部建置製造中心」預算授權案。預計投資廠房新台幣37億元及設備12億元，用於(1)矽光子設備組裝；(2)MEMS探針卡製造產線；(3)回焊設備製造產線；(4)薄膜探針卡產能擴充及(5)雷射清針機製造產線。

此外，公司也通過決議通過「新竹研發中心建置」預算授權案，以新臺幣15億元上限，興建廠辦及裝修。

漢測於9月22日以每股2,250元掛牌上櫃，當時創下今年最高IPO承銷價紀錄，同時凍資市場8656億元的熱門超級紅包，創下抽中一張賺245萬元的紀錄。

葉憶如／財經特派記者組長，主跑金管會、金控壽險、航空等

news.Title: 外資再砍台股逾800億　新台幣貶2分收32.508元
news.Content:
（中央社記者潘姿羽台北2026年10月22日電）市場AI疑慮未消，加上連假前賣壓湧現，外資今天再揮刀大砍台股逾800億元，股匯同步下挫，新台幣兌美元收盤收32.508元，小貶2分，台北及元太外匯市場總成交金額為35.71億美元。

儘管美股21日主要指數全面收紅，費城半導體指數上漲1.97%，台股今天在連假前賣壓提前湧現下，指數開高震盪翻黑，上下震盪達1290點，終場下跌846.34點，收在全天最低點46041.43點。

外資昨天回補台股曇花一現，今天再度轉為賣超，且大砍台股816.56億元。

外匯交易員直言，受到颱風可能導致台灣股匯市休市的預期影響，外資提前撤出資金、降低風險部位，使新台幣再度承受貶值壓力。新台幣兌美元今天以32.47元開盤後，上午震盪偏弱，午後隨著外資加大匯出力道，貶幅迅速擴大，最低觸及32.642元，出口商隨即進場拋匯，提供支撐，加上央行調節，終場貶幅收斂至2分。

外匯交易員指出，美元指數稍有回落，減輕亞幣貶值壓力，不過外資動向仍是牽動新台幣匯率的關鍵。由於市場對AI產業的疑慮尚未消散，一旦指標企業財報不如預期，或其他金融風險升溫，外資不排除再度擴大匯出。

展望後市，外匯交易員認為，若接下來幾個交易日台股逐步回穩，外資也未再大規模匯出，新台幣可望回到32.2至32.6元區間盤整，下一個觀察重點則是美國聯準會10月底利率決策會議釋出的政策訊號。

news.Title: Will Alphabet Stock Soar After Oct. 28? History Offers an Answer That’s Strikingly Clear.
news.Content:
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) has played a significant role in the artificial intelligence (AI) story so far, and that's helped supercharge revenue growth and stock performance. The company develops AI products and services, uses them to improve its own business, and offers them to customers through its Google Cloud unit.

Given high demand for AI capacity, Alphabet has been one of the key players involved in the infrastructure build-out. Alphabet, Amazon , Microsoft , and Meta Platforms together plan to spend more than $700 billion this year on the ramp-up. So, the pace of AI growth depends, to a certain degree, on these leading players.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

With this in mind, investors closely watch these companies as they are well-positioned to benefit from AI growth -- if the AI story continues to unfold as expected. And that brings us to the date of Oct. 28, which could represent a catalyst for Alphabet. Will the stock, which has climbed about 7% this year, soar after that date? History offers an answer that's strikingly clear.

Image source: Getty Images.

The strength of Google Search

Let's start off by considering Alphabet's path so far. The company built its solid billion-dollar revenue stream thanks to something that we all know well: Google Search . It has been steadily No. 1 in search, holding 90% of the market, and advertising across the Google platform has driven revenue over time. Advertisers, knowing we look for various types of information through Google, seek to reach us there about their products and services.

In the second quarter, Google advertising made up 68% of Alphabet's total $119 billion in revenue.

Though this clearly continues to be Alphabet's bread and butter, AI is progressively proving itself to be a powerful revenue driver for the company. Alphabet has developed its own family of large language models, Gemini, and is using this LLM to improve Google Search and the advertising experience -- as a result, advertisers may spend even more here in the future.

At the same time, Alphabet offers Gemini to customers through Google Cloud , and demand for this and other AI capabilities has skyrocketed. In the quarter, Gemini reported an 82% increase in Google Cloud revenue to more than $24 billion, driven by enterprise AI solutions and enterprise AI infrastructure.

Story Continues

Spending heavily to serve demand

But as I mentioned above, Alphabet is spending heavily to serve this demand. Capital expenditures totaled about $44 billion in the quarter to support the AI build-out, with 60% of the infrastructure investment in servers and 40% in data centers and networking.

Investors have been enthusiastic about the growth, but on occasion, they've worried about the depth and speed of the capex increases -- and that's weighed on Alphabet stock from time to time.

Now, let's consider the event coming up on Oct. 28 and what history tells us about stock performance. Alphabet is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings after the market closes. History tells us that, in the two weeks following the past four quarterly reports, Alphabet stock has advanced three times.

Source: Ycharts.

So, recent history has a strikingly clear message for us: Alphabet stock may soar after its upcoming earnings report. It's also important to note that the message regarding AI growth could support this. Demand has been strong throughout the AI boom, and tech companies such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing and ASML Holding , which have already reported earnings, have spoken of ongoing solid demand.

Of course, the one area that may weigh on investors' minds continues to be the levels of capex. Some investors have worried that tech giants are overspending, so this concern could get in the way of a positive stock performance from Alphabet after its report.

What does all of this mean for you as an investor? History says Alphabet may soar after Oct. 28, but the most important thing to focus on is a company's long-term earnings prospects and stock performance potential. And here, there's reason to be optimistic about Alphabet, making it a great stock to own as this AI boom continues to unfold.

news.Title: Zacks Earnings Trends Highlights: Meta, Tesla, Nvidia, Micron and Alphabet
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 22, 2026 – Zacks Director of Research Sheraz Mian says, "We are off to a bit of a mixed start in the Q3 reporting cycle, with the growth pace and the revenue-beat percentage tracking modestly lower relative to the recent past."

Q3 Earnings Season Preview: Revenue Beats Lag, Momentum Holds

Note: The following is an excerpt from this week's Earnings Trends report. You can access the full report that contains detailed historical actual and estimates for the current and following periods, please click here>>>

We get into the heart of the Q3 earnings season this week, with more than 250 companies reporting results, including 73 S&P 500 members. By the end of this week, we will have seen Q3 results from 118 S&P 500 members, or almost a quarter of the index's total membership.

We are off to a bit of a mixed start in the Q3 reporting cycle, with the growth pace and the revenue-beat percentage tracking modestly lower relative to the recent past. That said, the sample of results from the 9% of S&P 500 members that have reported is heavily weighted toward the Finance sector, and these initial mixed trends may shift as we head into the heart of the earnings season in the days ahead.

This week's line-up of earnings releases is comprised of a fairly representative cohort of bellwether operators from a broad mix of sectors and industries, including two of the Mag 7 players, Meta Platforms and Tesla, and several other Tech players like Netflix, Texas Instruments, IBM, Spotify, and others. We will get results from air carriers (United, American, Southwest), railroad operators (CSX, Union Pacific), credit card issuers (American Express, Capital One, Synchrony), and many other blue chips like Procter & Gamble, GM, AT&T, Halliburton, and others.

We will have a definitive sense of how good or otherwise the Q3 earnings season has been by the end of this week.

Looking at overall expectations for the quarter, combining the actual results from the 45 S&P 500 members that have reported already with estimates for the still-to-come companies, Q3 earnings are currently expected to increase by +24.6% from the same period last year on +11.7% higher revenues, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector remains a major growth contributor, but momentum is broad-based, with 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track for positive earnings growth in Q3. Importantly, the revisions trend remains positive and broad-based, highlighting a steadily improving outlook.

Story Continues

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates.

This positive revisions behavior is not a new development; it extends a tailwind that has been building for nearly a year. The positive revisions were at first concentrated in Technology and, more recently, Energy, following Middle East supply disruptions. However, for 2026 Q4 and also what we saw for Q3, the constructive estimate revisions have broadened significantly, rising across 7 of the 16 Zacks sectors—including Aerospace, Construction, Industrials, Finance, and Transportation alongside Tech and Energy.

On the negative side, Q4 estimates remain under pressure for these 8 sectors – Conglomerates, Autos, Basic Materials, Consumer Staples, Consumer Discretionary, Medical, Business Services, and Retail. It is important to note that estimates for full-year 2027 have also been trending higher.

Sector Focus: Broad-Based Strength

Q3 earnings are expected to be above the year-earlier level for 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors, with 5 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit growth. The Conglomerates and Consumer Staples sectors are the only ones expected to have lower earnings in Q3 relative to the same period last year.

The 5 sectors expected to enjoy double-digit earnings growth in Q3 are Aerospace (up +160.5%), Energy (+122.2%), Tech (+43.7%), Basic Materials (+29.5%), Transportation (+9.6%), and Industrial Products (+13.5%).

Q3 earnings growth for the S&P 500 index drops to +20.1% from +24.6% once the Energy sector's contribution is excluded from the index. Excluding the Tech sector, Q3 earnings growth for the rest of the index drops to +14.4%.

For the Finance sector, which has dominated the reporting docket thus far, Q3 earnings are expected to be up +7.3% from the same period last year on +6.3% higher revenues.

With Meta META and Tesla TSLA on deck to report results this week, it is useful to take a look at expectations for the Mag 7 group as a whole. The expectation is that Q3 earnings for the Mag 7 will increase by +20.9% on +22.8% higher revenues.

Excluding the Mag 7 group's contribution, Q3 earnings for the rest of the index would actually modestly improve to +25.8% (from +24.6%).

The Q3 earnings and revenue growth rate drops to +21.1% from +43.7% once the substantial contributions from Nvidia NVDA, Micron MU and Alphabet GOOGL are excluded.

Q3 Earnings Season Scorecard

Through Friday, October 16th, we have seen Q3 results from 45 S&P 500 members, or 9% of the index's total membership. Total earnings for these companies are up +46.3% from the same period last year on +13.9% higher revenues, with 82.2% beating EPS estimates and 62.2% beating revenue estimates.

The very strong earnings and revenue growth pace for this group of 45 S&P 500 members is mostly due to Micron, whose Q3 earnings increased +1075.7% from the year-earlier level. Excluding Micron, Q3 earnings for the remaining 44 index members that have reported would be up +10.4%.

For the Finance sector, we now have Q3 results from 44.3% of the sector's market capitalization in the S&P 500 index. Total earnings for these Finance sector companies are up +10.6% from the same period last year on +8.6% higher revenues, with 80% beating EPS estimates and 50% beating revenue estimates.

Not only are the growth rates tracking below other recent periods, but Finance sector companies also seem to be struggling to beat consensus EPS and revenue estimates.

The Earnings Big Picture

As we noted earlier, estimates for full-year 2027 are experiencing the same positive and broad-based revisions trend that we noted earlier in the context of 2026 Q4.

news.Title: European stocks buckle as French yields cross 5% barrier
news.Content:
Investing.com - European equity bourses buckled under pressure on Thursday, dragged lower by a relentless sell-off in French sovereign debt, while a tech sector retreat overshadowed resilient earnings from consumer defensive heavyweights.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The pan-European STOXX 600 index traded 0.8% lower, surrendering modest gains from the previous session.

France's CAC 40 led continental declines, down over 1%, while Italy's FTSE MIB slipped 0.1%, Greece's Athens General Index decoupled from broader European losses, trading 1% higher despite nationwide civil disruptions..

The benchmark French 10-year yield broke cleanly above 5%, continuing its upward creep to trade at levels last witnessed during the 2002 sovereign market cycle.

Speaking late Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to prevent a repeat of last weekend's violent anti-government riots as fresh protests loom. However, limited political progress toward passing spending cuts for France's 5.4% GDP deficit has left international allocators fearful of an extended structural stalemate.

Social friction expanded across Southern Europe. Thousands of students and teachers marched across Greece on Wednesday demanding higher education funding, echoing demonstrations across the continent.

Meanwhile, in Italy, weekend cost-of-living demonstrations in Milan prompted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni to enact tougher anti-rioting measures. Crucially, Italian BTP yields have avoided the severe penalty hitting French OATs.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Tech stocks slide on Meta capital restructuring and Asian spillover

Though social media giant Meta Platforms posted better-than-expected third-quarter revenue, global trading desks reacted with caution to its announcement of a new nonvoting share class.

The move, intended to provide Meta with flexible equity capital raising to finance its multi-billion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout, reignited anxieties over prospective shareholder dilution and escalating corporate capex.

Tracking broad-based overnight losses across Asian semiconductor supply chains, European tech peers ASML, ASM International, Infineon, and Soitec all fell between 3% and 5%.

Semiconductor assembly equipment provider BE Semiconductor Industries (BESI) fell 3% despite a new share repurchase program and management expecting positive order momentum to carry into the fourth quarter.

Story Continues

Cushioning broader market losses were resilient results from defensive giants.

Food and beverage leader Nestlé reported higher-than-expected organic sales growth for the third quarter, signaling strong pricing power and volume recovery across its core global markets.

Investors also digested quarterly revenue figures from luxury heavyweight Hermès which fell over 7% after reporting a modest 5.5% rise in sales .

news.Title: Wall Street Firm Names Amazon Its Top Pick With More Than 30% Upside. Is the Stock a Buy?
news.Content:
Morgan Stanley recently tapped Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) as its "Top Pick," placing a $350 price target on the stock. Analyst Brian Nowak called Amazon a "Rule of 90" company, meaning its annual revenue growth rate and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization ( EBITDA ) margin could exceed 90%.The analyst said he sees five catalysts for the stock to climb higher.

First, Nowak sees Amazon's cloud computing unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), growing faster than previously expected. He now expects AWS to grow by 47% next year and 42% in 2028, after Nvidia noted that Amazon is expected to buy 2 million of its graphics processing units (GPUs) over the next two years. The analyst also predicted that Amazon will spend a whopping $355 billion in capital expenditures in 2027 and $365 billion in 2028.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

In addition to AWS revenue nearly tripling from $128.7 billion in 2025 to $373.6 billion in 2028, Nowak also expects the segment's operating margins to expand. He sees them coming in at 42% in 2027 and 44% in 2028, helping lead to $16.50 in adjusted EPS in 2028. The analyst also thinks increased visibility into its AI model service, Bedrock, could help drive multiple expansion for the stock.

On the e-commerce side, Morgan Stanley sees Amazon becoming an AI shopping winner and expects it to eventually team up with Meta Platforms and its Muse AI agent, which it has initially been reluctant to do.

Finally, Nowak called out Amazon's use of robotics, noting that for every 10% of units processed through a robot-powered fulfillment center, Amazon can save between $2 billion and $4 billion a year. He said that Amazon's efficiency is expanding quicker than he initially modeled.

Is Amazon stock a buy?

Amazon is one of my favorite stocks right now and one I own. The company should continue to see AWS growth accelerate as its large AI infrastructure investments begin to kick in. It has large commitments from both Anthropic and OpenAI, with its backlog growing into the triple digits in Q2, ending the quarter at $496 billion. The company is getting a nice return on its chip and networking investments with a payback of less than three years, while locking in contracts for five years or more.

I think Amazon's AWS economics could improve even further if it can direct more of this business toward its own Trainum chips. In April, CEO Andy Jassy said its chip business has a revenue run rate of around $20 billion and is closer to $50 billion when including internal use. Meanwhile, rival Alphabet has said it is seeing a one-year payback on its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), so the opportunity is certainly there.

Story Continues

Regardless, Amazon has the best scale in the cloud computing space, and Jassy has said this could eventually become a $1 trillion revenue business.

I also feel that Amazon's e-commerce operations are underappreciated. The business continues to see strong sales growth despite an uneven consumer environment. At the same time, it has some attractive new growth initiatives, including expanding its logistics network to offer high-margin, less-than-truckload shipping. Meanwhile, the company has quietly become one of the largest digital advertisers on the planet, and it continues to see strong growth in this high-gross margin business.

Perhaps the most underestimated part of the Amazon story, though, is its leadership in robotics. The company is the largest manufacturer and user of robots in the world, with a fleet of over 1 million robots, all controlled by its DeepFleet AI model. This is creating significant operational efficiencies in its e-commerce operations, leading to profit growth that far exceeds revenue growth.

With the stock trading at a forward P/E of 25 times 2027 analyst estimates, Amazon trades at a huge discount to brick-and-mortar retailers like Walmart and Costco , making it a no-brainer buy in my view.

news.Title: Asian stocks sink to 3-month low on tech angst, Gulf tensions
news.Content:
By Jiaxing Li

HONG KONG, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Asian stocks retreated on Thursday as technology shares led a broad selloff, with Wall Street earnings failing to quell worries over soaring AI investment costs, while escalating Gulf ‌tensions boosted oil and weighed on risk sentiment.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slumped 1.8% to ‌the lowest level in nearly three months and was on track for a fourth straight week of decline.

Japan's Nikkei gave up earlier gains to trade ​2% lower, Korean shares tumbled more than 4%, while China's blue-chip CSI300 fell 2%, pushing it to the brink of a technical bear market. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index lost more than 3%.

Tech leaders in the region were among the biggest losers, with Japan's Tokyo Electron down more than 6%. Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung were down 5.7% and 4.2%, respectively, while Alibaba tumbled 6.5% in ‌Hong Kong.

In early European trading, the pan-region ⁠Euro Stoxx 50 futures declined 0.9%. U.S. stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis, dropped 0.8%.

Overnight, the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a slightly higher close. Space X posted its first profit as ⁠a public company and Meta reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, easing fears over the payoff from massive AI spending.

The optimism quickly evaporated in Asia, however, as investors refocused on AI costs, with Meta's plan to issue non-voting Class C stock reviving concerns over mounting ​capital ​commitments.

"There's a lot of noise out there at the moment and ​investors are still digesting this morning's results," said Kyle ‌Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

"Also, we're really only at the start of the meaty part of earnings season, which is coming at the same time that investors are tackling the uncertainty from an upcoming Fed decision, geopolitical risks, and US mid-terms."

Those geopolitical concerns were reflected in oil markets. Brent crude rose more than 2% to $111.03 a barrel, near a five-month high, after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised the risk of wider conflict and supply disruptions in the Middle East.

A flight ‌to safety pushed benchmark U.S. Treasury yields lower, with the 10-year yield ​falling nearly 6 basis points to 5.0857% and the 30-year yield touching ​a one-week low of 5.3850%.

French government bonds also remained ​under pressure after the 10-year yield climbed above 5%, as investors looked for signs the government ‌can contain social unrest and bring spending under control.

Story Continues

In ​currencies, the dollar index, which tracks ​the greenback against a basket of currencies of other major trading partners, dipped to 101.57. The euro was little changed at $1.1242.

The yen ticked up to 157.55 after Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino signalled his readiness ​to raise borrowing costs. The Korean won ‌was muted at 1324, after the Bank of Korea left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.00% on ​Thursday.

Gold eased to $4,067.5 per ounce. [GOL/]

Bitcoin fell 2.2% to $82,771.05, while ether was also 2.2% lower at $2,436.3.

(Reporting by Jiaxing Li ​in Hong Kong; Editing by Kate Mayberry and Shri Navaratnam)

news.AI_Summary:

• 此次合作結合聯電的深溝槽電容(DTC)製程技術與愛普的矽電容設計及系統整合技術。
• 雙方合作旨在應對下一代資料中心對電源效率日益增長的需求，特別是AI運算工作負載的快速成長。
• 聯電的DTC技術能將高密度電容配置於更靠近運算晶片的位置，以提供更穩定的供電效果。
• 合作的下一階段將進行封裝基板中電容的系統級效能與可靠度測試，並探討擴展至其他產品線。

news.Title: Meta Delivers Another Blowout Earnings Report. Here's What Investors Need To Know
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) came into its third-quarter earnings report, riding a bullish wave after its release of Muse, its AI personal agent that has topped the app download charts.

The launch of Muse and its frontier model, Muse Wonder, has helped dispel the notion that Meta is just an advertising business and alleviates one of the biggest risks facing the company, as nearly all of its revenue comes from advertising.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The third-quarter report shows the Facebook parent's momentum continuing to build, and it bodes well for its future. Here's what investors need to know about the latest report.

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Meta is executing across the board

It's hard to find a flaw in Meta's latest quarter. Revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, which topped expectations at $63.4 billion. On the bottom line, the company reported earnings per share of $3.83 due to the impact of its $18.59 billion settlement over litigation around teen health and social media and a $9.89 billion charge it took as part of that. Adjusted for that, it would have finished with $22.9 billion in operating income and $7.40 in earnings per share.

Meta's ad business continued to deliver strong results with ad impressions up 10% and the average price per ad up by 14%, showing the company is delivering results for advertisers.

The company also delivered those results with 15% fewer employees, as it cut its headcount by roughly 10,000 in layoffs earlier this year, freeing up more cash to invest in AI.

The company even sees a narrower loss in its AI-focused reality labs division, calling for a loss of $18 billion-$19 billion, which is still enormous, but is at least trending in the right direction. It forecast losses in that segment to narrow to around $15 billion next year, a clear positive sign.

2. Meta sounds more bullish than ever on the future

Meta's ad business is delivering blockbuster results, but the company also seems to have a swagger from its momentum in AI and the Muse launch that it didn't previously have.

Its CFO outlook commentary said, "Our AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement, better recommendations, and more efficient monetization." The company also called for strong overall revenue growth to continue through 2027.

Story Continues

CEO Mark Zuckerberg also shared that more than 10 million people in North America had set up Muse personal agents, and the company expects to eventually have billions of Muse users. Zuckerberg essentially said that he thought Muse could double the company's revenue over time, saying he expected Muse to reach a higher average revenue per user than it earns from advertising in the U.S. He also noted shopping has been the most popular use case, which is clearly monetizable for a company that has the world's second-biggest advertising business, and has half of the world on its platforms.

3. Meta is issuing a stock split

For the first time since its 20212 IPO, Meta is splitting its stock. The company is issuing one share of a new Class C non-voting stock for each share of Class A and Class B supervoting shares.

Effectively, the stock dividend will act as a 2-for-1 split, and the company expects the share price to reflect that once the stock dividend is executed on Jan. 19, 2027.

Management argued that creating a new class of non-voting shares would give it more flexibility in raising cash and in employee compensation. Additionally, the board of directors sees it as a way to continue maximizing long-term shareholder value and to keep Mark Zuckerberg at the helm of Meta.

Though stock splits don't change the fundamentals of a stock, investors still like them, and this one seems deserved with Meta stock trading around $700/share.

Overall, with strong growth in the core business and the emergence of AI, Meta looks well-positioned for further growth, especially as the stock trades at a discount to the S&P 500.
