news.Title: Meta sued in Australian class action over alleged social media harm to children
news.Content:
SYDNEY, Oct 22 (Reuters) - A class-action lawsuit has been filed in an Australian court against Meta ‌Platforms' Facebook and Instagram that alleges the social ‌media platforms exposed children to harmful content and kept them addicted ​through algorithms.

The lawsuit, filed in the Federal Court, Australia's second-highest, by law firm MinterEllison this month could be the first in Australia to blame social media for harming ‌its users, particularly children ⁠and teenagers.

• The class-action suit has been filed on behalf of eight plaintiffs, who ⁠allege they were harmed by Meta while they were under the age of 18, and are seeking compensation.

• "We are ​aware of ​this claim and we ​will defend ourselves vigorously," ‌a Meta spokesperson said by email.

• In a suppression order on Monday, the court prohibited the reporting of any information which could reveal the identity of the applicants, and the statement of claim.

• The lawsuit comes amid ‌rising tensions between Australia and ​Big Tech after a world-first ban ​on social media ​for children under 16, and newly proposed ‌rules that could let users ​switch off algorithm-driven ​content on their feeds.

• Meta in August agreed to pay $18 billion to settle with nearly all US ​states to ‌resolve claims it designed social media to addict ​children.

(Reporting by Renju Jose in Sydney; Editing by ​Christopher Cushing and Muralikumar Anantharaman)

news.Title: Lam Research: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its September 2026 quarterly earnings call, held on Oct. 21, 2026, Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) reported record quarterly revenue and profitability. Artificial intelligence workloads drive higher semiconductor complexity and boost demand for wafer fab equipment, which is the capital machinery used to manufacture chips. This structural shift expands the addressable market and creates long-term opportunities across memory and logic markets. Three key takeaways from the call stand out for long-term investors.

1. Advanced Dry Resist Technology Elevates Long-Term Revenue Projections

Lam Research is seeing increased adoption of its Aether dry resist technology, an advanced tool used for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography patterning in chip manufacturing. Customer demand for high bandwidth memory and logic chips led management to raise its cumulative revenue forecast for the product line by $1 billion.

As a result, we now expect cumulative Aether-related revenue to reach approximately $2.5 billion by the end of the decade, roughly $1 billion above our prior expectations.

-- Tim Archer, President and Chief Executive Officer

2. Maintenance and Service Division Growth Doubles Long-Term Targets

The Customer Support Business Group (CSBG), which provides maintenance, spare parts, and equipment upgrades for installed tools, is expanding rapidly as chipmakers run factories at high utilization rates. Full-year division growth is projected to reach more than twice its long-term target, supported by performance-based contracts and automation software.

Finally, turning to CSBG, we are set to exit calendar year 2026 with solid momentum, with annual revenue expected to grow more than 30% year-over-year.

3. AI Storage Architecture Shift Drives Additional NAND Wafer Capacity

Artificial intelligence models are forcing a redesign of flash memory storage tiers and creating demand for single-level cell (SLC) NAND, a low-latency memory format. Because SLC stores fewer bits per cell, chipmakers require significantly more wafer manufacturing capacity to deliver equivalent storage volume.

Said differently, for each percentage point mix shift of NAND bits to SLC class devices, approximately 2% more installed wafer capacity will be needed to support the same bit demand.

Looking Ahead

Artificial intelligence adoption is accelerating across enterprise and consumer markets and driving unprecedented demand for semiconductor manufacturing tools.

Story Continues

Underpinning our outlook for WFE growth is the continued rapid adoption of AI by enterprises and consumers.

A massive installed base and leadership in deposition and etch steps position the business to capture rising equipment intensity as chip designs shift to 3D scaling. Management is focused on resolving near-term supply chain constraints while expanding global manufacturing capacity to support long-term industry growth.

Our technology leadership, growing installed base, and strategic investments in product innovation and manufacturing capacity position Lam to capitalize on these inflections and drive sustained outperformance.

news.Title: Asian markets dip as investors weigh tech earnings, Gulf tensions
news.Content:
By Jiaxing Li

HONG KONG, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Asian stocks struggled to stay above water in early trade on Thursday, as tech earnings optimism provided only fleeting support amid lingering ‌concerns over AI and uncertainty in the Gulf.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan ‌was down 0.2%, on track for a fourth straight week of decline. Japan's Nikkei stock index gave up earlier gains to trade ​0.4% lower, while Korean shares were down more than 1%.

US stock futures, the S&P 500 e-minis, were down 0.4% at 7,765.8. Overnight, the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street to a higher close as better-than-expected earnings reports from market heavyweights helped ease some concerns over the sustainability and profitability of massive AI build-outs.

Space X posted ‌its first profit as a public ⁠company, Meta reported third-quarter revenue that beat expectations, while AI server maker Super Micro forecast quarterly revenue and profit margin that both topped estimates.

However, Meta's plan to issue ⁠non-voting Class C common stock drew renewed scrutiny on AI spending.

"There's a lot of noise out there at the moment and investors are still digesting this morning's results," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

"Also, ​we're really ​only at the start of the meaty part of ​earnings season, which is coming at the ‌same time that investors are tackling the uncertainty from an upcoming Fed decision, geopolitical risks, and US mid-terms."

In a sign of subdued risk sentiment, the yield on benchmark 10-year Treasury notes was down 4.2 basis points at 5.1065%, while the yield on 30-year notes was at a one-week low of 5.3968%.

Meanwhile, Brent crude rose 1.1% to $110.03 a barrel, near a five-month high. The US ordered diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid ‌Houthi strikes, while the New York Times reported the ​US and Israeli militaries had developed specific plans for renewed attacks ​on Iran after the US midterm elections, ​which take place on November 3.

In currencies, the dollar index, which tracks the ‌greenback against a basket of currencies of other ​major trading partners, dipped to ​102.2. The euro was little changed at $1.1231.

The yen was also flat at 158.125, after Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino signalled his readiness to raise borrowing costs. The Korean won ​was muted at 1325.9, after the ‌Bank of Korea left its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 3.00% on Thursday.

Gold was slightly ​lower at $4115.5 per ounce. [GOL/]

Bitcoin was down 0.4% at $84,284.05, while ether was 0.6% lower at $2,476.34.

(Reporting by ​Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong; Editing by Kate Mayberry)

news.Title: Meta: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
news.Content:
On its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 21, 2026, Meta (NASDAQ:META) announced the launch of its Muse personal agent, an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant designed for personal superintelligence. Rapid adoption of new AI tools and ad system upgrades is expanding user engagement and establishing new monetization paths. Three things management said stand out.

1. Muse Reaches 10 Million Users as Commerce Drives Adoption

Meta introduced its Muse personal agent, an AI assistant that executes tasks for users, and recorded rapid adoption driven by unexpected shopping volume. Building a large consumer network enables the company to generate transaction fees from business partners over time.

In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse personal agents, Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number 1 in the App Store almost every day.

-- Mark Elliot Zuckerberg, Chief Executive Officer

2. Reality Labs Narrowing Losses to $15 Billion as Focus Shifts

Management is pacing investments in virtual reality (VR) hardware to prioritize software and personal agent models. Reducing operating losses in this segment's profit and loss (P&L) statement frees up capital to fund high-return AI infrastructure.

So with these factors combined, we expect that the P&L of Reality Labs to improve from here with operating loss coming down to approximately $15 billion next year and trending toward profitability from there.

3. First-Party AI Models Cut Content Processing Costs by Over 80%

Transitioning content processing to internal Muse models improves recommendation accuracy across social feeds while drastically lowering compute expenses. Lower unit costs strengthen profit margins as engagement scales across apps.

In offline evaluations, these models are outperforming our prior production models and are reducing per unit content processing costs by more than 80% across Instagram threads, Facebook, and ads.

-- Susan J. Li, Chief Financial Officer

Looking Ahead

Engagement and ad efficiency are accelerating across Meta's social platforms. Infrastructure scale and global distribution give the business room to fund AI tools while tracking compute efficiency.

The benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.

Story Continues

Deploying personal agents to billions of users positions the company for long-term network monetization.

If compute efficiency continues improving quickly for another few years, which we think is highly likely, then Muse will be highly profitable over the years.

news.Title: Amazon vs. Target: Where Should Long-Term Investors Put Their Money?
news.Content:
Deciding between e-commerce dominance and brick-and-mortar stability requires a close look at the numbers. In this article, we'll take a look at Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Target (NYSE:TGT) to see which stock is a better buy.

Amazon dominates digital commerce and cloud infrastructure, while Target focuses on an omnichannel approach with roughly 2,000 stores across the United States. While both compete for consumer dollars, their business models and growth trajectories differ significantly. This comparison analyzes their financials and risks to help you navigate these retail leaders.

The case for Amazon.com

Amazon operates a massive digital marketplace and is a prominent name among retail stocks through its global online store and Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud computing division. The company serves a diverse range of customers, including individual shoppers, third-party vendors, and enterprise technology teams. It continues to leverage its proprietary logistics network and high-margin advertising services to maintain its leadership in the global economy.

According to its latest annual report filed for FY 2025, revenue reached $716.9 billion, representing growth of nearly 12.4% compared to the previous year. This growth was accompanied by net income of $77.7 billion, which reflects a net margin of close to 10.8%.

Amazon has total cash of $122.9 billion against total debt of $251.6 billion. Its debt-to-equity ratio is 45.6%, and its operating cash flow is $161.4 billion.

The case for Target

Target is a general merchandise retailer that uses its physical stores as fulfillment hubs for its digital sales. The company has established strong commercial ties with partners like Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), CVS , Disney , Levi's , and Starbucks (NASDAQ:SBUX) to drive guest traffic. It also operates the Target Plus marketplace and the Shipt delivery service while navigating the conclusion of its partnership with Ulta Beauty .

Based on its latest annual report filed for FY 2025, revenue reached $104.8 billion, which was a decrease of nearly 1.7% from the prior year. The company reported net income of $3.7 billion for the period, resulting in a net margin of 3.5%.

Target's total cash is $5.4 billion against total debt of $19.2 billion. Its debt-to-equity ratio is 107.5%, while its operating cash flow is $8.7 billion.

Risk profile comparison

Amazon faces intense competition across multiple industries, including e-commerce and cloud services, from well-funded competitors with significant resources. Its international operations expose the business to various geopolitical and regulatory risks, such as trade disputes and local licensing requirements. The complexity of its global fulfillment network and a high reliance on third-party suppliers and shipping companies create additional operational challenges for the business.

Story Continues

Target is susceptible to shifts in consumer spending patterns and macroeconomic instability within the U.S. economy, including inflationary pressures. The company manages significant supply chain risks and inventory shrink, which refers to the loss of products due to theft or administrative errors. Additionally, it faces ongoing legal risks, including product liability claims.

Valuation comparison

The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which uses future earnings estimates, suggests Target is the more affordable option, and its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio also shows it trading at a lower multiple of sales.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Between the two, I wouldn't hesitate to own Amazon. That's because if I were looking more in the traditional retail space, I would pick Walmart over Target, as I feel it's done a better job of integrating technology into its business and has an undervalued advertising arm it's building. And between Target and Amazon, the choice gets even easier for me.

While Amazon does have a retail platform, what's more interesting is its connection to artificial intelligence (AI), a market that will be immensely profitable. In 2026, the worldwide AI market is valued at $707 billion, but that's expected to jump to $1.9 trillion by 2032.

According to Statista, as of Q1 2026, Amazon is the global leader in cloud infrastructure via AWS, with 28% market share. The next-closest company is Microsoft , with a 21% market share. Amazon is also making its own chips, which helps it become more vertically integrated, achieve higher margins, and not rely on third-party suppliers. It's also integrating AI into its Alexa devices and has a stake in the start-up Anthropic, so Amazon has many ways to profit from AI. Between Target and Amazon, there's just a lot more money that Amazon can haul in, making it a stock I'd rather own for the long haul.

news.Title: U.S. stock futures drop as investors weigh Tesla, Meta earnings
news.Content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock futures fell sharply in Asian trading on Thursday as Tesla shares slid despite upbeat quarterly results, as uncertainty over a potential merger with SpaceX and concerns about the cost of artificial intelligence investment weighed on sentiment.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

S&P 500 Futures fell 0.9% to 7,732.75 points, while Nasdaq 100 Futures slid 1.6% to 29,517.25 points by 02:55 ET (06:55 GMT). Dow Jones Futures slipped 0.5% to 52,796.0 points.

The reports from the two companies, released after the regular market close, marked a key test for investor appetite for large-cap technology stocks as Wall Street moved deeper into the third-quarter earnings season.

Tesla shares fell nearly 5% in extended trading despite beating analysts' expectations for quarterly earnings and revenue.

Investors were concerned by the company's decision to cut its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to about $20 billion from an earlier projection of more than $25 billion.

SpaceX shares also fell more than 2% in extended trading. The decline came amid uncertainty over a possible combination of Tesla and SpaceX, both led by Elon Musk.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Musk said both firms had formed a special committee to explore a potential merger with Tesla, but no agreement had been reached on transaction terms, and there was no guarantee a deal would proceed.

The uncertainty followed a strong rally in SpaceX shares on Thursday after the rocket and satellite company reported robust quarterly results and flagged a potential merger with Tesla.

Meanwhile, Meta shares rose nearly 1% in post-market trading after reporting stronger-than-expected revenue and a positive outlook for the current quarter.

Meta reported earnings of $3.83 per share, ahead of the $3.57 expected by analysts, while revenue climbed 26% from a year earlier to $64.6 billion, exceeding estimates of $63.34 billion. Its results were supported by advertising growth and increased engagement across its platforms, although a large legal settlement added to quarterly costs.

In Wednesday's regular session, U.S. equities had drawn support from strong results from SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI).

The NASDAQ Composite rose 1.1% on Wednesday, while the S&P 500 gained 0.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended 0.7% higher.

Story Continues

Investors were also monitoring elevated oil prices and interest-rate risks. Brent crude traded above $110 a barrel in Asian trading Thursday amid geopolitical uncertainty, while U.S. inflation pressures have raised concerns about the Federal Reserve's policy outlook ahead of its meeting next week.

Attention now turns to Thursday's earnings from companies including Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG), Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC), Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT), and Honeywell (NASDAQ:HON).
