news.Title: Lam Research Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Lam Research Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record September-quarter results: Lam Research reported $8.22 billion in revenue, up 22% sequentially and 54% year over year, with record 52.4% gross margin, 40.2% operating margin and $2.20 in non-GAAP EPS.

Strong AI- and memory-driven outlook: Lam forecast December-quarter revenue of $8.6 billion and expects 2027 wafer-fabrication equipment spending to exceed $200 billion, led by DRAM, leading-edge foundry logic and NAND demand.

Growth remains constrained by capacity and supply: Near-term component shortages and clean-room limitations could delay shipments, while China revenue is expected to decline significantly in the December quarter. Lam generated record $3.24 billion in free cash flow and returned approximately 41% of it through buybacks and dividends.

From High Dividend Growth to High Yield, These 3 Stocks Just Boosted Dividend Payouts

Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) reported record revenue, profitability and earnings per share for its September 2026 quarter, as demand tied to artificial intelligence, advanced semiconductor manufacturing and packaging continued to support spending on deposition and etch equipment.

Revenue for the September quarter totaled $8.22 billion, up 22% sequentially and 54% from the same period in 2025, Chief Financial Officer Doug Bettinger said. The company recorded a gross margin of 52.4%, an operating margin of 40.2% and diluted non-GAAP earnings per share of $2.20, all records. Operating margin exceeded 40% for the first time, according to the company.

→ The AI Sell-Off Continues—These 3 Stocks Keep Raising Guidance Anyway

Analysts Just Raised Price Targets On These 3 Semiconductor Equipment Stocks

"In the September quarter, Lam again delivered record revenue and profitability," President and Chief Executive Officer Tim Archer said. He said AI-driven semiconductor demand and rising device complexity were increasing the intensity of deposition and etch processes across memory, logic and advanced-packaging applications.

December Outlook and WFE Forecast

For the December 2026 quarter, Lam forecast revenue of $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million. The company expects gross margin of 52.5%, plus or minus one percentage point; operating margin of 40.5%, plus or minus one percentage point; and earnings per share of $2.33, plus or minus $0.15.

→ Tesla's Roadster Reveal Hints at 2 Much Bigger Moves

Why Lam Research Still Looks Like a Buy After a 300% Rally

Bettinger said the December revenue outlook would have been "a little bit higher" without near-term supply-chain constraints. He did not quantify the impact, but said shipments delayed from the December period because of timing would move into the March quarter.

Story Continues

Lam expects calendar-year 2026 wafer-fabrication equipment, or WFE, spending to be in the mid-$150 billion range. Its preliminary forecast for 2027 calls for more than $200 billion in WFE spending, with percentage growth led by DRAM, followed by leading-edge foundry logic and NAND.

→ Luxury's Middle Market Is Cracking—These 3 Stocks Could Win

Archer said clean-room availability and supply constraints for certain components may limit the industry's ability to fully meet demand in 2027. The company is working with suppliers to expand capacity, he said, and expects to improve the supply situation shortly. Bettinger added that Lam expects 10 new Tier 1 fabs to come online during 2027.

At the midpoint of its December-quarter outlook, Lam expects calendar-year 2026 systems revenue to grow more than 40% year over year. Archer said the company expects 2026 to be its third consecutive year of WFE outperformance, supported by growth in Lam's served available market and product share gains.

Memory and Foundry Demand Drive Growth

Memory represented 46% of September-quarter systems revenue, unchanged from the prior quarter, while foundry accounted for 46%, up from 44%. Logic and other applications represented 8% of systems revenue.

Memory systems revenue reached a record dollar level and increased 120% from a year earlier. NAND accounted for 26% of systems revenue, compared with 23% in the June quarter, as customers continued converting to 256-layer and higher-class devices. NAND revenue rose about 40% sequentially, and Lam said it is seeing initial spending on 384-layer-class devices.

DRAM revenue also reached a record, with spending focused on technology additions and upgrades at the 1α, 1β and 1γ nodes for DDR5, LPDDR5 and high-bandwidth memory. Archer said Lam expects etch and deposition intensity to increase as DRAM architectures become more three-dimensional.

The company also discussed potential new NAND demand related to AI storage tiers. Archer said QLC NAND supports cost-effective data storage, TLC is used for higher-bandwidth context-memory and key-value-cache workloads, and SLC-class NAND is emerging for low-latency access in agentic AI applications.

Lam said shifting NAND production from TLC to SLC-class devices reduces bits per device by roughly three times. For every one-percentage-point shift of NAND bits toward SLC-class devices, about 2% more installed wafer capacity would be needed to support the same bit demand, according to the company.

Technology Investments and Advanced Packaging

Archer said foundry logic and DRAM accounted for about 80% of Lam's systems-revenue growth year to date. The company highlighted demand for its Akara etch, conductor etch and Aether dry-resist products in advanced patterning applications.

Lam said its Aether dry-resist solution has demonstrated sub-10-nanometer resolution with High-NA EUV and can reduce exposure dose by 10%. Aether products are ramping in high-volume HBM manufacturing using Low-NA EUV, Archer said. Lam now expects cumulative Aether-related revenue to reach about $2.5 billion by the end of the decade, approximately $1 billion above its previous expectation.

The company also cited opportunities in backside power delivery, where it has secured tool-of-record wins for four products at a leading customer. In advanced packaging, Lam said its Syndion etch product won four new positions across multiple customers for advanced logic and HBM through-silicon-via applications.

Lam expects advanced-packaging revenue to grow about 70% during calendar 2026. Archer said panel-level packaging is an emerging growth opportunity, with Lam having shipped panel plating systems to more than 20 customers globally. The company expects to achieve panel-level packaging market share exceeding its position in current wafer-level packaging.

Regional Mix, Services and Capital Returns

China represented 35% of September-quarter revenue, up from 26% in the June quarter, due to investments from domestic and multinational customers. Bettinger said China's contribution is expected to be significantly lower in the December quarter, primarily due to lower domestic-customer revenue, while multinational demand in the region should remain reasonably strong.

Korea accounted for 20% of revenue and Taiwan contributed 18%. Lam's Customer Support Business Group generated nearly $2.5 billion in revenue, its fourth consecutive quarterly record and a 40% increase from a year earlier. The company expects full-year 2026 CSBG revenue growth of more than 30%, followed by growth of more than 15% in 2027.

Lam generated record free cash flow of $3.24 billion in the September quarter. It repurchased about $1 billion of shares and paid $325 million in dividends, returning roughly 41% of quarterly free cash flow to shareholders. The company ended the quarter with $7.5 billion in cash and short-term investments and $3 billion remaining under its authorized share-repurchase program.

About Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX)

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) is a semiconductor equipment company that develops and manufactures systems used to fabricate integrated circuits. Its technologies support key stages of wafer processing, helping semiconductor manufacturers create the increasingly complex structures found in memory, logic and other types of chips.

The company's product portfolio includes etch systems, which selectively remove materials from wafers; deposition systems, which apply thin films; and cleaning solutions used to remove contaminants and residue during manufacturing.

news.Title: Cathie Wood Trimmed Ark's Alphabet Stake Even as Google Search Revenue Grew, While Ark Piled Into Rocket Lab Even After Its Neutron Launch Delay. Is Ark Betting Against the Wrong AI Winner?
news.Content:
On Sept. 22, Cathie Wood's Ark Invest bought roughly $25.1 million of Rocket Lab (NASDAQ: RKLB) shares, while selling $5.8 million of Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL) stock. However, Rocket Lab has since encountered another setback in its growth plans. On Oct. 14 , the company announced that its Neutron rocket's first launch had been delayed until 2027. Despite this setback, Ark Invest purchased another $9.3 million of Rocket Lab shares on Oct. 15.

Ark's investment decisions highlight the trade-off between Alphabet's established profitability and Rocket Lab's potentially higher, but less certain, long-term growth.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Alphabet's AI investments are showing results

Alphabet's search advertising revenue growth was not driven solely by higher ad prices. The company's paid clicks rose 13% year over year, while average cost per click increased 3% year over year in the second quarter. Google Cloud revenue also jumped 82% year over year to $24.8 billion, and operating income more than tripled to $8.8 billion in the second quarter. These numbers show stronger advertising monetization and profitable cloud growth, although Alphabet doesn't separately disclose AI profits.

Alphabet's upcoming third-quarter results on Oct. 28 could provide further clarity on its AI investments. J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth expects Google Cloud revenue to double year over year, partly driven by solid demand for Google's custom AI chips. However, Alphabet has also guided for $195 billion to $205 billion in capital expenditures for 2026. With such massive spending, sustaining revenue growth while protecting profit margins will be increasingly important.

Why Ark remains interested in Rocket Lab

Ark's investment thesis relies on a possible shortage of launch capacity in the U.S. in the coming years. The investment firm expects Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX), better known as SpaceX, could retire its existing Falcon 9 rocket launch system by the end of 2030, while increasingly using its next-generation Starship rocket to support orbital AI data centers. This could create opportunities for competing launch providers, including Rocket Lab, as government agencies, communications providers, and other commercial customers seek alternatives to SpaceX.

Story Continues

Rocket Lab already has evidence of commercial demand. The company has entered a multiyear launch deal with Synspective for 20 launch missions using its operational Electron rockets. The company also exited the second quarter (ending June 30, 2026) with a backlog of $2.36 billion. Rocket Lab's space systems segment, which manufactures satellites, spacecraft components, and related equipment, accounted for nearly 81% of the second-quarter revenue. Hence, Rocket Lab's existing business is not entirely dependent on Neutron's success.

However, realizing Ark's expected launch-market opportunity depends on Neutron becoming commercially successful. Rocket Lab has secured a launch contract with Kepler Communications for satellites supporting on-orbit computing, but the mission is scheduled no earlier than 2028. Hence, even a successful first Neutron launch in 2027 cannot guarantee regular, profitable operations.

Rocket Lab has also raised $1.94 billion by issuing 29.3 million shares to help fund its planned acquisition of Iridium Communications . While the deal could add recurring revenue, the share issuance also dilutes existing shareholders.

Rocket Lab is currently trading at over 39 times trailing-12-month sales, leaving very little room for execution missteps. Alphabet is trading at just close to 9.3 times sales, despite established profitability and more visible AI monetization. Hence, Alphabet currently appears to offer the stronger risk-adjusted AI investment opportunity, although Rocket Lab could deliver greater returns if its ambitious expansion succeeds.

The company forecast Q4 revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion and announced an effective two-for-one stock split expected to begin trading in late January 2027.

Synchrony Aces The Quarter As Credit Fears Fade

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) reported third-quarter 2026 revenue growth of 26% as advertising demand, engagement gains and AI-driven improvements across its apps supported results, while expenses rose sharply due to a nearly $10 billion legal charge and continued infrastructure investment.

Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg said Meta's family of apps reached 3.64 billion daily users during the quarter. Facebook and Instagram posted all-time highs in engagement, driven largely by video, while Threads surpassed X in monthly active users, according to Zuckerberg. WhatsApp also reached all-time highs in messaging activity.

→ The AI Sell-Off Continues—These 3 Stocks Keep Raising Guidance Anyway

The AI Buildout Is Only 15% Complete—Here Is Where the Next Dollar Actually Goes

The company reported total revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% from a year earlier on both a reported and constant-currency basis. Family of Apps revenue was $64.2 billion, including $63.1 billion in advertising revenue, which also rose 26%.

Total expenses increased 68% to $51.6 billion, including a $9.9 billion charge related to Meta's August 2026 agreement with multiple state attorneys general. GAAP operating income fell 37% to $13 billion, while the operating margin was 20%. Excluding the legal charge, Chief Financial Officer Susan Li said operating income would have risen 11% year over year.

→ Tesla's Roadster Reveal Hints at 2 Much Bigger Moves

Meta Platforms' AI Comeback Faces an Earnings Test—And a $10 Billion Charge

Net income was $9.9 billion, or $3.83 per share. Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, reached $34.9 billion as Meta invested in servers, data centers and network infrastructure. Free cash flow was negative $2.1 billion for the quarter.

Story Continues

Advertising and engagement trends

Meta said ad impressions delivered across its services increased 10% year over year, while the global average price per ad rose 14%. Li attributed pricing gains to better ad performance and improved macroeconomic conditions compared with the prior-year period, partially offset by impression growth in lower-monetizing regions and surfaces.

→ Luxury's Middle Market Is Cracking—These 3 Stocks Could Win

Meta continued to emphasize the role of AI in improving content recommendations and ad performance. On Instagram, global time spent per user reached an all-time high and rose by double digits year over year, with growth in both Reels and Feed. Facebook Reels time spent also reached all-time highs globally and in the U.S.

Li said Instagram Reels relevance initiatives introduced during the quarter lifted Reels time spent by more than 4%. On Facebook, a new generative retrieval architecture was deployed to about one-quarter of unconnected Feed views and half of Reels views, contributing a 1% increase in Reels watch time.

In advertising, Meta said its Meta Generative Recommender system drove a nearly 2% increase in conversions across targeted Facebook Feed segments. The company also expanded its GEM ad-ranking model, which increased conversions by 1.7% for off-site conversion campaigns and 9.6% for app-ad conversion campaigns, according to Li.

Meta's AI Business Assistant has also become a more active tool for advertisers. The company estimated that advertisers adopting its recommendations generated nearly 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion and increased advertising spending by 9% relative to similar non-adopters.

Nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one of Meta's generative AI advertising tools in the third quarter. Meanwhile, partnership ads surpassed a $15 billion annual revenue run rate after growing more than 97% year over year, Li said.

Muse agent expansion and monetization plans

Zuckerberg focused much of the call on Muse, Meta's personal AI agent. He said more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up Muse agents in roughly six weeks. About 25% of people who have set up Muse use it on a given day, according to Zuckerberg.

Shopping has been the most common Muse use case, with more than one-quarter of active users engaging in shopping and an average purchase size above $200. Zuckerberg later clarified that the commerce data includes travel purchases. Personal productivity and connections to services such as email and calendars were also among the leading use cases.

Meta has not yet launched Muse globally, with Zuckerberg citing the service's compute intensity, the need for regional product optimization and the company's desire to improve efficiency before broader expansion. Meta expects to improve Muse compute-cost efficiency by more than tenfold over the next year through measures including more efficient models, inference optimization and use of off-peak capacity.

The company expects Muse to remain free for most users, with revenue eventually generated through commerce fees paid by businesses, paid subscriptions for advanced models or additional token usage, and subscriptions for business features and workplace uses. Zuckerberg said the company plans to build enough capacity to serve more than 1 billion people over the next several years.

Meta is also developing enterprise offerings around its models, including an API, Muse Code and business agents. Li said Meta believes AI could create a diversified recurring revenue stream through subscriptions, usage-based APIs, messaging and other revenue sources, though the opportunity is expected to develop over multiple years.

Reality Labs, outlook and capital structure

Reality Labs revenue declined 6% to $443 million, as lower Quest headset sales were partially offset by growth in AI glasses revenue. Zuckerberg said Muse will begin coming to Meta Glasses next month and that the company expects subscriptions tied to glasses to increase.

Meta expects Reality Labs operating losses to decline to about $15 billion next year, following expected 2026 losses of $18 billion to $19 billion. Zuckerberg said the company is pacing virtual-reality investment more selectively and prioritizing personal-superintelligence initiatives.

Fourth-quarter 2026 revenue is expected to be between $73 billion and $76 billion.

Full-year 2026 expenses are expected to total $175 billion to $179 billion, including the legal charge.

Full-year 2026 capital expenditures are forecast at $135 billion to $145 billion.

Meta expects foreign exchange to represent an approximately 1% headwind to fourth-quarter year-over-year revenue growth.

The company ended the quarter with $82.4 billion in cash and marketable securities and $83.7 billion in debt. Meta also announced plans to create a new class of non-voting capital stock that will be distributed as a stock dividend, giving shareholders one non-voting share for each existing share held. The move effectively represents a two-for-one stock split, with trading expected to begin in late January 2027.

news.Title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty to New Mexico in data privacy case
news.Content:
By Diana Novak Jones

Oct 21 (Reuters) - A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms on Wednesday to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data, hitting the company with one of the largest financial penalties in US history.

The ruling came in a ‌case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their ‌consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data.

"Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the ​heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict.

Mathew found that a penalty of more than $219 billion was warranted based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25 billion.

In a statement, C.J. Mahoney, Meta's chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal.

"This ruling, and the Attorney General's approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico," Mahoney said. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new ‌rules for what people can say online."

New Mexico Attorney General Raúl ⁠Torrez said in a statement after the ruling the penalty was one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in US history.

Meta previously faced a $5 billion penalty from the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 over the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Six other states settled their lawsuits against Meta related ⁠to Cambridge Analytica for $459.2 million as part of a $17.1 billion multistate settlement the company reached in August to resolve states' claims that the company's platforms had harmed teen mental health.

LAWSUIT FILED FIVE YEARS AGO

New Mexico's attorney general sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

The state accused Meta of lying to Facebook users ​in ​New Mexico about who had access to their data and its handling of hate speech and misinformation posted ​on the platform. It alleged the company knew third parties had broad ‌access to users' data and tolerated hate speech or other harmful content when it benefited the company's bottom line.

Story Continues

Cambridge Analytica, now defunct, used the data for voter profiling and targeting.

"It has been a long time coming holding Big Tech accountable," Torrez told a press conference in Albuquerque after Wednesday's ruling. "I think today's judgment is a clear break with that past and a very clear warning to those in this space and beyond that we intend to protect our people and protect our consumers."

Mathew's decision comes as Meta faces thousands of lawsuits and pressure from lawmakers over the impact of Instagram and Facebook on teen mental health, with another trial slated to begin next week.

Earlier this year, New Mexico won $942 million in a pair of trials against Meta over ‌claims it facilitated sexual exploitation of young people on Instagram and Facebook and misled consumers about the ​platforms' safety.

Analyst Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson & Co, called the latest New Mexico ruling costly ​but unlikely to impact the company's value.

"Meta is worth nearly two trillion dollars, and ​will likely continue to appeal these cases and drag them out," Luria said.

EXPERTS EXPECT LONG APPEAL FIGHT

Jurors in September had found that the company and ‌its leadership made 26 misleading statements on data privacy, hate speech and ​other subjects. Multiplying those statements by their potential ​audience, they said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico's consumer protection laws.

At a hearing on October 1, Randi McGinn, a lawyer for New Mexico, had asked Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion.

"This court should speak to Meta in the only language it understands, which is money, and the ​value of its stock price," McGinn said.

In court filings, Meta urged ‌Mathew to cap the penalties at $3.45 billion. The evidence showed that Meta does not sell user data and New Mexico did not prove that any consumer had ​actually been misled, the company said in court filings.

(Reporting by Diana Novak Jones in Chicago, additional reporting by Andrew Hay in New Mexico and Jaspreet Singh ​and Anzar Mehraj in Bangalore. Editing by Alexia Garamfalvi, Nia Williams, Aurora Ellis and Stephen Coates)

news.Title: Citadel's Ken Griffin Makes Stark Call on AI Boom
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Citadel founder Ken Griffin says investors are almost certainly in the middle of an artificial intelligence bubble , even as he believes the technology could reshape the economy and create a new generation of dominant companies. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with AMZN. Is AMZN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Griffin said the biggest problem is that corporate America is still struggling to prove that enormous AI spending is producing enough economic value. Corporate America has been very uneven in its ability to extract value from its AI models, Griffin said at the Future of Global Markets Conference in New York. He added that companies are increasingly looking at their bills from OpenAI and Anthropic and asking whether the productivity gains justify the cost. That question is becoming more important as spending on AI infrastructure continues to soar. Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) backed Anthropic, which is expected to file for an IPO in the coming weeks, could spend as much as $750 billion on additional computing power in the years ahead , according to The Wall Street Journal. Griffin said Anthropic's long-term success will depend on proving that its models become indispensable across industries. But his warning is not the same as saying AI is a fad. Any radical transformation of our economy is generally intertwined with a bubble, Griffin said. He compared the current environment with the dot-com era, when investors poured money into companies with weak or speculative business models even as the internet itself went on to transform the global economy. Investor Takeaway I think Griffin's point is more nuanced than simply calling AI overvalued. He is effectively saying the technology can be transformative while the capital flowing into it is still excessive . That distinction matters. The biggest risk may not be that AI demand disappears. It is that too many companies are being valued as if they will all become long-term winners. History suggests they will not. Griffin also believes AI could threaten white-collar jobs and established competitive advantages while simultaneously creating what he called a golden era for entrepreneurs. For investors, the key things to watch are AI monetization, enterprise productivity gains, infrastructure spending, cash burn and whether companies can convert usage into durable profits . If Griffin is right, the AI boom could still create enormous winners. But some of today's valuations may not survive the journey. Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 futures slipped in early Asian trading after both benchmarks advanced on Wall Street. The picture in Asia was mixed, with futures pointing to losses in South Korea and gains in Japan. Elsewhere, Treasury yields rose, helping lift the dollar, while gold held steady around $4,140 an ounce.

The latest results will test whether earnings can keep the AI trade on track as investors weigh strong growth against the mounting cost of funding the industry's expansion. Concerns have grown in recent weeks that heavy spending on data centers and computing capacity may take longer to translate into profits.

"It's all about earnings," said Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James Investment Management. "There's definitely a tension in the market between the growth path of the AI names and the ability to finance the industry."

Tesla Inc.'s spending again fell short of Wall Street expectations, complicating Elon Musk's plan to transform the electric-vehicle maker into an AI and robotics company. Capital expenditures totaled $4.73 billion in the third quarter, well below the $7.95 billion analysts had expected, according to estimates compiled by Bloomberg.

Meta Platforms Inc., by contrast, raised its capital-spending outlook as it ramps up investment in AI, underscoring the vast sums technology companies are committing to the buildout.

The scale of that investment is putting greater attention on whether infrastructure can keep pace. BlackRock Inc. Chief Executive Officer Larry Fink warned that delays in building data centers could push up computing costs and threaten economic growth.

"If we don't build out these data centers, it is actually more inflationary because the cost of compute is so high right now," Fink said in an interview on Bloomberg Television Wednesday on the sidelines of the Berlin Global Dialogue event. "And the faster we can build out more data centers, the more compute we have, the faster we can bring down the cost."

Story Continues

Elsewhere, a late advance in Brent crude faded as concerns over an escalation in Middle East hostilities eased. The US clarified that it had ordered the departure of some staff in Saudi Arabia only, rather than across the Gulf region as a news report had suggested.

Oil also pulled back from intraday highs after the Kremlin said Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to trilateral negotiations with the US and Ukraine on a potential peace deal.

Still, traders remained wary after repeated efforts to broker a ceasefire since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago failed to produce a lasting breakthrough.

"The market has seen numerous iterations of potential ceasefires and diplomatic breakthroughs, so there is understandable skepticism around whether improving rhetoric will translate into tangible progress," said Rebecca Babin, senior energy trader at CIBC Private Wealth Group. "Still, the shift in tone is tempering upside momentum."

Intel Corp. touted progress with its long-delayed US factory expansion, saying it was finishing up a plant in Arizona and making headway on the chipmaker's newest site in Ohio.

news.Title: Buying This Stock Right Now Could Be a Once-in-a-Generation Opportunity
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) is emerging as one of the biggest beneficiaries of a major shift in artificial intelligence infrastructure . Its latest growth projections suggest that the company could be significantly larger in just a few years.

Management recently raised its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to approximately $20 billion, up from its previous forecast of $18 billion. That's a massive number for a company that generated $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026. Marvell is now also targeting $70 billion to $90 billion in annual revenue by fiscal 2031, with much of that growth expected to come from custom AI chips and data center networking.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The custom chip advantage

Today, companies such as Microsoft , Amazon , and Alphabet 's Google rely heavily on Nvidia 's graphics processing units (GPUs) to run their AI systems. The tech giants are increasingly developing chips specifically designed for their own workloads. These custom chips, known as application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), can deliver better efficiency and lower costs for certain AI applications.

Marvell helps develop these chips. It also supplies networking technology that allows thousands of processors to communicate inside enormous AI data centers. Demand is accelerating rapidly. In fact, Marvell's data center business is now the company's largest revenue contributor.

A once-in-a-generation opportunity

If Marvell reaches $80 billion in annual revenue by fiscal 2031, the midpoint of management's target, its business would be nearly 10 times larger than it was in fiscal 2026. Management has also projected approximately $30 in adjusted earnings per share by fiscal 2031. Assuming Marvell can deliver those earnings and investors are willing to pay 25 times annual profits (a valuation that could be reasonable for a rapidly growing AI semiconductor company), its stock could reach approximately $750. That's more than triple its recent price of $237.

Of course, there's still some risk. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) is a powerful competitor you can't ignore, and AI infrastructure spending could slow. But if you're willing to hold for several years and tolerate a bit of volatility, Marvell could indeed prove to be a once-in-a-generation opportunity.

news.Title: Google Strikes Surprise Deal With Major AI Rival
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google is adding OpenAI's latest

models to Google Cloud, opening a new revenue opportunity by letting enterprise customers buy access to tools from one of Google's biggest AI rivals.

The agreement will bring GPT-6 Astra and OpenAI's Codex coding agent to Google Cloud in the coming weeks.

Is GOOG fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Customers will be able to access the models through Google Cloud's Model Garden and purchase them directly through Google Cloud Marketplace.

That matters because businesses can use their existing Google Cloud spending commitments to pay for OpenAI services, rather than negotiating separate contracts.

The arrangement lowers the friction for companies that already spend heavily with Google Cloud but want access to OpenAI's models.

It also creates an unusual competitive dynamic.

Google and OpenAI are fighting for leadership in generative AI, yet Google is effectively willing to sell access to a rival's technology if it strengthens the broader economics of its cloud platform.

For Google Cloud, the logic is straightforward.

The more AI workloads customers run through its infrastructure and marketplace, the more opportunity Google has to deepen enterprise relationships and capture additional spending, regardless of which model customers ultimately prefer.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of this deal is that Google is choosing distribution economics over model exclusivity .

Rather than forcing customers to choose between Gemini and OpenAI, Google can make money from enterprises that want both.

That could make Google Cloud more attractive as a neutral AI platform and potentially increase the value of existing cloud commitments.

The trade-off is that Google is also making it easier for customers to use a direct competitor's models.

For investors, the key things to watch are how quickly enterprises adopt OpenAI models through Google Cloud, whether the arrangement drives incremental cloud revenue, and how Google balances third-party model access with its own Gemini ecosystem .

The deal shows that the AI battle is becoming more complicated.

Google and OpenAI can compete at the model layer while still doing business together at the infrastructure layer.

news.Title: Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Will Be the Biggest Winner of 2027
news.Content:
In my view, artificial intelligence (AI) stocks will once again lead the market higher in 2027. However, I think there will start to be a rotation away from the pure-play pick-and-shovel infrastructure players and toward the hyperscalers that control the bulk of the spending. And against that backdrop, I think Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) is poised to be the best performing stock among AI mega-caps in 2027.

Whenever a new technological evolution is in its early phases, a large fraction of the gains go to the hardware companies that lay the foundation for it. However, in later stages, the gains should increasingly go to the companies that are benefiting from the prior investments.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

This pattern could certainly be seen in the dot-com boom. Hardware giants like Cisco , Sun Microsystems, and JDS Uniphase led the early build-out, but companies like Amazon and Google (now Alphabet) were the ones that captured the vast majority of the cumulative economic value over the long run.

I think a similar dynamic should start to play out again beginning next year, with Alphabet in position to be the clearest beneficiary. One of the biggest differences between the dot-com era and the AI era is that some of the companies funding the current build-out are the same ones building the end-user applications and platform ecosystems. Back in the late 1990s, it was telecoms that were doing most of the heavy lifting on infrastructure, while today it is the hyperscalers themselves. That is also one of the big reasons why these companies have been increasingly designing their own chips, and this is where Alphabet shines.

During the early phases of a new infrastructure build-out, there typically are large supply-and-demand imbalances. In this case, that gave semiconductor companies massive pricing power. The greatest example of this can be seen in the memory market, where prices have skyrocketed to unprecedented heights due to the shortage of memory chips. However, over time, supply chains normalize, production catches up to demand, and hardware prices come down. Investors have already started pricing in the potential of this happening.

Multiple advantages

In this middle phase that we are entering now, Alphabet has the biggest advantage because it has designed its entire ecosystem around its powerful custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). These processors give it a huge cost advantage in training its own AI models and running inference workloads. They also provide it with the strongest long-term cloud computing economics.

Story Continues

When using its own chips, Alphabet is getting a payback on its chip investments in about a year, compared to two to three years for rival hyperscaler Amazon. Meanwhile, a one-year payback on custom compute allows Alphabet to reinvest its operational cash flow back into data center expansion much faster than peers that are more reliant on Nvidia 's graphics processing units (GPUs) and therefore face longer payback horizons. Its chips are so highly regarded that, in association with its design partner, Broadcom , it is also selling them directly to compute-starved Anthropic, giving it another high-margin revenue stream.

Ultimately, Alphabet is poised to be one of the biggest AI winners because it controls every single layer of the AI stack. This starts with its custom chips, then moves to it having its own top-tier AI model, Gemini. Alphabet also has its own cloud platform (Vertex AI) and its own cloud security solution (Wiz). Alphabet then has the important product layer with Google Search, YouTube, and its other apps, where it can incorporate its Gemini model to improve its products and drive growth.

Alphabet also controls a large piece of the distribution layer through its ownership of the Chrome browser and the Android operating system, to go along with its revenue-sharing agreement for Google Search to be the default search engine on Apple devices. This essentially makes it the gateway to the internet and, increasingly, AI. And finally, it also controls the ad layer, as its ad network makes it easier to monetize consumer AI.

Altogether, this gives it the ultimate AI flywheel, and the value of that should start to shine through even more next year. That's why I think Alphabet will be the best-performing mega-cap AI stock in 2027.

news.Title: Trading Day: Tech it away
news.Content:
By Jamie McGeever

ORLANDO, Florida, Oct 21 (Reuters) - Buoyant AI sentiment on the back of quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer lifted Wall Street on Wednesday, as relatively calm energy, currency, and US bond markets allowed tech earnings to dominate. European markets were more lively, however, and France's 10-year bond yield rose above 5% ‌for the first time in nearly a quarter of a century.

In my column today, I look at five AI quirks and conundrums that investors should be aware of as ‌the US earnings season gets underway.

Today's Key Reads

• Government websites go dark as software flaw sparks security scramble

• Anthropic logged net loss of over $80 billion in first half of 2026

• Smouldering debt risk haunts French markets: Mike Dolan

• UK inflation ​and borrowing climb before Healey's first budget

• Meta ordered to pay $25 billion to New Mexico after jury finds company misled consumers about data privacy

• Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: South Korea +3.3%, best day since September 7. Europe +1%, UK steady. Mexico +1.5%. Nasdaq +1%, Dow +0.7%, S&P 500 +0.6%.SECTORS/SHARES: Seven sectors on the S&P 500 rise, four fall. Tech +1.6%, communications services -1.3%. Meta +4% after the bell on earnings, Tesla +2%, IBM +7%.FX: US dollar steady. Biggest G10 gainer is Aussie dollar, Indian rupee rises to six-week high. Biggest decliner Mexican peso, -1.5%.BONDS: French 10-year yield hits 5% for first time since 2002. US 20-year auction mixed — 2.73 bid/cover at the higher end of range of ‌the last year, but highest auction yield since 1986, some analysts ⁠say.COMMODITIES/METALS: Oil mixed — Brent steady, WTI settles lower. Gold little changed at $4,135/oz.

Today's Talking Points:

Anthropic

AI leader Anthropic posted a whopping $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of this year. That was up significantly from a $13 billion loss a year earlier, largely due to a $72 billion accounting charge. The net loss is almost ⁠double the $42 billion loss reported for calendar year 2025. Revenue in the first six months of the year was just over $16 billion.

Are these figures bullish or bearish? Depends which camp you're in. The headline loss is alarming, but it was mainly due to a one-off charge. Revenue is low and growth is slowing, but exclude the accounting charge and break-even doesn't look quite so far away. However, are the numbers and trends those ​of ​a company eyeing a $1.5-$2 trillion IPO valuation?

Sub subprime

Is the US housing market frozen? It's certainly seizing up, which ​is traditionally a major red flag for the wider economy. Pending home sales ‌in September plunged to the lowest since records began a quarter of a century ago, and housing starts fell 5.2% in the month to their lowest since the pandemic. US homebuilder sentiment, meanwhile, has plunged to the lowest level in nearly 14-1/2 years.

Story Continues

Rising Fed interest rates, stubbornly high home prices, and mortgage rates the highest in three years at 7.50% are all factors. But it is remarkable that activity now is even weaker than it was at the heights — or depths? — of the 2008 US housing market crash and its aftermath, and the Covid-19 pandemic in 2020. Given the importance of housing and related services to the US economy, growth could suffer.

Pounding the beat

UK finance minister John Healey delivers his first budget next week. To say he faces a few challenges would be an ‌understatement. Figures this week show government borrowing in September rose more than expected again, and public debt surpassed ​the psychologically key £3 trillion mark. Part of the reason why borrowing last month rose so much was debt interest payments — ​bond yields are the highest in decades, and with the debt pile growing, it's a ​difficult cycle to get out of. He has little wiggle room next week.

Bad news for sterling, right? Not necessarily. The latest inflation and wage growth data ‌have cemented market expectations for a rate hike on November 5. Indeed, ​traders now reckon the Bank of England will be ​the most hawkish G10 central bank over the next year or so, along with the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, and raise rates more than 100 bps. Sterling has pounced on the euro's weakness, surging almost 3% in the last month to its highest since May last year. And cable is rebounding from its year low. Next stop $1.35?

What could move ​markets tomorrow?

• New Zealand inflation (September)

• South Korea interest rate decision

• Canada PPI ‌inflation (September)

• US Treasury sells $26 billion of 5-year TIPS

• US earnings including Procter & Gamble, Union Pacific, Western Digital, Lockheed Martin

(Reporting by Jamie McGeever; Editing by Nia Williams)

news.Title: Q3 Earnings Beats for Meta, Tesla, IBM and T.I.
news.Content:
Mag 7 companies are now being heard from in Q3 earnings season. Meta Platforms META — parent company of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Messenger and Threads — outpaced estimates on both top and bottom lines after the closing bell today. Earnings of $3.83 per share surpassed the $3.45 analysts were looking for, on revenues of $64.6 billion in the quarter, its highest ever, and up +26% year over year.

Earnings were still well off the pace set in the year-ago quarter, and that's because Meta was hit with a $10 billion charge (of an $18 billion settlement overall) in a multi-state deal regarding social media addiction in young people. Revenue guidance was increased to a $73-76 billion range for the current quarter, as the company also projects between $135-145 billion in additional capex spending on AI infrastructure.

Tesla TSLA also outperformed the Zacks consensus on earnings and revenues, with $0.48 per share coming in 3 cents higher than estimates on revenues of $28.05 billion, beating the $27.78 billion estimate. Auto Gross Margins (minus EV credits) were up +18.1%, better than analysts had projected. Full-Service Driving (ESD) subscriptions rose +67% year over year to 1.74 million in the quarter.The Tesla robotaxi has now clocked 2 million unsupervised miles, and its Optimus robot production has begun at its Fremont, CA auto plant.

It's been a busy week for Tesla CEO Elon Musk, who saw his SpaceX SPCX Q3 numbers skyrocket (no pun intended) after Tuesday's close. He has also been implicated in the Starlink slowdown in Ukraine that hampered the U.S. ally's ability to conduct its war against Russia. This compares to year-ago revenues of $5.32 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

What's Next for Lam Research?

news.Title: Marvell Stock Is Bouncing Back. 3 Reasons the Bulls Aren’t Backing Down.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (MRVL) stock has started recovering after it got caught up in the recent AI selloff. After spending most of last week in the red, shares have been climbing this week. Including this morning gains, MRVL stock is up about 6% for the week, joining a broader rebound in semiconductor stocks after a tough period for the sector.

At its Oct. 6 Investor Day, the chipmaker raised its revenue goals and shared plans to become a bigger supplier of AI infrastructure. Marvell's custom AI chips, data center connectivity business, and improving growth outlook are three reasons why analysts believe this rebound has staying power.

More News from Barchart

Dear Nvidia Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 20

'No Question Tesla's Going to Merge With SpaceX' — Kevin O'Leary Says If You Own Tesla Stock, You'll Own the New Company After Flying Roadster Demo

Charlie Munger Said He Was Still Buying Apartment Complexes 'To Give Me Something To Do' but Ran Them the Opposite Way, 'It's All Deferred Gratification'

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

1. Marvell's Custom AI Chips Could Become a Much Bigger Business

The AI chip race is moving beyond standard GPUs. Big cloud companies are now creating processors that fit their specific needs, aiming for better performance, lower power use, and reduced costs. Marvell makes custom chips for these companies, so it stands to gain as more data centers use proprietary AI processors.

At its Investor Day, management raised its custom-chip revenue target for fiscal 2029 to more than $12 billion, up from the previous goal of more than $10 billion. The company now expects custom revenue to more than triple by 2029, thanks to anticipated growth in programs for large cloud customers. Although these are just goals for now, this upgraded outlook shows just how confident management feels about the business. Marvell's expanded Google partnership is another reason to be bullish. If Marvell reaches certain milestones, its expanded partnership with Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) Google could bring in as much as $120 billion in sales by fiscal 2033. This suggests Marvell's custom-chip business is becoming more important as cloud providers seek processors built for their needs.

2. Connectivity Is Emerging as a Second Major Growth Engine

AI requires more than computing power, and it is becoming a new growth area for Marvell. Large AI clusters rely on fast connections between chips, servers, and racks, which increases the need for optical interconnects, digital signal processors, and networking technology. Marvell provides solutions across these areas and supports the wider AI infrastructure, not just processors.

Story Continues

In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Marvell made $2.17 billion from data center revenue. This was a 46% increase from the year-ago quarter and made up 79% of the company's total sales. During the investor day event, management also attributed the fiscal 2028 revenue target to connectivity. This indicates that the company's higher expectations are not based solely on one custom-chip opportunity. Management also highlighted opportunities in faster optical networking, including 1.6-terabit and future 3.2-terabit technologies, as AI data centers require increasingly high-speed connections.

3. Wall Street Has a Much Bigger Growth Story to Consider

Also at its Investor Day, Marvell made a bold move by raising its long-term targets. The company now aims for revenue between $70 billion and $90 billion, with $80 billion as the midpoint. For comparison, Marvell's fiscal 2026 revenue was $8.2 billion. To hit the midpoint, Marvell would need to grow its annual revenue to nearly ten times its 2026 level within just five years. Management now estimates that its total addressable market could reach about $400 billion by 2030, four times its earlier estimate. This shows why management believes the company can grow significantly without relying on just one new product or customer.

The company is focused on more than just revenue growth. For fiscal 2031, Marvell aims for gross margins between 56% and 59%, operating margins of 44% to 46%, free cash flow margins above 36%, and adjusted EPS over $30 at the midpoint of its revenue forecast. Management said these targets reflect current customer relationships, recent design wins, ongoing development programs, and plans to secure supplier capacity before demand increases. Marvell's ability to meet these goals will depend on how well it executes.

Wall Street responded to Marvell's long-term outlook by raising its price targets. TD Cowen upgraded Marvell to "Buy" with a $350 target, while Piper Sandler, Needham, and Bank of America subsequently raised their targets to $400. Meanwhile, Oppenheimer and RBC Capital increased the target price to $425.

Despite the broader AI selloff, MRVL stock has climbed 169% so far this year. The average target price for the stock is $337.05, pointing to a possible 42% gain. Jefferies has assigned the highest estimate of $450, which would mean a potential 90% rally from current levels. Overall, most analysts are still strongly bullish about MRVL stock. news.Title: Europe's financial regulators query Google over cloud outage that hit banks
news.Content:
By Phoebe Seers and Elizabeth Howcroft

LONDON/PARIS, Oct 21 (Reuters) - Financial regulators in Europe are questioning Google after a cloud computing outage on Tuesday left millions of bank customers without access to ‌key financial services for hours.

The European Banking Authority said that it has been in contact with ‌Google Cloud to obtain further information on the incident, understand its implications and assess its potential impact on financial entities in the ​EU, a spokesperson for the watchdog told Reuters.

Alphabet's Google said the disruption, which lasted several hours, was caused by a "power event" in a London-based network that serves customers across Europe. Revolut, Lloyds and HSBC were among the banks affected.

Lloyds and HSBC did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A Google spokesperson said: "We have resolved a disruption to ‌Google Cloud services at a third-party ⁠facility in our europe-west2 cloud region due to a power event. Services have been restored. We will update our public status dashboard with an analysis."

At Revolut, which has around ⁠13 million UK customers, a wide range of services including logging in, card payments and cash withdrawals were affected on Tuesday, according to the bank's website.

Revolut said in a statement that it was reviewing the incident to reduce the impact ​of ​any future third-party disruptions, and that customer funds and data ​had remained safe throughout.

The outage is the ‌first major test of new rules across Europe designed to strengthen the resilience of technology providers, including cloud firms, on which the financial sector depends.

The European Union last year designated 19 technology firms as critical third-party providers to the financial sector, bringing them under joint direct oversight of three financial regulators — including the EBA — for the first time. Britain took similar steps for four cloud providers, citing the risk that an outage at a ‌major supplier could affect multiple financial firms at the same ​time. Google Cloud falls under both regulatory frameworks.

In Britain, parliament's Treasury ​Committee has written to the Bank of England ​and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), seeking details of the regulators' response to the outage ‌on Tuesday, the scale of the disruption and ​any financial harm caused.

The FCA ​said it was engaging with Google over the incident. Under Britain's critical third party regime, designated providers like Google Cloud must report serious outages to the FCA and the BoE.

Story Continues

A spokesperson for the Bank ​of England declined to comment.

Under UK ‌rules, banks ultimately are responsible for the services they provide to customers, including when they ​rely on third-party providers.

(Reporting by Elizabeth Howcroft in Paris and Phoebe Seers in London; additional reporting ​by Lawrence White in London; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria)

news.Title: AppLovin vs. Pinterest: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
As the digital advertising market evolves, investors are weighing the explosive growth of AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP) against the social commerce potential of Pinterest (NYSE:PINS). Which stock is the better buy?

AppLovin provides the behind-the-scenes software that helps mobile apps grow and make money, while Pinterest is a visual discovery engine where users plan their future purchases. Both companies thrive on advertiser spending, but they offer very different risk and reward profiles for investors looking to capitalize on the next wave of ad-tech innovation.

The case for AppLovin

AppLovin provides software tools for mobile app developers and recently divested its internal apps business to focus on advertising technology. Its platform uses AI-driven bidding to help clients like Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) reach users across global mobile games. Many of its clients are also competitors, which creates a complex relationship dynamic and means revenue can be sensitive to industry shifts.

In FY 2025, revenue reached nearly $5.5 billion, marking a significant 70% increase over the previous year. This growth helped the company achieve net income of approximately $3.3 billion, which represents a net margin of 60.8%. This is a strong improvement from the 49% net margin recorded in the prior fiscal year, reflecting higher profitability at scale.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 1.7x, meaning total debt is 1.7 times the value of shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with current assets, was healthy at 3.3x. Free cash flow, calculated as operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, reached close to $3.9 billion for the fiscal year.

The case for Pinterest

Pinterest operates a visual discovery platform where over 619 million monthly active users find inspiration for shopping and DIY projects. It makes money primarily through advertising, particularly in the retail and consumer packaged goods sectors. The company has focused on making its pins more shoppable to better compete among tech stocks that bridge social media and commerce.

In FY 2025, revenue grew to approximately $4.2 billion, representing an increase of nearly 15.8% year over year. The company reported net income of roughly $416.9 million for the period, resulting in a net margin of 9.9%. While the company is profitable, its net margin is lower than its peer in this comparison as it continues to invest in platform updates.

Pinterest maintains a very conservative balance sheet as of its December 2025 reporting, with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.1x. The current ratio, measuring short-term liquidity, was exceptionally high at 7.6x, indicating a large cushion of assets to cover near-term obligations. However, stock-based compensation represented roughly 68.6% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Story Continues

Risk profile comparison

AppLovin faces risks from third-party mobile platforms like Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) and Alphabet, which control privacy policies that can limit data availability for ad targeting. The company is also dealing with several securities class action lawsuits and a legal challenge regarding the distribution of inappropriate ads to children. Intense competition from large rivals, including Amazon and Unity Software (NYSE:U), further complicates its market position.

Pinterest depends heavily on its ability to keep users engaged, as its revenue is tied to the size and activity of its user base. The company is vulnerable to changes in search engine algorithms and mobile operating system policies that restrict how it tracks user behavior. It also relies on Amazon for its cloud infrastructure and faces ongoing regulatory scrutiny regarding data privacy and content moderation for younger users.

In Q2 2026, revenue grew more than 50% year over year and the underlying profitability was exceptional, though revenue came in slightly below analyst expectations and the stock fell sharply after the report, a reminder that expectations for this company run very high.

Revenue grew 18% in Q2 2026 and AI is improving how ads perform on the platform. The opportunity in social commerce with this company can't be dismissed.

The honest challenge with Pinterest is that converting that engaged audience into consistent profits has taken longer than investors expected. The company is still posting GAAP net losses while AppLovin generates substantial free cash flow. For me, owning the platform already delivering on its promise feels like the stronger starting point. AT&T Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | AT&T Inc. Quote

T's Advanced Connectivity Revenues Gain Ground

Advanced Connectivity revenues increased 7.2% year over year to $29.48 billion. Service revenues rose 6.1% to $23.9 billion, while equipment revenues climbed 12.2% to $5.58 billion, benefiting from stronger wireless equipment activity.

Wireless service revenues rose 5% to $17.76 billion, supported by retail subscriber growth, converged accounts and pricing actions. Promotional discounts partially offset these gains. Advanced home internet revenues jumped 23.4% to $2.98 billion, reflecting fiber and AT&T Internet Air growth, including contributions from the acquired Lumen mass-market fiber business.

AT&T's Internet Additions Reach a Record

The company added 442,000 fiber and 327,000 fixed wireless internet connections during the quarter. Total consumer and business locations reached with fiber exceeded 39 million, keeping AT&T on track to surpass 40 million by year-end.

The advanced home Internet convergence rate reached 42.8%, representing the proportion of advanced home internet customers also subscribing to AT&T's postpaid wireless service. Its converged customer base expanded by approximately 350,000. Postpaid phone churn was 0.92%, indicating the share of subscribers leaving the service.

T's Business Connectivity Growth Offsets Declines

Business fiber and advanced connectivity revenues grew 8.7% year over year to $1.99 billion, primarily on higher fiber and fixed wireless revenues. This contributed to a 2.5% increase in overall business service revenues.

Business transitional and other revenues fell 14.6% to $1.02 billion as demand for virtual private network and wholesale services declined. Other service revenues were down 8.6% to $148 million, illustrating the continuing shift away from older offerings.

AT&T's Legacy Business Continues to Contract

Legacy segment revenues declined 24.5% year over year to $1.52 billion amid lower demand for copper-based network services. Operating expenses decreased 23.5% to $1.02 billion, reflecting lower personnel costs, network decommissioning and reduced fulfillment cost amortization.

Legacy operating income dropped 26.7% to $498 million, with operating margin falling 90 basis points to 32.8%. More than 90% of wire centers have been approved to stop selling legacy services as the company works toward substantially retiring its copper-based network.

Story Continues

T's Adjusted Profit Grows Despite Charges

Consolidated operating expenses increased to $28.2 billion from $24.6 billion, largely reflecting a $2.6 billion noncash impairment tied to the planned sale of AT&T Mexico, employee separation costs and higher wireless equipment expenses. Advertising and bad debt costs also increased.

Reported operating income declined to $4.1 billion from $6.1 billion, while adjusted operating income improved to $7.6 billion from $6.6 billion. Adjusted EBITDA increased 5.4% to $12.51 billion, with the adjusted EBITDA margin edging up to 38.7% from 38.6% a year ago.

AT&T's Latin America Revenues Rise

Latin America revenues increased 13.2% year over year to $1.24 billion, primarily driven by favorable foreign exchange movements and postpaid wireless subscriber growth. Service revenues rose 14.7%, while equipment revenues advanced 10.8%.

Operating expenses increased 11.4% to $1.2 billion due to currency effects, higher bad debt expenses and equipment costs. Operating income improved to $45 million from $22 million, while EBITDA rose 18.6% to $236 million.

T's Cash Flow and Outlook Take Focus

Free cash flow increased to $4.95 billion from $4.87 billion a year earlier. Cash provided by operating activities from continuing operations totaled $10.52 billion, while capital investment reached $5.57 billion. The company returned approximately $4.8 billion to shareholders, including $2.8 billion in share repurchases.

AT&T ended the quarter with $10.77 billion in cash and equivalents and $149.82 billion in net debt. Net debt increased sequentially following the EchoStar spectrum purchase, taking the net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio to 3.13.

Management now expects adjusted earnings around $2.40 per share in 2026. It projects capital investment of $23 billion to $24 billion this year and $22 billion to $23 billion annually in 2027 and 2028. Free cash flow targets are at least $18 billion in 2026, $19 billion in 2027 and $21 billion in 2028.

news.Title: Electric Utility NiSource’s Data-Center Power Business Can Continue to Grow — And NI Stock Is Cheap
news.Content:
Energy utility NiSource (NI) continues to meaningfully expand its data-center power business, most recently announcing a major deal with Microsoft (MSFT) on Oct. 16. Meanwhile, the Indiana-based utility expects its earnings per share, excluding certain items, to grow at a robust compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9% to 10% between 2026 and 2033, while the company — which serves roughly 3.3 million natural gas customers and 500,000 electricity customers across six states — may be able to expand its data-center business to other states. Finally, two banks have been bullish on NI stock recently, while shares are changing hands at a relatively low valuation despite a significant dividend yield.

As a consequence of all of these points, value investors, growth-at-a-reasonable-price investors, and conservative investors may want to consider buying NI stock. Let's take a closer look.

Crude Oil Prices Fall on Diplomacy Hopes to End Iran War

Crude Oil Prices Erase an Early Rally on Unconfirmed Iran Peace Talks

NiSource Has a Promising Data-Center Power Business

On Oct. 16, NiSource announced that it had reached a 20-year electricity supply deal with Microsoft (MSFT). Under the deal, the utility will provide the tech giant with about 1,100 megawatts of power beginning in 2028.

This agreement comes after NiSource signed a contract to power Alphabet's (GOOGL) "large‑scale data center in northern Indiana" in April. Moreover, in November 2025, the company disclosed that it would provide as much as 3 gigawatts of power to Amazon's (AMZN) data centers for 15 years. In April 2026, the utility noted that it had expanded its agreement with Amazon.

All of the large, upcoming data centers that NiSource intends to power will be built in Indiana. However, since the utility firm also distributes natural gas in states like Ohio, Virginia, and Kentucky, it may eventually be able to power data centers in other states as well.

What Do Analysts Think of NI Stock?

After meeting with management in September, BMO Capital trimmed its price target for NI stock to $45 from $49 but kept an "Outperform" rating. More recently, however, analysts raised their target from $45 to $48 per share. BMO Capital has become more confident in the value of NiSource's business, while low visibility for data centers in a number of states is reportedly incentivizing firms to build facilities in places like Indiana.

Story Continues

For its part, in July, Keybanc also named NiSource as one of two companies positioned to exploit strengthening electricity demand from data centers. NiSource has reportedly been able to reduce worries around the burden on ratepayers as well as political opposition to data centers.

On the valuation front, NI stock currently trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 20.8 times. Because the company expects its adjusted EPS to expand at a CAGR of 9% to 10% between 2026 and 2033, that valuation actually appears relatively low and attractive. Plus, NI stock has a meaningful forward dividend yield of 2.81%.

Overall, NI stock has a consensus "Moderate Buy" rating on Wall Street based on 17 analysts with coverage.

news.Title: 1 Number Every UPS Investor Should Watch in Q3 Earnings
news.Content:
In the case of United Parcel Service (NYSE: UPS), it's all about adjusted operating profit margin. This key number lies at the heart of the company's transformational strategy, which entails reducing less-profitable Amazon deliveries in favor of higher-margin e-commerce deliveries, particularly in targeted markets such as healthcare and small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs).

At the same time, UPS's investments in smart facilities and automation are intended to improve productivity and, ultimately, margins. Everything points to margin expansion, but is it working out like that for UPS right now? Let's find out.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

UPS changes guidance

In the fourth-quarter earnings presentation in January, management forecast full-year revenue of $89.7 billion and an adjusted operating profit margin of 9.6%, implying $8.611 billion in adjusted operating profit. The headline guidance was maintained on the first-quarter earnings call in April. Still, on the second-quarter earnings call, management increased its full-year revenue guidance to $91.2 billion and specifically said that adjusted operating profit would be about $8.65 billion.

Why the guidance change isn't good news

Superficially, it's an increase in revenue guidance and also an increase over the implied guidance of $8.611 billion I calculated above. However, there are two key considerations for investors, and they matter a lot for the upcoming results of a company with a near-7% dividend yield .

First, the new guidance implies an adjusted operating margin of 9.48%, down from the 9.6% initially forecast. Second, it's important to understand the nuance of the guidance change. As previously discussed, due to rising fuel costs, UPS raised fuel surcharges by $1.173 billion in the first half. Bearing in mind that the increase in full-year revenue guidance was $1.5 billion to $91.2 billion, it's reasonable to expect a large chunk of the revenue increase is due to the fuel surcharge.

Turning to the difficult question of how much profit UPS is making from the fuel surcharges, its fuel cost and third-party costs increased by $744 million, resulting in a net difference of $429 million -- a figure slightly more than the increase in adjusted operating profit guidance.

To be clear, management's position is that the fuel surcharge is intended solely to cover increased fuel costs, and there are associated costs related to fuel disruptions as well. Moreover, CFO Brian Dykes argued that "the net impact to consolidated operating profit dollars was modest" on the second-quarter earnings call.

Story Continues

In the absence of knowing exactly what kind of figure "modest" implies, it could be argued that the combination of a positive contribution from fuel surcharges over fuel cost -- something not likely to prove sustainable -- actually implies a significant decrease in adjusted operating profit margin if the impact of fuel is taken out.

The key metric to look out for

As noted, this is the year when UPS should start to build on margin improvement, not least because it finished the so-called "glide down" of Amazon deliveries by 50% (volume) from the start of 2025 to the middle of 2026. That's why investors are so focused on margin, particularly the expected adjusted operating profit margin in the U.S. domestic package segment.

I've replicated what the Wall Street consensus, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence , is expecting for the segment, and the company's total adjusted operating margins will be below. As is often the case with Wall Street estimates, the full-year U.S. Domestic Package margin guidance mirrors management's 7.5% guidance given on the last earnings call.

Watch UPS's margin guidance

All told, in the absence of management disclosing the exact figure, it's hard to know exactly how much fuel surcharges are adding to the blue chip stock's profitability. However, management has guided to a full-year U.S. Domestic Package adjusted operating profit margin of 7.5%, and the implied total company adjusted operating margin guidance is 9.48%.

Any failure to maintain those figures or meet the Wall Street analyst consensus in the table in the third quarter would suggest its margin trajectory isn't quite what most hope for. That said, if UPS beats both expectations, the margin expansion story will support the case for the stock.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again

In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. If you'd invested $5,000 then, you'd be sitting on $2,813,887 today.*

Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It's a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast.

news.Title: Cisco (CSCO): Can It Profit From Helping Customers Spend Less on AI?
news.Content:
Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ: CSCO ), included in Insider Monkey's 10 Best Pick and Shovel AI Stocks to Buy for the Long Term , has another way to benefit from AI investment: helping customers control their operating costs. Agents can repeatedly call models and retry tasks, creating unpredictable bills. Monitoring that waste could support lasting software demand.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) has a forward P/E of 20x and a trailing P/E of 32x. Trailing P/E uses earnings from the past twelve months; forward P/E uses forecast earnings. Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE:ANET) has a forward P/E of 39x. Its latest quarterly GAAP operating margin was 45%, versus 25% here, supporting a premium. The lower valuation looks reasonable if earnings growth becomes dependable cash generation.

For Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO), the midpoint of management's separate fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $5.05–$5.11 implies approximately 17% growth from $4.33 in fiscal 2026. Networking revenue grew 22%, supporting the outlook. Fiscal 2026 GAAP EPS was $3.33; adjustments included stock compensation, acquisition amortization, and restructuring. Reported earnings also benefited from investment gains excluded from management's adjusted results. These accounting effects are separate from expected operating growth. Software deserves valuation weight when recurring relationships produce cash after reinvestment .

AI Complexity Creates a Monitoring Problem

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) has added Tokenomics capabilities to Splunk Agent Observability, connecting AI usage and spending with agent performance. Customers can identify expensive workflows and compare model cost with quality. Switching routine tasks to cheaper models could reduce bills while preserving useful output. Monitoring remains necessary as applications and models change.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) can bring network information into those investigations and sell through established enterprise relationships. Integrating monitoring into operating routines could lower selling costs and support renewals. The commercial test is whether AI adoption expands recurring customer spending .

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) still has work to do. Fiscal 2026 software revenue rose 4% to $23.2 billion, while total subscription revenue increased just 1%. Observability revenue also grew 4%, but network assurance supplied the growth while the observability suite declined. New monitoring features need to reverse that decline before they can change the earnings mix.

Story Continues

Customers Must Save More Than They Pay

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) prices Agent Observability around spans, which record individual workflow operations, with included evaluation capacity and optional additional resources. Cheaper models can lower customers' token bills without reducing monitored activity. Eliminating unnecessary workflow steps, however, could constrain billable usage. Expanding coverage and retaining customers must compensate. Customers should measure savings after monitoring fees and integration work, while preserving task quality.

Dynatrace, Inc. (NYSE:DT), with a forward P/E of 30x, offers competing AI cost and performance tools. Its predominantly subscription-based business helps explain its premium. Collecting, storing and evaluating more data also costs money. Higher monitoring volumes create value only if subscription revenue grows faster than delivery and development costs.

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) generated $12.8 billion of fiscal 2026 free cash flow, down 4%, after deducting capital spending from operating cash flow. Higher capital spending and a final $2.3 billion transition-tax payment weighed on cash generation. Inventory absorbed $2.54 billion, while financing receivables absorbed $1.84 billion across the business. Equipment supply and customer financing tie up cash before collections arrive.

Inventory purchase commitments reached $17.17 billion, versus $7.60 billion, reflecting hyperscaler demand and higher memory prices. Supplying AI infrastructure requires more upfront investment. Delayed shipments could postpone collections; weaker demand could leave expensive components unused and force write-downs that reduce margins. Year-end debt was $29.5 billion, against $15.9 billion of cash and investments. Shareholders need software growth that strengthens cash conversion .

Conclusion

Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) looks fairly valued at 20x forward earnings. Helping customers spend less on AI can become profitable recurring business when savings support renewals and broader adoption. Sustaining the valuation requires delivery of the earnings outlook, stronger subscription growth, and cash conversion after investment. A higher software premium needs improving monitoring revenue and margins; useful dashboards alone will not earn it.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of CSCO as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than CSCO and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock .
