news.Title: Jim Cramer and Ken Fisher’s AI Pick: Microsoft (MSFT)
news.Content:
Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has gone almost nowhere over the past twelve months, with the stock up about 2% in that period. The stock ranks second on our list of the top 10 stocks Jim Cramer and billionaire Ken Fisher like . The company reports its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results on October 28, so can the stock gain in the coming weeks? Let's analyze as the earnings date nears.

How Microsoft Makes Money From AI

Microsoft earns AI revenue in two main places. Microsoft 365 Copilot is an AI assistant inside Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams that companies pay for per employee. It passed 30 million paid seats in the fiscal fourth quarter. Azure, Microsoft's cloud, rents computing power and AI models to businesses, and its revenue grew 43% in that quarter. Microsoft also holds a financial stake in OpenAI, whose products run on Azure first.

Microsoft sells new AI tools faster than most rivals because its software already runs inside almost every large company, so customers skip the long process of approving a new vendor. Its commercial backlog, which is signed business not yet delivered, rose 84%, or 25% without OpenAI. See whether the spending is paying off.

Will AI Agents Replace the Office Seat?

This is the biggest worry on the software side. Most of Microsoft's revenue and profit still come from software sold per user. If AI agents do office work, companies need fewer employee seats, and Microsoft itself expects seat growth to slow over time. Microsoft has three answers. Companies need cloud computing to run AI agents, and Azure rents it out. Its customers' work data already sits in Microsoft's systems, which AI agents need to do useful work. Microsoft is also building its own AI models, expected by 2027, to cut what it pays outside AI providers when people use Copilot.

Impax Global Environmental Markets Fund described the same selloff in its investor letter. Click to read the full letter.

Capacity, Chips and OpenAI

Capacity is the first open question. Bloomberg reported that Microsoft restricted new cloud subscriptions at key data center hubs in the US and Europe because it lacked capacity. Morgan Stanley estimates Microsoft added about 3.25 gigawatts of capacity in fiscal 2026 and expects about 4.25 gigawatts in fiscal 2027.

Chips are the second. Microsoft unveiled its Maia 300 AI chip this month and says it delivers 40% more output per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. Production starts early next year. The chip could reduce Microsoft's reliance on Nvidia, but earlier Maia versions shipped only in limited volumes.

Story Continues

OpenAI is the third. It makes up a large part of the backlog, which is why the 84% growth drops to 25% without it. A change in that relationship would hit Microsoft's AI sales.

What Wall Street Wants to See on October 28

Microsoft has beaten earnings estimates in each of the last four quarters. The stock has rebounded in recent weeks, so Morgan Stanley says it faces a higher bar. The firm rates Microsoft Overweight and wants to see Azure growth in the mid-40s, better monetization of Microsoft 365 and Copilot, and disciplined operating expenses. The stock is up about 40% over the past six months, so investors expect a clean report. Check out the full analysis here.

Three Ways the Report Could Land

If Azure grows 44% to 45% or faster and Microsoft shows Copilot use deepening, the rally has support. If Azure lands on guidance but capital spending rises faster than cash flow and Microsoft gives no new Copilot data, the stock could stall, since expectations have moved up. If Azure growth falls short, capacity limits persist or OpenAI news hits the backlog, the AI-spending worry that sent shares down after the fiscal 2026 third-quarter report could return. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) has beaten earnings estimates four quarters in a row, and the market will want to see a fifth.

While we acknowledge the potential of MSFT as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. I won't be surprised to see this semiconductor stock emerge stronger from the recent sectorwide sell-off and soar by 2030. Let's look at the reasons why TSMC could step on the gas and jump nearly 3x by the end of the decade to hit $1,200.

Image source: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

TSMC accelerating growth is great news for investors

TSMC's Q3 revenue increased 41% year over year to $46.7 billion. Even better, the company's net profit margin increased to 51.1% last quarter from 45.7% in the year-ago period. As a result, TSMC's earnings per share jumped by 57% from the year-ago period to $4.60.

Importantly, TSMC sees its growth rate picking up nicely this quarter. It expects $53.3 billion in Q4 revenue at the midpoint of its guidance range, implying a 58% increase over the prior-year period. Also, TSMC sees its operating margin at 57.5% in the current quarter, an improvement of 3.5 percentage points over last year.

The improvement in TSMC's revenue growth rate and its expanding margins can be attributed to the robust demand for the company's advanced chips used in AI data centers. TSMC management cited multiple AI-related catalysts driving growth. The emergence of agentic AI applications, the growing demand for server central processing units (CPUs) that run inference workloads, and the need for networking components to connect AI chip clusters and data centers are all boosting the demand for TSMC's chips.

It is worth noting that TSMC got 69% of its revenue from the advanced 2-nanometer (nm), 3nm, and 5nm nodes combined in the previous quarter. That was an improvement over the 60% revenue contribution from these nodes in the year-ago period. Notably, the company began recognizing revenue from the 2nm node last quarter and is now planning to aggressively ramp up output of chips manufactured using this process node.

Story Continues

The shift toward the 2nm node should be a tailwind for the company's revenue and earnings in the long run. That's because the 2nm node reportedly commands a 50% premium compared to the 3nm node. Also, TSMC has been gradually increasing the prices of its advanced process nodes. The Taiwanese giant is reportedly planning to implement a 5% to 10% price increase next year for advanced nodes, along with a 10% to 15% increase in advanced packaging prices. The higher prices should eventually filter down to the company's bottom line.

Another important point is that TSMC management expects its AI-related revenue to grow faster than the mid-to-high 50% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) it originally estimated through 2029. As such, it is easy to see why analysts have increased their earnings per share (EPS) expectations from TSMC.

TSM EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

The math behind a $1,200 stock price

The above chart indicates that TSMC's earnings could increase to $29.82 per share in 2028. The company delivered EPS of $10.65 in 2025, indicating its bottom line is on track to grow at a 40% CAGR through 2028.

Importantly, analysts expect TSMC to maintain an identical growth rate over the long run.

TSM EPS LT Growth Estimates data by YCharts

If TSMC's earnings increase by 43% in 2029 and 2030, its EPS could jump to $60.98 at the end of the forecast period (using 2028's projected EPS as the base). The tech-laden Nasdaq-100 index has a forward earnings multiple of 22. Assuming TSMC trades at even 20 times earnings in 2030, its stock price could reach $1,219 (based on the $60.98 EPS estimate).

That implies a potential jump of nearly 3x in just over four years. So, this AI stock could surpass the $1,200 mark by 2030, suggesting investors should look at the bigger picture and consider buying TSMC for healthy long-term upside.

news.Title: KLA (KLAC) Earnings Expected to Grow: Should You Buy?
news.Content:
KLA (KLAC) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 28, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This maker of equipment for manufacturing semiconductors is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.18 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +34.1%.

Revenues are expected to be $4.05 billion, up 26.1% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.28% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

Story Continues

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for KLA?

For KLA, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.03%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that KLA will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

Analysts often consider to what extent a company has been able to match consensus estimates in the past while calculating their estimates for its future earnings. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that KLA would post earnings of $1 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.05, delivering a surprise of +5.00%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

KLA doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

news.Content:
L1 Capital , an investment management firm, released its "L1 Capital International Fund" (unhedged) third-quarter 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here . This Quarterly Report covers the unusually complex investment environment, AI's opportunities and challenges, portfolio strategy, September 2026 performance, and recent adjustments. The Fund returned +3.5% net of fees in the September 2026 quarter, outperforming its benchmark's 1.5% gain, despite a stronger Australian dollar. Energy, Information Technology and Communication Services performed well, while Utilities, Industrials and Real Estate lagged. The portfolio held 22 investments, with the ten largest representing about 63% of assets. The strategy emphasizes diversification across different earnings drivers rather than concentration in a single sector or theme, including AI. Amid geopolitical instability, higher interest rates, and rapid technological change, the Fund assesses multiple scenarios while maintaining exposure to high-quality companies and managing valuation risk. It views AI as both an opportunity and a source of uncertainty, focusing ultimately on businesses with durable competitive advantages, earnings, and cash generation. Additionally, reviewing the Strategy's top five holdings provides insight into its best positions for 2026.

In its Q3 2026 investor letter, L1 Capital International Fund highlighted Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ). Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) is a multinational software company that develops and supports software, services, devices, and solutions, holding dominant positions in software, cloud infrastructure, generative AI, and gaming. On October 20, 2026, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) closed at $531.87 per share, reflecting a market capitalization of $3.95 trillion. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) posted a one‑month return of 6.25%, while its shares gained 2.18% over the past 52 weeks.

L1 Capital International Fund stated the following regarding Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

" Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) contributed more than 0.5 percentage points to returns. Microsoft has also been a core Fund holding for an extended period. While it is an enormous and diversified business, two developments are particularly important to our assessment of its future earnings power and valuation.

The first is adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot. Management disclosed in its most recent quarterly update that paid seats had reached 30 million, with net seat additions more than doubling quarter-on-quarter. After a relatively slow start, Copilot's capabilities have improved materially, with both independent assessments and our own experience indicating meaningful progress. Microsoft's competitive advantages in trust, distribution and security are also showing signs of proving increasingly valuable as enterprises focus on the governance, integration and cost of deploying AI at scale. The second critical issue is Azure, Microsoft's cloud computing and AI infrastructure platform. The investment case is not simply about revenue growth, but whether Microsoft can generate attractive returns on hundreds of billions of dollars of capital expenditure. Broadening its product offering and reducing dependence on OpenAI are also important considerations. So far, the indicators are encouraging. Microsoft's share price has been volatile, rising 38% during the September quarter. For the world's fourth largest company, with a market capitalisation approaching $4 trillion, this is a remarkable move, particularly given the absence of a comparable change in our fundamental assessment of the business. Rather than demonstrating a dramatic improvement in Microsoft's prospects over three months, we think the share price recovery largely reflects a reversal of previously excessive investor pessimism. Today's share price more appropriately balances the potential risks and returns."

news.Title: UPS to Report Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
United Parcel Service UPS is scheduled to report its third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 27, before the market opens. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the to-be-reported quarter's earnings per share and revenues is pegged at $1.63 and $22.23 billion, respectively.

The bottom-line projection indicates a year-over-year decline of 6.3%. The consensus mark for the to-be-reported quarter has remained stable over the past 60 days. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for quarterly revenues implies a year-over-year expansion of 3.8%.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

For 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for UPS' revenues is pegged at $91.71 billion, implying a 3.4% year-over-year uptick. The consensus mark for 2026 EPS is pegged at $7.19, indicating a year-over-year improvement of 0.4%.

This package delivery company's earnings beat estimates each of the past four quarters, with the average surprise being 12.4%.

United Parcel Service, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

United Parcel Service, Inc. price-eps-surprise | United Parcel Service, Inc. Quote

Q3 Earnings Whispers for UPS

Our proven model predicts an earnings beat for UPS for the September quarter. The combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold) increases the odds of an earnings beat. That is exactly the case here. You can uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they're reported with our Earnings ESP Filter.

UPS has an Earnings ESP of +0.95% and a Zacks Rank #3. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

Factors Shaping UPS' Quarterly Performance

We expect the still-ongoing macro uncertainty due to the Middle East conflict to have dented UPS' performance in the September quarter. The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has resulted in a sharp jump in oil prices. This has been naturally hurting the bottom line of transportation stocks, like UPS. This is because fuel expenses represent a key input cost for a transportation company.

UPS' decision to scale back business with Amazon AMZN is expected to have kept third-quarter volumes muted. Management reached an agreement in principle with Amazon to reduce the e-commerce giant's volume by more than 50% by June 2026. CEO Carol Tome noted that Amazon was not the company's most profitable customer. The reduction in volumes is compelling UPS to right-size its network. We expect overall volumes to decline 5.4% year over year in the September quarter.

That said, third-quarter results are likely to reflect UPS' efforts toward improving profitability over sheer volume, through its "Better, Not Bigger" strategy. Under the cost-cutting initiatives, UPS has substantially reduced its U.S. operational workforce and closed daily operations at multiple leased and owned buildings. Moreover, UPS has been focusing on increasing automation in sorting and operations and leveraging AI for logistics planning to boost efficiency.

Story Continues

The shift in focus toward higher-margin areas such as small and medium-sized businesses or SMBs and healthcare logistics from low-margin volumes (like Amazon) is expected to be reflected in UPS' first-quarter results. Notably, SMBs contributed 34.5% to total U.S. volume in the June quarter, reflecting a 250-basis-point year-over-year improvement. We expect SMBs to have performed strongly in the September quarter as well, boosting results.

UPS Underperforms on Price Front

Shares of UPS have declined marginally year to date ("YTD"), similar to the Zacks Transportation-Air Freight and Cargo industry. Shares of rival FedEx FDX have seen a single-digit (% -wise) rise in the same timeframe.

YTD Price Comparison

On the basis of the forward 12-month Price/Sales (P/S), UPS' shares are trading at a discount compared with the industry average. FedEx is cheaper. UPS and FedEx each currently have a Value Score of B.

Investment Thesis for UPS Stock

UPS is looking to grow its per-package revenues by gaining more business in segments like healthcare. A few years back, UPS acquired Bomi Group, an industry-leading multinational healthcare logistics provider. Last year, UPS acquired Andlauer Healthcare Group as part of its commitment to offer global specialty capabilities.

Because of this strategic shift, UPS did not increase its quarterly dividend this year, keeping it at $6.56 annually. In the event of the company failing to put an end to its struggles through the strategic shift, the high payout ratio may lead to a dividend cut, which would be disastrous for dividend investors.

End Note

It is worth noting that the company has the brand and the network to continue generating steady cash flows in the long run. This makes UPS a compelling long-term player in the transportation space. However, the near-term headwinds, including the macro uncertainties and volume declines, are hard to ignore.

So, all in all, it is worth holding on to UPS stock for now. Betting on the stock ahead of its upcoming results does not seem like a good idea. It is better to wait for management's commentary on volumes and cost-cutting efforts, apart from the updated 2026 guidance, to get more clarity on near-term prospects.

news.Title: Can Netlist's New LIGHTNING ULL DDR5 Boost Its AI Market Reach?
news.Content:
Netlist Inc . NLST recently announced next-generation LIGHTNING Ultra-Low Latency ("ULL") DDR5 RDIMMs for Agentic AI workstations and servers. The DDR5-6000 and DDR5-6400 products are designed to boost responsiveness in memory-sensitive AI and enterprise workloads.

The latest modules feature a JEDEC-compatible "drop-in architecture" supporting qualified deployments on AMD and Intel server platforms.

Netlist highlighted that internal testing demonstrated up to 10% lower loaded memory latency compared with conventional DDR5 RDIMMs, potentially improving performance in latency-sensitive applications.

The new products target agentic AI workstations and servers, multi-agent systems, retrieval-augmented generation, large language models and vector databases. Applications also extend to high-frequency trading, scientific computing and electronic design automation, cloud infrastructure and data analytics.

Netlist remains focused on portfolio expansion to boost its presence in the AI memory market. On the last earnings call, management highlighted that its Lightning portfolio of overclocked, low-latency DDR5 RDIMM and UDIMM products has been gaining traction. Meanwhile, NLST's CXL NVvault solution is sampling with system-on-chip vendors, hyperscalers and key OEMs for next-generation hardware platforms. Netlist is also upbeat about MRDIMM and high-performance server memory architecture aimed at overcoming the bandwidth limitations of DDR5 RDIMMs. Management, citing industry analysts, noted that MRDIMM could be a $100 billion market by 2030.

Meanwhile, agreements with Micron MU and Samsung also strengthen its IP monetization strategy. The five-year licensing arrangement with Micron provides for $600 million in payments, beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The LIGHTNING expansion could strengthen Netlist's position in AI infrastructure space, although wider adoption and meaningful revenue contributions remain key to its long-term growth prospects amid increasing competition in the semiconductor space.

Competitive Landscape

Netlist operates in a highly competitive memory market alongside established players, including Micron, Samsung Electronics, SK hynix SKHY and Rambus RMBS. While Netlist has recently strengthened its ties with Micron and Samsung through licensing agreements, competition in advanced AI memory technologies remains intense. Rambus represents another notable competitive force, offering DDR5 RDIMM and MRDIMM interface chipsets for data-center applications.

Last month, Micron demonstrated a 512GB DDR5 RDIMM capable of speeds up to 9,200 MT/s.

Story Continues

A few days back, Rambus unveiled a Power Management IC ("PMIC") solution. PMIC is designed to facilitate low-power, high-performance LPDDR6 Small Outline Compression Attached Memory Modules (SOCAMM2). Earlier in the year, Rambus expanded its DDR5 portfolio with complete DDR5-9600 chipsets for both client and server memory modules.

South Korea-based SK hynix has a strong presence across DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory ("HBM") markets. Recently, SK hynix showcased its next-generation AI memory portfolio, including 256GB DDR5 3DS RDIMM and 128GB DDR5 MRDIMM and 192GB SOCAMM2, at the OCP Global Summit 2026.The company also unveiled the second-generation 256GB CMM-DDR5 solution, offering approximately 30% better energy efficiency and more than twice the bandwidth than its predecessor.

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, ASML and BWX Technologies
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 15, 2026– Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM, ASML Holding ASML and BWX Technologies BWXT.

3 Stocks Set to Benefit from Long-Term AI Tailwinds

The AI revolution continues to fuel strong demand across the semiconductor industry, with companies that manufacture advanced chips and the equipment needed to produce them seeing significant benefits. The massive buildout of AI infrastructure has also created opportunities beyond the semiconductor space, particularly within the energy sector.

For those seeking exposure to the favorable AI-related tailwinds, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing , ASML Holding and BWX Technologies fit the criteria. All three recently posted strong quarterly results, with growth forecasts also remaining strong.

Taiwan Semiconductor Sees Huge Growth (Again)

Taiwan Semiconductor has undoubtedly been among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, with its advanced manufacturing capabilities critical for producing the powerful chips that AI applications demand.

The company's latest quarterly results reflected continued momentum, with revenue climbing 41% YoY to $46.7 billion. Earnings similarly soared 58% from the same period last year, with demand for advanced chips remaining red-hot.

Importantly, its advanced 2nm, 3nm, and 5nm technologies accounted for 69% of total wafer revenue, reflecting the continued shift toward leading-edge manufacturing.

Both the earnings and sales outlook remain bright as well, with management forecasting Q4 revenue between $52.3 billion and $54.3 billion and the stock currently sporting a favorable Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

BWXT Benefits from Nuclear Demand

BWX Technologies is similarly positioned to benefit from the AI revolution, though in a much different way. Its nuclear-related offerings are increasingly attractive as the massive buildout of AI data centers drives electricity demand higher.

The company recently delivered a solid quarterly release, posting $901.6 million in revenue and adjusted EPS of $1.07, reflecting YoY growth rates of 18% and 5%, respectively. Its backlog also climbed 40% YoY to $8.4 billion, providing solid visibility for the periods to come.

While government contracts and broader nuclear demand remain the primary drivers of its current results, the AI-related electricity boom adds another favorable longer-term catalyst. The strong performance also led management to raise its FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.70-$4.8, with annual EPS revisions remaining on a bullish trajectory over the past year.

Story Continues

The AI-related nuclear opportunity remains promising, but much of the potential upside is longer-term, contrasting the more immediate benefits semiconductor companies have been experiencing, helping explain the weakness in shares we've seen throughout 2026.

ASML Sees Strong Demand

ASML Holding is another major beneficiary of the AI revolution, providing critical lithography equipment used to manufacture advanced semiconductors. The company's offerings have become increasingly important as chipmakers expand capacity to meet robust AI-related demand.

Its latest quarterly release was solid again, with revenue climbing 52% YoY to $13.4 billion alongside 132% YoY growth in adjusted EPS. The favorable backdrop led the company to raise its FY26 revenue guidance, with EPS revisions also remaining on an upward trajectory across the board.

The longer-term outlook remains bright as AI infrastructure investments continue to drive demand for increasingly advanced chips, with ASML's lithography technology playing a critical role in their production.

Bottom Line

The AI revolution continues to create opportunities, with the companies listed above each positioned to continue benefiting.

TSM and ASML remain the most direct beneficiaries from a near-term standpoint, while BWXT's outlook is considerably more long-term focused as the energy industry evolves to meet the soaring demands of power stemming from the boom.

news.Title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Microsoft, Palantir Technologies, Micron Technology, Lam Research and IonQ
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 21, 2026 – Zacks.com announces the list of stocks featured in the Analyst Blog. Every day the Zacks Equity Research analysts discuss the latest news and events impacting stocks and the financial markets. Stocks recently featured in the blog include: Microsoft MSFT, Palantir Technologies PLTR, Micron Technology MU, Lam Research LRCX and IonQ IONQ

Here are highlights from Tuesday's Analyst Blog:

AI, Semiconductors & Quantum Computing: What Lies in Store for 2027?

Artificial intelligence (AI) has dominated technology investment in 2026, driving heavy spending on data centers, advanced chips and computing infrastructure. Semiconductor demand has benefited from this expansion, particularly in high-bandwidth memory and advanced manufacturing. Quantum computing, meanwhile, remains an emerging investment opportunity, with companies working to turn research breakthroughs and commercial partnerships into viable businesses.

In 2027, investors are expected to focus more on companies that can convert rising demand for AI, semiconductor and quantum technologies into actual revenue and earnings growth.

The scale of investment is substantial. Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending of $2.67 trillion in 2026, up 49.5% year over year, in its September report. Its August forecast put global semiconductor revenues at $1.56 trillion in 2026 and $1.94 trillion in 2027. These projections clearly show the economic importance of AI infrastructure. However, they also raise questions about capital efficiency, supply constraints and the sustainability of demand.

Macroeconomic conditions will influence this investment cycle. On Oct. 13, the International Monetary Fund projected global economic growth of 3.1% in 2026, identifying AI investment as a source of support while warning of risks from geopolitical conflict, higher energy prices and rising bond yields. Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve raised its federal funds target range to 3.75%-4% in September, citing elevated inflation. Higher financing costs can weigh on capital-intensive projects and valuations, making investment returns particularly important in 2027.

AI: Monetization Becomes the Key Test

Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending to reach $3.64 trillion in 2027, with AI infrastructure accounting for approximately $1.98 trillion. AI services and software are also projected to expand, reflecting growing efforts to integrate AI into business applications. Gartner has noted that enterprises are increasingly emphasizing cost control, usage tracking and measurable outcomes.

Story Continues

The key question is whether AI-driven revenue growth and productivity gains can justify the substantial investment in computing infrastructure. In 2027, enterprise adoption, inference demand and the deployment of AI agents are expected to be important indicators to watch. Microsoft , through its Azure cloud and AI offerings and Palantir Technologies , through its enterprise AI platform, are two companies investors can monitor for evidence of AI monetization, customer adoption and operating efficiency.

Semiconductors: Memory and Manufacturing Take Center Stage

Gartner projects semiconductor revenues to approach $1.94 trillion in 2027, including $1.08 trillion from memory. This forecast highlights the importance of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), DRAM and NAND alongside AI processors. SEMI separately expects global 300mm fab equipment spending to rise 14% to $151 billion in 2027, supported by advanced-node and memory investment.

These projections create opportunities across foundries, chip-design companies and equipment suppliers. Micron Technology , a major memory-chip manufacturer and Lam Research , a supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, offer exposure to two important parts of this investment cycle.

Quantum Computing: Commercial Progress Remains Uneven

Gartner projects global quantum-computing revenues to reach $1.1 billion in 2027, compared with $869.9 million in 2026. It expects public-sector spending to lead industry demand, reaching $245 million in 2027. These figures suggest a developing market rather than widespread commercial adoption.

Investors can monitor IonQ , which develops trapped-ion quantum computing systems and D-Wave Quantum, which focuses on quantum annealing and related computing solutions.

news.Title: CIEN Wins Space Norway Cable Deal: Can Subsea Networking Drive Growth?
news.Content:
Ciena Corporation CIEN is strengthening its position in the global subsea networking market after securing a turnkey contract from Space Norway to modernize existing subsea cable systems in Svalbard and deploy advanced networking technology for the upcoming Arctic Way system. The project highlights the growing importance of resilient, high-capacity communications infrastructure in remote regions where connectivity is essential for scientific research, government operations and national security.

The agreement combines upgrades to legacy infrastructure with the deployment of a new subsea network expected to enter service in 2028. By supplying optical networking equipment, advanced transponders and network management software, Ciena aims to improve capacity, reliability and operational efficiency across Space Norway's Arctic communications footprint. For Ciena, this approach creates an opportunity to supply technology across multiple routes and potentially support future network extensions.

A key aspect of the deal is Ciena's combination of optical transmission hardware and network management software. The technology is designed to improve network capacity, simplify operations and support reliable data transmission across demanding subsea routes. Ciena 6500 Optical Platform provides optical transport capabilities for high-capacity networks. In the Arctic project, it will support communications across the new and upgraded subsea systems. Its Navigator Network Control Suite also provides visibility and control, helping Space Norway manage operations across its infrastructure while supporting operational redundancy.

The Space Norway agreement fuels Ciena's already strong business momentum, driven by increasing demand for high-speed connectivity and AI infrastructure. Ciena reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $1.67 billion, representing 37% year-over-year growth. It also raised its fiscal 2026 revenue outlook to $6.42 billion (+/-$50 million). For fiscal 2027, management expects at least 30% revenue growth.

CIEN's Optical Growth Faces Competitive Challenges

CIEN continues to strengthen its position in the optical networking market as rising demand for high-capacity connectivity drives investments in digital infrastructure. Recently, Openreach deployed Ciena's Waveserver platform with WaveLogic 6 1.6Tb/s technology to expand its OSEA portfolio, offering high-capacity connectivity across U.K. cable landing stations, data centers and core network nodes. The solution combines 400G and 800G traffic over 1.6Tb/s wavelengths, supporting up to 32 400G services in a compact 2RU chassis.

Story Continues

However, Ciena operates in a competitive optical networking market. Winning contracts does not automatically guarantee attractive margins, especially when turnkey delivery involves substantial execution responsibilities. It faces competition from other optical networking vendors like Corning Incorporated GLW, Cisco Systems CSCO and Nokia NOK.

Assessing CIEN's Market Peers

Cisco's vertically integrated networking stack is expanding across scale-out and scale-across AI architectures. In the fiscal fourth quarter, it won three new hyperscaler designs – a P200 scale-across system, a G200 scale-out system and an optical line system. Fiscal 2026 hyperscaler AI orders were about 60% Silicon One-based systems and 40% optics, while Acacia generated more than $1 billion in orders in the fiscal fourth quarter. Management has line of sight to multiple additional design wins over the next six months across G300, G200 and P200 systems and optics. In September, management said Cisco supplies chips and full systems to hyperscalers and plans to become independent of merchant silicon providers by fiscal 2029, giving it greater control over product design and supply.

However, the outlook still depends on converting G300, G200, P200 and optics opportunities, and becoming independent of merchant silicon providers by fiscal 2029.

Corning has entered the second half of 2026 with its growth outlook tied to AI infrastructure and optical connectivity. It launched Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 and continues to see opportunities in advanced optics products tied to AI-driven data center build-outs and semiconductor manufacturing demand. Corning is also expanding its GenAI optical portfolio with multicore fiber and high-density connectivity solutions that improve network capacity and reduce installation complexity. Secular demand for bandwidth, cloud computing and AI infrastructure continues to support Corning's Optical Communications business.

GLW also announced a long-term partnership with NVIDIA to expand U.S.-based optical connectivity manufacturing capacity by 10 times and increase domestic fiber production capacity by more than 50%. In September, Corning secured a multiyear, multibillion-dollar agreement with Verizon to supply more than 80 million miles of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions through 2032, strengthening its long-term revenue visibility and positioning it to benefit from expanding broadband and AI infrastructure demand.

Nokia continues to benefit from its broad portfolio spanning mobile networks, optical transport, IP routing, fixed broadband, software and services. This integrated offering enables the company to address evolving customer requirements across telecommunications operators, enterprises and hyperscale cloud providers. Network Infrastructure delivered double-digit growth in second-quarter 2026, supported by continued momentum in Optical Networks and IP Networks. The planned divestiture of the Fixed Wireless Access CPE business simplifies the portfolio and allows greater investment in higher-growth opportunities such as AI networking and optical technologies.

While AI and cloud demand is supporting Optical Networks and IP Networks, carrier spending remains mixed across regions and business lines. Management continues to expect stronger performance in the second half of 2026, but quarterly demand patterns remain influenced by customer capital expenditure timing and software revenue recognition. Management noted that supply constraints continue to affect portions of the optical networking market, contributing to long-term customer ordering patterns.

news.Title: AEIS Rides on Strong Semiconductor Growth: Can It Beat KLAC and MKSI?
news.Content:
Advanced Energy AEIS benefits from strong demand for semiconductor equipment, driven by increasing investments in advanced logic and memory manufacturing. The company's growing adoption of precision power solutions and expanding product portfolio strengthen its competitive position against KLA KLAC and MKS MKSI, which are also benefiting from semiconductor industry growth.

The company reported record semiconductor revenues of $278 million in the second quarter of 2026, increasing 33% year over year and 27% sequentially. Growth was driven by robust demand for leading-edge memory and logic technologies, alongside rising etch and deposition intensity. Management expects semiconductor revenues to increase nearly 50% year over year in the second half of 2026, reflecting sustained customer demand.

AEIS is strengthening its market position through innovative plasma power technologies, including its eVerest and eVoS platforms. These solutions deliver improved yield and throughput for advanced semiconductor manufacturing processes. The company is also gaining traction in system power applications, securing design wins in semiconductor testing, atomic layer deposition and thermal sensing. New product ramps and additional design wins are expected to accelerate revenue growth in 2027 and beyond.

The company's expanding manufacturing footprint is another growth catalyst. AEIS expects to begin generating revenue from its new Thailand facility in the fourth quarter of 2026. Once fully developed, its global manufacturing network is expected to support approximately $5 billion in annual revenue-generating capacity, providing flexibility to address rising semiconductor and data center demand.

AEIS's strong semiconductor revenue growth, expanding product portfolio and improving manufacturing capabilities are expected to boost top-line growth and position it favorably against KLAC and MKSI. For the third quarter of 2026, Advanced Energy expects revenues of $640 million, plus or minus $20 million.

AEIS Faces Stiff Competition

The company is facing stiff competition from companies like KLA and MKS. Both KLA and MKSI are expanding their footprint in the semiconductor market.

KLA is benefiting from strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in AI infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory and advanced packaging. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, revenues reached a record $3.66 billion, increasing 15% year over year and 7% sequentially. Management attributed the performance to rising AI infrastructure investments and greater process-control intensity across memory and advanced packaging.

MKS is benefiting from rising AI-related investment across semiconductor and advanced packaging markets, with demand broadening through memory, logic, advanced PCBs, photonics, and chemistry equipment. Second-quarter 2026 semiconductor revenues rose 28% year over year to $554 million, with broad-based growth across deposition and etch applications. Management expects third-quarter 2026 semiconductor revenues of $630 million (+/- $15 million), implying more than 50% year-over-year growth, supported by a healthy backlog, NAND upgrades, advanced logic and DRAM demand and design wins in dissolved gas and RF power.

Story Continues

AEIS Share Price Performance, Valuation and Estimates

Advanced Energy shares have surged 14.4% in the year-to-date period, underperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's rise of 17% and the Zacks Semiconductor Equipment - Wafer Fabrication industry's surge of 52.5%.

news.Title: If I Could Only Buy 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Semiconductor Stock to Buy Before 2027, It Would Be This One
news.Content:
Last week was the worst stretch for chip stocks in over a year. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index dropped more than 11%, a hot inflation print raised the cost of funding every data center on the drawing board, and the impact of worries about CoreWeave 's (NASDAQ: CRWV) debt load spread to every company selling into AI infrastructure.

Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) sank by nearly 17% in five days. And yet, if your goal is to own one AI chip stock heading into 2027, that decline is the reason why you should look into picking up shares of Marvell now rather than later. Even as investors were selling, the company spent the week revealing its most specific, product-level work of the year, and almost nobody noticed because they were watching the tape.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

What Marvell announced while its stock was falling

Marvell is not a GPU company. It designs chips that sit around GPUs: the custom accelerators that hyperscalers and AI labs are building for their specific workloads, the optical and copper links that connect thousands of processors into clusters, and the memory controllers that keep those chips fed with data. That is the business the company put on display at the Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose from Oct. 12 to Oct. 15.

Two announcements from the event stood out to me. On Oct. 12, Marvell unveiled the second generation of its Structera X memory expanders -- chips built to attack what the company calls the "memory wall" in AI inference. The problem is simple: As models get bigger and context windows get longer, GPUs run out of memory before they run out of math. Structera X lets a server bolt on up to 6 terabytes of standard DDR5 memory, share it across four hosts, and compress it on the fly, which the company says cuts time to first token by 40% to 50%. The first generation Structera X is already shipping to hyperscalers, and a Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) hardware engineering director was quoted in the company's release. Test models of the second generation will be available in Q1 2027.

Then, on Oct. 13, Marvell followed by unveiling two 3-nanometer connectivity chips, a 3.2-terabit retimer and a new active electrical cable chip that doubles copper reach to more than six meters between AI servers and switches. Both support UALink, the open standard that non-Nvidia accelerators use to talk to each other. Early samples of both are already available for potential customers.

Story Continues

That sounds like a lot of jargon, so here is the plain version. An AI processor's usefulness will always be limited by the memory it can reach and the capacity of the connections that link it to neighboring chips. The new products Marvell announced last week address both of those bottlenecks: one lets a server strap on far more memory than the GPU came with, so it can handle bigger models without choking, and the other helps racks of accelerators talk to each other over longer, cheaper copper cables without the signal falling apart. These are tools crucial for AI infrastructure, and Marvell is selling them.

Some numbers to consider

On Oct. 6 -- a week before the AI sector rout -- Marvell held its first investor day in years, and management used the event to publicize a target worth reading twice: It's aiming for revenue in the range of $70 billion to $90 billion by its fiscal 2031, up from $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026, with implied non-GAAP earnings above $30 per share . The engine driving it toward those targets is what management calls "XPU attach," the networking, memory, and security chips that get pulled along with every custom accelerator a cloud provider designs.

Big targets deserve some skepticism, and this one assumes 55% to 60% annualized growth for five years. But even if it achieves growth at half that rate, the stock near $228 is cheap against what the company expects to earn. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) saw enough to buy $2 billion of Marvell preferred stock in March, and Nvidia does not make such investments casually.

Other things to consider: Marvell trades at a high trailing earnings ratio; custom chip revenue is lumpy and tied to a few customers; and if hyperscalers pull back due to higher borrowing costs, Marvell will feel the pain before Nvidia does. But last week's sell-off was driven by financing fears, not by any customers walking away, and Marvell kept shipping through it. For anyone able to buy this stock and hold onto it through 2027 or longer, the 17% discount the market just gave it makes it look like a steal.

news.Title: Not Micron. Not Sandisk. This Storage Stock Is Riding the Same AI Infrastructure Wave.
news.Content:
When it comes to artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure stocks, Micron Technology and Sandisk have been getting plenty of attention this year. Both are benefiting from the massive demand for memory and storage driven by the global expansion of AI data centers.

While Micron manufactures memory chips and Sandisk specializes in flash storage, Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC) makes the high-capacity hard disk drives (HDDs) that cloud computing companies use to store enormous amounts of information.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

It's a different part of the AI infrastructure business but one that's becoming increasingly important as companies build more powerful AI systems. And that's why I think Western Digital deserves a closer look. The stock is up more than 100% so far this year, with plenty more room to run.

AI needs more than powerful processors

Companies like Nvidia , Broadcom , and Advanced Micro Devices get a lot of attention surrounding AI infrastructure because they make powerful processors essential to allowing AI models to process information quickly.

But what happens to all that information after it's processed?

AI companies need somewhere to store training data sets, model outputs, historical records, and the enormous amounts of new information their systems generate. And keeping everything on expensive, high-performance flash storage isn't necessarily practical.

Western Digital's HDDs are important because traditional hard drives -- while slower than solid-state drives (SSDs) -- can store large amounts of information at a lower cost.

A Western Digital customer survey released in May found that 87% of respondents prioritized expanding storage capacity and reducing total ownership costs. Among respondents who knew their storage mix, 70% reported that hard drives accounted for more than half of their storage capacity.

That helps explain why HDDs aren't becoming obsolete as AI expands. They're serving a different purpose.

Western Digital is expanding its storage capabilities

Western Digital is also developing new technology to make its drives more attractive to cloud computing companies.

In February, the company announced a roadmap that includes hard drives capable of storing more than 100 terabytes of information. It also introduced a 40-terabyte drive that's undergoing customer qualification. (A terabyte is about 1,000 gigabytes.)

Story Continues

Demand for additional storage doesn't appear to be slowing. A September IDC study sponsored by Western Digital found that 61% of surveyed organizations experienced at least 25% data growth over the previous year due to AI. Nearly three-quarters expected similar growth over the next three years.

Western Digital stock at a glance

Shares of Western Digital are up 105% so far this year -- not as much as Sandisk and Micron but still much better than the broader index.

Revenue for the company's fiscal fourth quarter (ending July 3) was $3.75 billion, up 44% from a year ago and 12% from Q3. The company continued to improve its margins, which increased from 41% to 54.1% over the last year, and generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) net income was $3.19 billion, a whopping 1,215% increase from a year ago. Notably, much of that increase was attributable to Western Digital's interest in Sandisk, which the company spun off in 2025. Western Digital recorded a $2.05 billion gain from Sandisk. Adjusted net income, which is more representative of the company's hard-drive business, was $1.38 billion, up 130% from a year ago.

For the full fiscal year, Western Digital had revenue of $12.92 billion, up 36% from fiscal 2025, and adjusted earnings of $3.88 billion, up 120% from the previous year.

Why I like Western Digital right now

I love AI infrastructure stocks because you can invest in the industry's expansion without having to predict which AI platform will eventually dominate the market.

Whether companies are training new AI models, operating cloud computing platforms, or deploying AI applications for their customers, they're generating information that needs to be stored. And Western Digital is building the high-capacity drives that can handle much of that demand at a relatively low cost.

I don't see the demand for data storage from AI disappearing anytime soon. Micron and Sandisk have demonstrated just how attractive the memory and storage markets can be for investors. Western Digital is participating in that same infrastructure expansion even if its products don't get the same attention.

For investors seeking another way to participate in the growth of AI infrastructure, I think Western Digital makes a compelling case.

news.Title: Chip stocks shrug off a scary morning, but history says the shakeout isn't over
news.Content:
Wall Street's AI darlings were in free fall at the open. By midmorning, they were leading the comeback.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) sank to its lowest level since early August early Tuesday. It was supposed to be the moment Monday's relief rally fell apart after an eight-session losing streak.

Instead, buyers stormed in. The index is now higher on the day and back above Friday's close, springing a bear trap much like the one forming in CoreWeave ( CRWV ).

The rebound is broad too. Roughly 3 of every 4 stocks in a 60-stock Yahoo Finance chip basket have turned green, including heavyweights AMD ( AMD ), Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ), Intel ( INTC ), and Micron ( MU ). GlobalFoundries ( GFS ) tops the list.

Notice who's missing from the party. Chip equipment makers Lam Research ( LRCX ), KLA ( KLAC ), and Applied Materials ( AMAT ) are still in the red, along with Arm ( ARM ). Even Nvidia ( NVDA ), the AI trade's bellwether, is barely keeping up.

Buyers are picking their spots, favoring the companies that make chips over the ones that sell them the tools.

History says the real test may still be ahead

The track record says don't count on the bottom being in just yet.

After every losing streak of seven sessions or more since 1994, the index traded below the streak's final close within a month, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. After the longest streaks, it was lower a month later most of the time.

And those dips weren't shallow. The typical one after the longest streaks ran about 9%. Tuesday's barely scratched 1% before buyers pounced.

One-day comebacks like this one haven't settled the question either. They've been a coin flip for chips.

The bulls do get a consolation prize. Three months out, the index was usually higher.

BofA Global Research called last week's rout a "positioning-driven hiccup on the fringes of the AI trade" in a research report. If that's right, the bounce has room to run. If not, the next dip is the one to watch.

For the index, it starts with the summer floor around 11,000 to 11,140, built from lows in late July and September, plus Friday's close. Holding it keeps Tuesday's comeback intact.

Lose it, and the next stop is the 10,450 to 10,500 zone, where chips bottomed in late July and traded in late April.

On the upside, bulls first need to clear 12,600 to 12,700, which capped the index in early October. Above that sits the early-October peak zone near 13,200 to 13,350.

Watch whether Tuesday's low holds and that big 11,000 level just underneath. That's where the silicon meets the road.

Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Lam Research (LRCX), which belongs to the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, could be a great candidate to consider.

This semiconductor equipment maker has an established record of topping earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The company boasts an average surprise for the past two quarters of 7.89%.

For the most recent quarter, Lam Research was expected to post earnings of $1.69 per share, but it reported $1.82 per share instead, representing a surprise of 7.69%. For the previous quarter, the consensus estimate was $1.36 per share, while it actually produced $1.47 per share, a surprise of 8.09%.

Price and EPS Surprise

Thanks in part to this history, there has been a favorable change in earnings estimates for Lam Research lately. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the stock is positive, which is a great indicator of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Lam Research has an Earnings ESP of +2.25% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on October 21, 2026.

Investors should note, however, that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss, but a negative value does reduce the predictive power of this metric.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Story Continues

Because of this, it's really important to check a company's Earnings ESP ahead of its quarterly release to increase the odds of success. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

news.Title: 3 AI Stocks to Buy Amid This Deep Correction
news.Content:
The past few weeks have been tough for many artificial intelligence (AI) investors. A hot inflation report, AI financing concerns, and Chinese memory chips are some of the headwinds that have stalled the rally.

However, a few bad weeks don't justify exiting positions. In fact, these are the exact times when contrarian investors load up on positions and get greedy when others are fearful.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

These three AI stocks below have endured steep price cuts even though their fundamentals continue to improve.

1. Sandisk

This memory chipmaker is down by roughly 30% in less than one month, showing that the AI correction is even hitting big-name companies. Perhaps the narrative will shift when Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) reports earnings on Oct. 29, but there is already plenty to like about the stock.

Sandisk produces NAND flash memory products that are critical as AI models, agents, and inference require vast amounts of memory capacity. Without sufficient memory, these products stop working or experience significant drops in quality.

People have become accustomed to AI models like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok handling their questions and providing actionable information in ways that a basic search can't. All of the data centers powering AI tools need NAND flash products, like the ones Sandisk offers.

While Sandisk isn't the only NAND flash memory provider, it's certainly the industry leader. That explains why Sandisk more than quadrupled its revenue year over year and authorized an additional $14 billion for stock buybacks. The dip comes at a good time for Sandisk's buyback program and for investors focused more on where the company is heading in five years than on what has happened to its stock price over the past month.

2. Nebius

High-volatility growth stocks usually get hit the hardest during these types of corrections, so it's no surprise that Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) has taken a beating over the past month. It has dropped by more than 30% in approximately two weeks despite parabolic demand for AI compute.

Nebius' Q2 shareholder letter explained that the company can sell out all of its 2027 capacity right now but is intentionally waiting it out because megawatt values keep climbing. Long-term contracts are now yielding $20 million to $25 million per megawatt each year, but Nebius is also signing short-term deals in the $40 million to $50 million per megawatt range.

Story Continues

The neocloud provider is also getting its customers to foot most of the bill for data center construction. Approximately 70% of deals come with prepayments, and those funds cover 50% to 60% of associated capital expenditures. Nebius can fill in the gap with GPU financing, bonds, and using its completed data centers as collateral.

Nebius and other neoclouds have slumped more than most AI stocks, as CoreWeave 's bond yields have reached 15%. However, this is a CoreWeave problem that is being misinterpreted as a neocloud problem. That should become clearer when Nebius reports earnings in November.

3. Comfort Systems USA

Comfort Systems USA (NYSE: FIX) hasn't been as bruised as the other two stocks on this list, but it's still down by more than 20% in less than two weeks. The company specializes in HVAC, electrical, and plumbing for large facilities. That puts it nicely at the intersection of the AI boom, which contributed to the company's 51% year-over-year revenue growth in the second quarter.

The company's Q2 revenue reached $3.27 billion compared with a backlog of $14.06 billion. As more data centers are built, revenue should continue to increase. Those same data centers will also need regular maintenance, which opens up long-term revenue streams for the company.

Comfort Systems USA uses an acquisition strategy to gain market share rapidly and make it more difficult for competitors to catch up. It consists of more than 50 companies spread across 184 locations in the United States. That growth also comes with solid finances. Comfort Systems USA managed to boost its dividend by 12.5% this year thanks to surging profits.

news.Title: Will Higher Ad Revenues Aid Meta Platforms Stock in Q3 Earnings?
news.Content:

In the second quarter of 2026, Meta Platforms reported $59.4 billion in ad revenues, up 27% year over year, with a 14% increase in ad impressions and a 12% rise in average price per ad.

news.Title: Can GFS' Manufacturing Expansion Boost Its Future Growth Prospects?
news.Content:
GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc . GFS has been selected to operate two new semiconductor manufacturing facilities at its Malta, New York, campus under a U.S.-Japan investment initiative worth up to $21 billion. The expansion will increase the company's U.S. production capacity and support demand for chips used in automotive, industrial, communications and data center applications.

Under the project, GlobalFoundries will use Japan's initial investment of around $10 billion to build a new semiconductor manufacturing plant, which is expected to begin operations in 2029. An additional investment of approximately $10 billion could fund a second facility. Each plant is expected to add around 900,000 300mm wafers of annual production capacity. The project is expected to create approximately 27,000 construction and related jobs, along with more than 1,000 skilled manufacturing positions.

Separately, the company will reallocate $955 million from its existing U.S. government award to invest in silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and advanced packaging at its New York and Vermont facilities. These technologies are expected to support growing demand for artificial intelligence (AI), cloud data centers and high-speed communications.

The investment could strengthen GlobalFoundries' position in the U.S. semiconductor market, support key customers such as Renesas, Apple, Cirrus Logic and General Motors, and enhance its role in the global semiconductor supply chain.

GlobalFoundries' Peers

United Microelectronics Corporation UMC provides semiconductor foundry services for chips used in communications, automotive, consumer electronics and industrial applications. The company specializes in mature and specialty process technologies, including solutions for display drivers, power management and connectivity. UMC focuses on manufacturing reliability, process efficiency and long-term customer relationships to support demand for chips across a wide range of electronic devices.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited TSM manufactures advanced semiconductors for leading global technology companies, supporting applications such as AI, high-performance computing and mobile devices. Its advanced process technologies help produce powerful, energy-efficient chips for smartphones, AI accelerators and high-performance computing systems. TSMC provides advanced packaging technologies that help improve chip performance and meet the growing computing demands of next-generation applications.

Marvell Technology, Inc. MRVL develops semiconductor solutions for data infrastructure, including AI systems, cloud computing and data centers. Its portfolio includes networking chips, optical connectivity solutions and custom silicon designed to support high-speed data transfer and efficient computing. As AI workloads increase the need for faster connectivity and greater data processing capacity, Marvell is focusing on technologies that help cloud providers and enterprise customers build scalable, high-performance infrastructure.

Story Continues

news.Title: Amkor's AI Packaging Growth Accelerates: Can the Momentum Last?
news.Content:
Amkor Technology AMKR is benefiting from accelerating AI and data center investments, driving demand for its advanced semiconductor packaging and test solutions. Computing revenues reached a quarterly record in the second quarter of 2026, increasing 20% sequentially and 23% year over year. Management projected nearly 30% sequential Computing revenue growth in the third quarter, supported by AI infrastructure demand and its high-density fan-out (HDFO) data center CPU ramp.

The opportunity extends beyond one program. Amkor has active engagements across 2.5D integration, HDFO and emerging co-packaged optics technologies. Management highlighted 11 customers across 2.5D programs and five HDFO customers with 10 active engagements, targeting four product launches in each category during 2026. Its 10-year advanced packaging agreement with TSMC and multi-year NVIDIA partnership strengthen technology collaboration and long-term growth opportunities.

Improving manufacturing efficiency provides another advantage. Gross margin expanded to 16.8% from 12% a year earlier, supported by higher factory utilization. Meanwhile, manufacturing expansions in Arizona and Korea should strengthen its ability to support future AI and high-performance computing demand.

However, substantial capital requirements, semiconductor cyclicality and manufacturing execution risks remain challenges. Amkor expects 2026 capital expenditures of $2.5 billion to $3 billion, while underutilized Arizona capacity could pressure margins during its initial ramp.

Accelerating AI demand, expanding customer programs and strategic partnerships position Amkor to sustain advanced packaging growth, but successful capacity ramps and consistent utilization will be essential to sustaining momentum.

How Are AMKR's Advanced Packaging Rivals Positioned?

Intel Corporation INTC competes in advanced AI packaging through its Foundry business, offering EMIB silicon bridges, Foveros 3D stacking and EMIB-T technology. Intel operates advanced packaging facilities in New Mexico, supporting high-density chiplet integration for demanding data center workloads. By combining semiconductor fabrication with advanced assembly and testing capabilities, Intel offers an integrated manufacturing alternative that could challenge Amkor's position in complex AI packaging.

GlobalFoundries GFS is expanding its presence in the advanced packaging ecosystem through silicon interposer manufacturing. In October 2026, GlobalFoundries announced a five-year, $2 billion agreement with TSMC to manufacture silicon interposers for its CoWoS advanced packaging ecosystem. With production expected to ramp in the first half of 2028, GlobalFoundries could strengthen competition for advanced packaging opportunities, although its interposer manufacturing role differs from Amkor's assembly-and-test services.

Story Continues

news.Title: NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
news.Content:
NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on October 27, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $4.14 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +33.1%.

Revenues are expected to be $3.77 billion, up 18.8% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 0.47% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for NXP?

For NXP, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.27%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that NXP will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that NXP would post earnings of $3.54 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.61, delivering a surprise of +1.98%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates three times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

NXP doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.
